title: Tyson Bagent, Jordan van den Berg look ahead to preseason opener | Press Conference
text: We've seen you with jump in with the first team. What What has that meant to get that opportunity? >> It's meant the world to me. You know, I'm thankful opportunities. It's uh being able to go out there and prove it to myself and to my coaches is just an honor. So, I'm really thankful there. >> What's the self assessment of this camp today for yourself? >> Definitely. No, I'm still learning the technique, trying to work on fundamentals. You know, that's always something I'm going to take pride in doing, but you know, I'm just trying to tag every day like it's my last day, so I'm just all out. Jordan, what did you think of Jeremy said that you have a mean streak? Uh, is that where's that come from? >> A mean streak. >> Yes. >> I don't know. I just like to play with violence. You know, this is a place where you're able to play for violence and get praised for it. So, I really enjoy that aspect of the game. I >> think it was Neville last week that mentioned that coming to this organization was the best thing that could have happened for you. Um, you you kind of drawn a lot of that praise from some of your veteran teammates. What has the experience of kind of learning this team and this culture been like for you? I mean, it's been awesome. We got some really great veterans in the room, you know, Neville Street, uh, Grady Jarrett. So, just being able to be around them and absorb as much as I can has been such an honor. You know, they got so much wisdom and they like an extra coach in the room. So, just being able to come into an organization where they are older players that I can just lean on and learn the game from has helped me tremendously. Jeremy said uh to us earlier today how they're trying to work with you playing a little bit more control because the energy you bring, the violence you play with, it's almost like they got to pull you back a little bit. Is that is that hard for you to do? >> Uh yes, sir. Definitely. I'd say in college I was just trying to explode out as violent as possible, but you know, I got to sometimes slow it down a little bit to let my technique and fundamentals catch up. And then like I feel like now like with my fundamentals and technique just catching up, I'm able to go more fast and more violent every day. What do you think your feelings are going to be for that first snap in preseason? >> I can't wait. I can't wait to prove myself. >> How do you describe how great is a a resource for a rookie and particularly for you? >> Definitely. So, coming out of um Georgia Tech, we had coach Jay Simpson. He was the defensive line coach at the Falcons. So, we watched tape on Grady every single day. So, just being able to watch that in college and then come here and actually see it in person has been such a huge honor. So, it's been I'm just trying to learn and absorb as much as I can. >> Have you talked to him about the stuff you watched in college at all? >> Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Definitely. >> Jordan, what was your reaction when you were featured in that power slam AI video by by Ben? >> I don't know. I just laughed. I don't know what to think of it. >> It seems like every practice ends with a touchdown to Katie Davis. >> Just two D2 cats being guys. I guess he's he's done an exceptional job uh being a new guy coming in uh very cerebral picking up the offense very well and he's very fast. So both those two things have helped him a lot. >> How much more advanced do you feel even in the offense now in year two under? >> Uh I I feel great. This is this is the first time I've been able to run the same offense for um multiple years in a row. So, uh, I think that, you know, just watching practice, you can really see that just overall with the whole offense. We're able to peel back more layers than we were able to last camp. So, I think just all you can compare it to is where we were at this point last year. And I think we're in a really good spot because of that. >> What do you make of the opportunity to I think Ben said this morning, you're going to play about a half on Saturday. What do you make of that opportunity? >> Uh, the opportunity is everything. Every rep that I can get out there is an absolute dream come true to me. Um, so I'm extremely excited and uh am looking forward to, you know, putting out good tape out there and, you know, doing whatever we need to do to be successful. >> Where do you think you strides from this point last year? >> Yeah, I think from, you know, once you get a a certain number of years in this thing, I think it's all just the the the leaps that you make are all mental. Um, I think just being having a deeper understanding for the game of football itself. Um, not really penciling myself into just looking at one section of the field, being able to see the full picture. Um, and I think that's really just a credit to, uh, the guys that that we have around us. Uh, the coaching staff, they do a great job making us feel prepared and and knowing when it's time to really, you know, teach the next steps. Uh, which I think they've done a good job in the spring and then obviously into training camp. >> Tyson, ball location has been such an emphasis in the conversation with Caleb, but I imagine it's been applied to all four of you guys in that room. Can you just kind of give us a glimpse on on what that looks like, the way the coaches are hammering at home and getting you guys in that mindset? >> Yeah, I think it's every play. uh even you know the you know quote unquote breather plays which would be like a screen for us uh they're still harping on ball needs to be on the front peck everybody's got a landmark we know where they're going to be uh but they you know they are not shying away from that coaching point at all um every time that you don't hit them in the front peck on a screen or whether that be a runner's ball uh with people running side to side uh really just harping on you know giving guys a chance to catch the ball and tuck it as fast as they can and be able to use their weapon so that we can get as much uh yak after the catch as possible. Um, and I think that, you know, with with that intense coaching point, um, and them holding us to that standard, you can see that, uh, you know, it just all it does is make everybody better. So, >> how much has the speed jumped out to you just of the receivers at camp? >> Yeah, I think that we get a we get a top 10 chart for miles per hour after every practice, you know, whoever is in the top 10 on that miles per hour. And it used to be there'd be a couple guys hitting 20. Uh now it's almost like all 10 are you know in the 20 miles per hour plus. So testament to the the guys that they brought in. They brought in a lot of speed, drafted a lot of speed. Um so it's been fun and you know just puts more of a you know stressor on us to hit these guys in stride and let them do what they do after the catch. >> How do you view the preseason games as opposed to practices test? >> Yeah, I think it's all a test. I think that's spring and camp. Uh I I encapsulate the preseason into as as camp that is included for me. Um it's all a test, you know, trying to take advantage of every single rep. Um cuz you you never know when when uh you know, you could make or not make the team. Uh I mean, we saw that last year with Jade A uh being able to, you know, do his thing on the last drive of the last game. Uh which is really we'd like to think about that as like the last day of camp. So, uh, really want to make the most everybody, uh, with making the most out of these reps cuz you, you know, all you are is your tape. So, you want to put a good resume out there and, you know, play good ball no matter what the situation is. >> So, what's the biggest change in the quarterback room? >> The biggest change in the quarterback room, I would just say, you know, this is also the a year where I've been able to have the same guys in the room for a consecutive year. Also, I think Miller Moss has been a great addition. He fits in well, gels well, gels well with all the guys in there. Uh JT, you know, we talk about players getting better year to year. I think JT as a position coach has has we've seen a lot of strides. Uh you know, the quarterbacks personally have seen him make a lot of strides as a coach. Uh the overall comfortability. Uh nobody feels stupid asking a question because we're all, you know, very tight in there and understand that everybody's just trying to make the most of all their opportunities. Um but really just the camaraderie in there. Obviously, you have, you know, the greatest teammate I've ever had in my career so far, Case Keenum, in there. Uh being able to give insight to so many different things. Um, and I think, you know, me and Caleb able just continue able to grow our relationship. This is year three together. So, I think just naturally you start to become more and more, you know, boys as as the years come on. So, I think it's just the the comfortability and then also just uh the mindset that's in there, which is just, you know, being on the attack, you know, trying to do the best that we could do and making the most out of every play. >> What makes that kind of teammate? What what makes him the great teammate that he is? That's high praise there, obviously. man. Uh I would, you know, you could talk about the football aspect of it. Obviously, we've said it many times before. He's been in every um every position that has to do with the the quarterback position in the NFL. He's been in that position. He's been he's been a franchise guy. He's been on the practice squad. He's been a backup. He's done all these amazing things. Um but I think you take the football aspect out of it. Uh the insight he's able to give just as um you know, a human being, just the good dude that he is. Uh, I think at least for me, I can only speak for myself, has allowed me to also become even a better player and even a better teammate than I, you know, I could have imagined. So, um, that's really just a hats off to just who he is and how he was raised. When >> getting his reps, what are you looking for from him and what have you observed of his camp so far? >> Um, you know, I, you know, I I tend to maybe look at Caleb once we get in the film room. Um, but when we're out there on the field, I'm kind of looking at what the defense is is showing. Just trying to take my eyes away from the football, see the bigger picture, like I hinted at, uh, before, uh, which is a skill in itself. Everybody wants to watch the ball, see where he throws it, see, you know, what his feet look like, the, you know, how he escapes the pocket, whatever. I'm just trying to see bigger picture down the field, and kind of just trying to answer the tests in my own head for, you know, what I maybe would have done based on the look or based on the coverage we got. Um, and then obviously coming in the film room, that's where you can kind of, you know, obviously you can rewind a bunch. So, uh, then you can kind of rewind, see what see what his feet looked like, what he was thinking, and, uh, you know, how he handled the what whatever the given play was. >> Listen, we we've seen, um, Kaden Davis make a bunch of plays in camp. What can you tell us about him? >> Um, you know, he's obviously he's he came from the UFFL. Uh, had a good UFFL season this past spring. Um, he's b he's been in the league. He's been in Ben's offense before. um track guy, very fast. Um D2 guy, so a lot of lot of grit there. Um and really just like I said, picking up the offense very well, doesn't ask a lot of questions. Is that where he's supposed to be when he's supposed to be there? So, you know, you you mesh those things together and it usually ends pretty well, which is why we've seen him have success so far. >> You were that guy when you were here as a rookie. I know he's been in the league a little bit. There were people that know who you were and then everybody kind of found out quickly. Is it fun for you to see guys like that? Like you mentioned Jay last year to see some of these guys allowed training camp and then preseason to pop. >> Yeah, I you know it's it's it's one of the most amazing things ever being able to see a guy put in the work, put in the time. Uh you know, especially somebody like Kayen who obviously you know without even spending too much time with him, you understand how much he cares about the game um and how much he cares about, you know, doing his job on the given play. So being able to see guys like that that work really hard have success. Uh I think that's what you know that's what we that's why we love the game and that's why you know coaches love the game too. Being able to see a guy that's not high on the depth chart right now. Being able to see him implement the coaching points that they give you know day in and day out you know it really feels good for everybody all around. >> Mentioned Jade a couple times. Just where is he at now compared to maybe this time last year? How's it going most of those opportunities so far? Yeah, I think the biggest jump that you see with players in NFL is from year one to year two just with overall just comfortability on what the heck is going on. Um, you know, especially when you can add that you're in the same offense, you know, from year one to year two as well. I think we be a we've been able to see him uh run routes um a lot faster. You know, he's not thinking, he's playing uh he's and he's a guy I think that you can plug in a in a couple different positions uh that's able to do, you know, a couple different things. you know, his size, strength, and obviously he could take the top off as well. So, um, being able to see that jump, being able to him run fast without thinking, uh, which is something that you see a lot of with, you know, rookie wide receivers. So, I think it he has a chance to have as big of a year as he wants to. So, I think he's done great so far. >> Couple more. >> You've had a good connection with Cole at at various points at camp so far. Obviously, he's one of the few guys that predates you here in this locker room. How do you describe what Cole's worth is to this team? Yeah, I think it's uh um you know, I talked a lot about Case Keenum. Uh Kamett is very close to also being one of the greatest most professional. I mean, you guys see it when he come up when he comes up here in the podium. Have you guys ever seen somebody more professional than Cole KT after I saw him on the podium? Yeah, he said a lot of nice things about me, but I don't usually watch these. I don't usually watch these. And my dad sent it to me. I'm like, "All right, whatever. I'll watch it." and just listening to him answer questions, it's like he gives the greatest answer you could ever imagine on every single question. So you you translate that translate that to everything else that he does day week in and week out, preeason, off seasonason, during the season, he's always doing what he's supposed to be. Uh you talk about a guy that leads by example, nobody leads by example more than KT. Um, and I think that the impact that he has on the guys around him and especially you can you can really zoom into that tight end room, what a great veteran to have, you know, in your room for a guy like Coloulston, for a guy like Sam, you know, all those tight ends that are coming up in that room. Um, yeah, the his, you know, he means he means the world to this team, I think, and I think that everybody that you ask would say the same thing. >> You've you've uh you talked about Moss' addition to the locker room. What advice would you give him trying to make the most of his rep that he does get in practice right now? >> Uh advice that I would give to Miller is uh just to continue doing exactly what he's been doing. Um you know, if there was something that was glaring that, you know, I thought he should be doing that he wasn't doing uh that would be something where, you know, you could have a conversation with him about that. But as far as I'm concerned, uh, postpractice walkthroughs, post walkthrough walkthroughs, um, anything that any any type of rep that he can even remotely get his hands on, he he's taking advantage of. And, uh, you know, for a guy that has been in that situation, that's really all you can do is, you know, take those mental reps and, you know, try to translate it for when they do throw you in the fire here in this preseason. So, I thought that he's handled himself extremely well. Um and I think that because of that he will have a lot of success uh this preseason. >> You mentioned a lot of the you know consistency and that how that's helping to have the same coaching staff running the same offense in this second year. Um how is that helping in the camaraderie off the field for the team compared to years prior knowing you guys saw some success. How does it feel? Um yeah. >> Yeah. I mean, it it feels good and I think that uh because we're in the same offense for another year. Obviously, you're still you're still honing in on the details, you know, you're still always rewinding back to the fundamentals of the game, but as far as learning a new language, you know, that's not happening right now. So, I think that instead of having to absolutely just plug your head into the playbook as soon as you leave here until you go to sleep, guys can relax a little bit, joke around with each other. you know, we can go out to O line dinner and I'm not thinking about these weird third down calls or um you know, anything of that nature. So, I think that just overall guys are more comfortable walking around with a lot more confidence, knowing where they're supposed to go and where they're supposed to be. Um, which I, you know, I think it's a good question because you do see a little bit more camaraderie than than years past I

title: Kevin Warren, George H. McCaskey on state of the Bears | Press Conference
text: Uh good afternoon. It really is good to see everyone here uh today. Thanks for taking the time to come out uh to Halis Hall. Uh what uh my goal is today is to spend some brief opening remarks uh just from a football operations standpoint, business operations standpoint, and then obviously uh stadium update. So, thanks for taking the time. First and foremost, I just want to thank our operations staff here at Halis Hall for uh helping us to get organized for training camp. Uh training camp sets the tone for the season and they've done an outstanding job of making sure that this is a great place for us to spend time during training camp. Also want to take a moment to acknowledge the individuals in uh Chicago and Chicagoland area and also in northwest Indiana and in Hammond who have been impacted by these horrible storms. this week. Uh there are a lot of families and individuals uh who are struggling right now. So we want to let them know that our thoughts and prayers are with them right now. And just want to thank the fans. We have absolutely the best fans in all of sports. The best, the best, the best. We love our fans. And then I just want to take a moment is just to say uh how grateful I am to work with the Macy family, especially uh George Macsky um for providing us with the resources, the infrastructure here to build a worldclass franchise. So George, thank you. And Pat, thank you and your entire family for doing that. From a football operations standpoint, Coach Johnson and Ryan Poles uh have built a really unique uh relationship. Uh they work well together. Uh they have a great partnership. They respect each other. They've hired great staff members. Uh their staff members have worked well together. And uh it is just outstanding to see a general manager and a head coach in the National Football League who are young, who are vibrant, uh who are aggressive, and [snorts] uh who've built an incredible relationship together. And uh we have assembled a team that's going to be fast, uh aggressive, hardworking, competitive, and just relentless. And so we want to thank Ryan and coach uh for for building this roster. Uh we can win this year. we can win for many years to come. Uh we can win big. And our focus here is to make sure that we create a football operations department uh that has that sustainable success across the NFL. And uh and we're in good hands with uh Coach Johnson and Ryan Ples. And Darnell Wright is a prime example of that. A young player who was drafted here into the system uh who's evolved, who's grown. He turned 25 years old earlier this week and and it shows the the vision and the foresight for us to be able to sign him to an extension not have a protracted hold out and those are things that we want to do and that's where uh we appreciate the Macy family also for [snorts] providing us the resources and the infrastructure to be able to do that. From a business operation standpoint, uh we're really building a unique partnership between our business side and our football side, which really can create uh that longevity of sustainability across the National Football League. We're excited that uh we've expanded our partnership portfolio uh during the last few months. I mean we have Granger who's our media backdrop partner um EA Sports Culligan Water Advocate Healthcare Curic Dr. Pepper USA Shell and Lexus to name a few. These are the type of partners that we want to build long-term relationships with and we're grateful for their relationship. We've had record revenue at the Chicago Bears this last year. Uh our season ticket holder renewal rate was at 99%. We have low suite inventory and you'll see when you go to Soldier Field this weekend that we have some new inventory on the south line of Soldier Field of some RVs uh where fans will be able to rent those on game day. And regarding the stadium development project, as you know, on June 5th of 2026, we as a Chicago Bears board voted to focus our attention on advancing our stadium project in Hammond, Indiana. We've done that. We've been working diligently to complete all of the topographical studies, the geographical studies, environmental studies, u in addition to assembling the land that's needed uh to build a worldclass uh stadium project and also mixuse develop and also working on the financing and the capital stack that's required to bring this project to life. the uh representatives from the state of Indiana all the way from the governor's office to representatives in northwest Indiana have been phenomenal partners. They've been stellar to work with, very professional, diligent with a can do attitude. To be clear, the due diligence at the Lost Mar site that we've talked to you about before is completed and the due diligence is ongoing at the Wolf Lake terminal site. That's the new site that uh we've been able to find. While we were working on the Lost Mar site, uh we discovered a potentially new site that could even be as good or better uh than the Lost Mar site. So, we're in the middle of that due diligence. It's a lot of work uh that happens on a daily basis. We are in regular almost daily communication uh with the state of Indiana working on this. We have an excellent deal, a win-win partnership together. And uh because of the significance of this decision from a stadium standpoint, we will make sure that we take our time to get this right because not only are we building a world-class stadium, but we're building a world-class mixeduse development, and we want to make sure that we get this right. Um, we we have uh had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois and uh and uh also we're just grateful that uh the NFL has been very helpful to us, especially Commissioner Goodell. But even though we've had occasional meetings with the state of Illinois, our sole focus at this point in time is working on a worldclass stadium and mixeduse development in Hammond, Indiana. I'll pause there and take any questions. Just to clarify on the the two sites you just mentioned in Indies, >> the due diligence you did on Lost Marsh. >> Yes. >> Did that come back as a viable site. So it's not a pivot to the other site. It's just looking at an additional one or would they be together used? >> Yes. I'm glad that you asked that question. It's a great question. Yes, it's not a pivot for anything. Uh that's that's an issue with the loss shite. That is a viable site. We could build there. It works. Uh but as we studied that site and we are working very hard to make sure that we build holistic environment in Hammond is that when we looked at the lost marsh site and then were able to discover the opportunity at the Wolf Lake terminal site we thought if we could cohesively bring those together uh and just make sure that entire area comes together from a mixeduse standpoint it would even be better. So, Los Mark Shite works. I'm glad you asked that question, but that's where it's uh has come from. >> Kevin JB Prrisker said today that that he's had discussions or the state's had discussions about what you guys might want, but there's been nothing in writing. Do you plan on putting something in writing soon? And and second, I mean, can you rule out the state of Illinois at this point? >> I mean, I guess Governor Pritker is correct. There is nothing in writing. we don't have an offer uh from the state of Illinois and our focus now is on on Indiana and obviously like I said there have been occasional meetings that have taken place and um but right now our focus is on on Hammond Indiana to make sure that we bring that to life. >> You expect a decision about which state you're going to put the stadium in? Well, I mean, this this has to we're at the point right now uh that because we do have one viable site uh in Hammond, Indiana, and we expect here um to have another viable site and maybe to be able to merge those sites together um and then we'll continually proceed forward. So, it's it's reached that point now where we we are starting to get some clarity and the moment that we finish our due diligence and have the appropriate capital stack and financing together, we are are looking forward to making a decision so we can break ground and get our project going forward. >> Um, >> you know, my expectations especially on these development projects, uh, I've been there before. Uh, they take time and so I'm not I'm not at all, you know, disappointed in it. They take time. I think the biggest thing for our fans, we have to get this right. I mean, this is a 40 to 50 year decision and um and we have to pull all these things together. So, I'm just I'm I'm looking forward to to bringing it to close uh from a legislative standpoint so we can get on to the construction. >> What mistakes do you guys think you've made along the way and maybe not understanding maybe the political process or getting stuff wrong with the state of [snorts] Illinois? You >> know, thanks for that question. I don't think we've made any mistakes as you study these projects. I really look at these as learning opportunities to come together. They are complex. I mean, the Chicago Bears, we haven't had our own stadium in 107 years of Chicago Bears football. You look what's going on around the league from Kansas City to Cleveland to Washington to various locations. These projects are complicated. They're expensive. Uh they're challenging. They require political um willpower. They're financially um you got to lean into that from that standpoint. So I don't look at we've we've made any mistakes. Uh we've made the necessary steps at that appropriate time to be where we are today and and it's good to be in a position that we'll be able to bring this to some closure. >> Since the board vote in June, how do you characterize the meetings with Illinois lawmakers and what those have been about? I mean, they they've been um minimal. Um so I wouldn't have any characterization as far as how we would characterize those. >> What is your sense for why the Arlington Heights project hit a dead end in Springfield? >> Well, I mean, I don't know why it hit a dead end in Springfield, but we've been very clear for the last couple years, the things that we've always needed uh is property tax certainty. We need infrastructure uh certainty. Um that's what we've needed. So, that has not changed. there's some other things associated with it. So, I don't know why Springfield um as far as what you said is why it hit a snag, but um you know, one of the good things about what we've had is since we did have the board decision, we have really focused on Indiana. That's where our time and energy and effort has been spent and we've had extremely productive meetings there and feel really good what's going on uh with the state of Indiana, specifically in Hammond, Indiana. Kevin, since your focus has been on Indiana the last few months, would you say there has been meetings with Illinois? Are you still representing the Bears in those meetings with Illinois? >> Um, yes. I mean, when when not all of them, I mean, that's why we've had to be able to break uh up and and do different things. So, we're always there. I mean, from in one way or another, but I have not been in in all of the meetings with the state of Illinois. President said this morning that he's committed to getting a deal done in Illinois, whether it's in Chicago or in Arlington Heights. Does that mean Chicago is back on the table? >> I can. You'd have to ask him that. I I can't answer that uh question. Uh our focus again at this point in time is in Hammond, Indiana, and we're doing everything that we possibly can. We don't have any legislation in Illinois. We don't have a deal with Illinois, and so it wouldn't be fair for me to answer a hypothetical question like that. Are you comfortable waiting until the veto session to potentially explore some action in Illinois? I >> I think it's prudent for us to move with pace based upon where we are. Uh these costs have gone up. We've talked about it before at, you know, almost $150 million a year. We just looked at the financial numbers last week and you compare to where it was last year. These are real issues. You notice the market is very uncertain and uh so it's not only the political and the legislative decisions that we have to make, it's the financial decisions that we have to make. And we have a family uh who's committed uh sizable resources, $2 billion out of their personal uh money out of the organization to build this stadium. And so that's why it's really important from a time standpoint where we're reaching that point where we have to make a determination and decision. The longer this goes goes on, it creates complications just from a building operation design standpoint. >> You mentioned the learning opportunities. [clears throat] >> What did you learn navigating >> Uh I I think in not only Springfield but just generally speaking, you have to learn how to you have to have options. Um, you have to uh be organized to be diligent. Uh, you have to be patient. And the the worst thing you can do in these stadium projects is to make a determination that you look back and say, "Boy, if we had taken a little more time or worked on this or explored that because there's not really a doover once you break ground." And so I think the learnings is that these projects are complex. That's why teams do it every 30 to 40 to 50 years. is not something you do on a regular basis. So, I think it's been incredibly powerful learnings and we're skilled. Uh we're in a position to make really good decisions and uh we'll continually focus and go forward. >> Last two, Chris and Jason. Kevin, there's a lot of fans who are really disappointed about the idea of this team moving to Indiana. What's your message to them as to why you see this as a viable option? >> I mean, I agree. Uh, I mean, I understand uh how a fan could be upset, but but I think what's important to recognize this is important for the fans is for us to build a world-class stadium. It's it's time the time has come for us to do it. They deserve a much better game day experience than we have now. um they deserve the opportunity for us to be able to bring world-class events here from the Super Bowl that we'd have a chance to bid for to World Cup to concerts to college football playoff games to other professional sports. And so our focus is on the fans and it's important that we build a world-class stadium that has a mixeduse development with restaurants and hotels to have that special game day experience with with with smooth ingress and egress. And so the focus every single day, every meeting we're in, we're focusing on the importance of building this relationship with the fans, but I can understand frustration and hopefully when we finish the stadium and open up and they get a chance to experience that they'll be grateful for what we have done. >> Kevin, what's your what's your target right now for breaking ground and opening your stadium? >> My wife told me about 6 months ago, don't give any more target date. So just get the work done. Oh, Greta, I love you and I'm listening to you and uh so I think the target is is the right time. We'll know when it is, but I will say we're making very very good progress here. And uh we have one site that works, Lost Marsh, and then to have another site uh is really unique and and we think if that comes together um that we will have an absolutely dynamic atmosphere in in Hammond, Indiana, not only from a stadium, from a mixeduse development, from a game day stadium, um development overall. And so I'm just I'm looking forward to this opportunity. I'm grateful uh to have been able to kind of work on this and uh and and it'll be exciting day when it comes to uh fruition, but but time is now and it's time to bring this to a close and and uh I'm grateful of where we are and I think everyone will be pleased one once we make a final decision and two once we break ground and three once we open up and to be able to enjoy it. The Chicago Bears fans uh deserve a new new environment. Uh, I want to start by echoing Kevin's comments that our hearts go out to all these people that have been impacted by these devastating storms um, south of Chicago and in northwest Indiana thousands of people without power and enduring some real hardship and uh, we're thinking about them and wishing the best for them. Um, Kevin also mentioned the fans and I want to thank and salute our fans. They've been uh a tremendous presence at training camp practices. A lot of enthusiasm, a lot of energy, a lot of excitement, a lot of anticipation. We're very grateful for their dedication and their loyalty. Um it's very difficult as we did today to have to again close practice because of these uh weather conditions. I feel terrible for all the people that were looking forward to this experience and won't be able to have that experience. So, uh, we wish him the best and we thank them. And also want to thank our staff that work so hard to make these people feel welcome at the Halis Hall campus and in particular Megan Clancy, Emily Rooney, Lee Twarling, and Michelle Burke Mckowsky and their staffs for going out of their way in some hot and humid conditions that you've experienced yourself to make our fans feel at home here at Helis Hall. very grateful for that. Also want to thank uh Kevin for all of his efforts. Um I've heard many times that the Bears hired Kevin to build a stadium and that's not accurate. We hired him for so many other reasons. his vision, his leadership, his consensus building, his um ability to make difficult decisions in difficult times, his ability to see around corners, and all of the other many traits that he brings to this position, and he's done an outstanding job for us. The fact that he has previous stadium experience was viewed by us as a plus. Kevin has reminded me more than once that it took the Vikings 11 years to get a stadium done in Minnesota. And I've reminded Kevin just as often, we don't have that kind of time. And since Kevin has exhaustively answered again all of your stadium questions, be happy to entertain any non-stadium questions that you have. And Cheryl, somebody's reminded me more than once that you have more seniority than hub. So why don't you start us off if you have a question? >> George, when you look at this plan for the stadium, is there any concerns about Chicago not being part? They will be Chicago Bears. They be the Hammond Bears. >> No, we will be the Chicago Bears whether we're in Arlington or whether we're in Hammond. And as Kevin said, our focus is on Hammond. That's where we're advancing our efforts and that's where the bulk of our uh time, attention, and resources are being devoted. >> You've owned that [clears throat] since it was first approached in the letter in December. The idea of moving to Northwest Indiana has been a source of anxiety and stress to at least Bears fans that I know. Do you understand their point of view there that even though Indiana is close to downtown, it means something significant to them to leave the state? >> Yeah, we feel that anxiety. Um, we feel that stress. We talked about this in March. It's going to require an adjustment. Uh, but when I've driven that route, other than a sign telling me so, I wouldn't know that I've just crossed the state border. And as Kevin said, once people see the building, once they get in there, once they understand that our top priority from day one was a worldclass stadium experience, we think we'll make that adjustment. We think Bears fans are up for that. >> George, what Kevin mentioned, the the league and all this, the NFL, and you're obviously in close communication with the league all the time, your family. What feedback have you heard from Roger Goodell or the league on the idea of the Bears moving to Indiana and are they fully on board with it? Well, we had two uh reports to our stadium committee of which I happen to be a member. Um and they've identified um two viable sites, Arlington and Hammond. Um we've spoken to the commissioner often. He visited the Lost Marsh site himself. Um, we think that ultimately they will become comfortable. Uh, this has happened with other teams in other markets. Most recently, Kansas City Chiefs. Um, tremendous legacy at Arrowhead Stadium. They won a lot of games there, a lot of exciting moments, and this is a move across the state line which I'm sure the Hunt family and Clark Hunt are confident Chiefs fans will be able to make the adjustment. Uh, we see many parallels there. I'm curious how you uh feel about the idea of bare weather going away if if you indeed get a enclosed stadium completed. >> Uh yeah. Well, I heard a lot about bare weather um back in January. You know, this team from Southern California is going to come in here and we're going to expose them to bare weather and um they wound up with the W. So, um it's fun to think about snow flurries and u braving uh the elements. I was out there myself. Um, but to host the number of events that we could host in a fixed roof stadium to be able to attract these major events which all along Chicagoland has lost out on. We think that will more than offset um the advantages of bare weather. >> What about the What about the two sites >> being in southwest Indiana? How soon might you all pivot and start to reimagine what you're going to do with the land out in Arlington? >> Um, we haven't really gotten that far. Um, like we said, our our focus is so much on Hammond that um um what to do with the Arlington Park property. That that'll take care of itself in time. >> George, how would you describe the discussions with Illinois legislators since the the board voted for Indiana and Jim? um minimal. >> We haven't actually heard from you since that those events played out at the end of May down in Springfield. What transpired? What can you share about whether it was disappointment from not getting the legislation you need through those days until the board actually voted to fully pivot towards Indiana? Like what were those discussions like internally to get everybody fully on board? Well, we were waiting to see whether there would be some uh substantive action taken. Um, we thought we had presented a pretty compelling case that a stadium in Arlington uh would be beneficial not only for the village of Arlington Heights um but for the community and for the entire state really. Um tremendous driver of economic activity, job creation, tax revenue, sales revenue. Um ultimately um that argument was unsuccessful. >> What is your understanding of the tax dynamics in the state of Indiana for those residents that would have to crystallize for this project to become a go for you guys across the border? >> So there's enabling state legislation and that includes some uh local taxes in um I believe Lake County and Porter County. >> You expect that revenue to be to be generated fully to to get your project off the ground? >> Yes, >> George. I know the focus is Indiana, but are you hopeful that Illinois comes up with some sort of plan for you guys, whether it's in October or the summer and Arlington does become the focus again? Are you hopeful that it that Arlington is the property where you guys build? >> Uh, well, somebody mentioned the commissioner, he has um said to us many times in league meetings, hope is not a strategy. We have to deal with the here and now. We have to deal with real circumstances, and these are the real circumstances. Are you second guessing some of your speaking of strategy, are you second guessing some of the strategy of the last few years to gain inroads in Illinois? >> Um, I don't think so. I think you, as Kevin said, you learn from every experience. Um, and as Kevin knows well, and I I've I'm sure you've seen it happen in other markets, these are very challenging issues. um financial, tax, logistical, political, traffic, environmental um and they all come together and in the end um there needs to be a political will to accomplish something. >> You guys have mentioned multiple times the obvious that the costs are rising with every given day. It's been a little unclear though where that extra money will come from. Have you guys discussed that? I guess is the Macy family prepared to eventually have to kick in more money than you guys have already committed? >> Uh well, we said before um excuse me, our part of the financing is is going to be primarily um debt. So, that is a constant concern. Anybody who's ever um built a house, the longer it takes, the more expensive it is. Um construction inflation is a very real concern for us. George, when you think back to four years ago when you spoke at Hershey High School about the Arlington Heights plant and kind of see where you guys are at now with the pivot to Chicago in the middle there and keep kind of putting your focus on a new site. How do you kind of put in perspective where you come from that? Is is it difficult for you to say we are so excited about Arlington Heights and then say we are so excited about museum campus and then say we are so excited about breakfast Indiana. >> Yeah. Uh that seems like a long time ago. I guess it was at least four years. Um, and that's how long we've been working on this project. Um, trying to convince people that this is a a project that could benefit a lot of people. Um, you have to be u malleable, you have to be adjustable, you have to be flexible. >> George, you and Kevin have both used the word minimal when uh talking about how often you've spoken with Illinois legisl legislators. Are you waiting for them to come to you, for lack of a better word? >> Um, I wouldn't say that. I mean, um, we're all adults here. Um, we can have constructive conversations and I don't think it has to be, you know, who calls who first. I mean, let, um, if there are substantive discussions to be had, uh, let's have them. um in Indiana um they've been very proactive, very communicative, very um solutionoriented. >> Last two hub >> George, it's pretty obvious. Um I know it's not up to you between you and and the state of Illinois and the state of Michigan. Bears fans are >> you uh had a Freudian slip there, hub, when you mentioned Michigan. >> Connected Michigan, Indiana. I'm sorry. Um, [clears throat] it's pretty obvious though the majority of Bears fans are not going to be particularly happy if the team leaves and goes to Indiana. >> And this is based on your >> uh stringent surveying question. I'm asking you the question. >> Okay. >> I according to my research, what research have you guys done on how your fans are going to feel about this? [clears throat] Because it seems obvious that there's going to be more negativity than positivity if you leave the state. >> Yeah, I don't I don't mean to make light of it. just um questioning the premise of your question, how you could claim to speak for a majority of Bears fans, but um yeah, we understand that that's out there um and it needs to be dealt with. We are doing uh surveying, research, data collection um to address those issues. And as I said months ago, this is going to require an adjustment. But it required an adjustment when we went from wriggly to soldier. It required an adjustment when we went from um soldier to champagne temporarily and it required an adjustment when we came back to the quote unquote new soldier field. That that's how it works over the course of 100 years plus of franchise stewardship. [snorts] George, just to follow up on your answer to Herb's question about property in Arlington Heights, you guys have not had discussions about contingency plans for a 326 acre $200 million property. if you would. >> Nothing substantive. No, just haven't gotten there yet. >> Thank you. >> All right.

title: Ben Johnson on preparation for Bears' preseason opener vs. Browns | Press Conference
text: All right, game week is here. I know our guys are excited about changing the lens a little bit and and getting to go to Soldier Field on Saturday. Um you know, we made some decisions as a coaching staff. What will end up sitting a number of our our our starters as we view it um on both sides of the ball. You know, I I'm not going to go through player by player right now, but there there'll be a handful of guys that aren't participating in this match up. Um and yet I I think we're going to get some good evals of the guys that are out there and make sure that we have enough to to to go win this game. So, really excited about that. Um I know I alluded to the left tackle position last time I was up here. I'll go ahead and and address that right now. Our plan for that game is we'll we'll start Quran uh first quarter and and we're looking to alternate him and Jedrick uh throughout that game based on the quarter. So, um hopefully get an equal number of snaps right there for those two guys and and we'll continue to reassess where we're at at that position as we go. So, I'll open it up from there. >> And with that, with Quran, what do you want to see Saturday to uh just further the evaluation? >> Yeah, I think we just want to see guys compete. We want to see guys playing fast. Um you know, it's it's all of it. It's run game, it's pass game. I don't think there's anything specific. We want to see consistency, level play, and um see guys go out there and and compete to win the game. >> What has he shown you to this point in camp that's turned your head? >> I I I've seen improvement from from last year. Um and yet there's still glimpses of where we would need the consistency to be a little bit better. And I think we felt that, you know, we talked about Tuesday being a big day for for the team and and what we came away from is, you know, some of these guys they, you know, it got hot and fatigued and legs got tired and and we got to continue to fight through. And so, that's what camp is for and, you know, that was practice 11. We still got call it 3 weeks to go here to to fight through that and and so each opportunity we go out there it's to show that we're making improvements from from the previous exposure. So, um that that's a part of it. I I love where he's at though. He's really he's working hard. He's got a better understanding of the offense, that's clear. And you can tell his confidence level continues to rise each practice he's out there. >> And with Caleb, I assume he's not playing? >> He's not playing. >> So, how will you determine whether between now and the start of the season you need to see some actual game snaps from him or not? >> Uh I don't know that I need to see game snaps. What we're trying to assess is the volume throughout the week and um making sure we're hitting our benchmarks to make sure our team is ready to go for 17-plus game season. That's That's what we're looking to do. And so, each individual is a little bit different, I get it, and yet, you know, we work closely with our sports science department. Uh we get feedback after every practice, where we stand, guys that have high workloads, things of that nature. Um you know, next week we can address when it gets there, but we have a plan in place of the reps, the workload we want to get as a team between the joint practice with Cincinnati Cincinnati and the game reps as well. And so, that all plays a part together, and and everything's really really fluid on how we're how we're handling that. But, um do I need to see Caleb Williams in the pre- No, I don't. I I I see him every single day in practice, and I know what we're going to get come the season. And yet, at the same time, there is a workload and there's a number of reps that we want to hit as a team. And so, um we'll make sure we even that out, whether that's game reps or not. >> Xavier Woods is probably still learning the system and finding his way around the building and all that, but you've had him out there a little bit. What are your early very early observations about what he can provide to the defense? >> Yeah, yeah, he's a pro, and you can see he's got that approach about him. He knows what uh his body needs, he knows um all these schemes that that DA has. Uh I think he does a really he's really taken to the system. He's a You throw him in there with the ones and we're not missing a beat on the back end right now. And so that's encouraging to see. Hopefully we'll see, you know, him feel a little bit more comfortable just in this setting with his teammates and see his personality start to come out a little bit more. I think that's where I don't have a good gauge yet. I'm not spending enough time with him um out there, but I like what I've seen so far and I I like I said, I don't feel like we've missed a beat on defense on the back end. I think the communication's been really clean. >> You talked about creating evidence on Tuesday. What evidence did you find in your run game with all the the especially in the short yardage >> Yeah, no, I I think there was a lot to come out of that practice and I thought there was a healthy amount of back and forth between both sides of the ball and uh you know, I think early on there Here's what I know. I know DeAndre Swift is is he's right where we need him to be right now. I was very pleased with what he looked like, how he approached the day. Um I feel really good about our offensive line and how they're coming off the ball. Specifically, you know, that right side of the line was huge for us a year ago and uh I felt like we're we are we're continuing to pick up where we left off in that regard. So um there's still some things we got to clean up just in terms of the operation. We still had too many false starts. I think we can still do a better job communicating across that unit, but I was really pleased with what Swifty what Monongai looked like. And yet, you know, we might have started hot on offense in short yardage and then you go down to goal line and the defense bows up a little bit, which was great to see. You know, we talk about fighting for every blade of grass and you could really see that come to life down there as well. So like I said, there was a healthy back and forth between the two sides um and some really good things uh that you could see from individuals. >> Is that back and forth Would you say that's how it's been most of camp? That Is Has that been healthy for you guys? And as somebody who comes who's in charge of the offense, how do you uh juggle that on a day-to-day basis? >> Yeah, no, I I think that's that's what you want for your team is you want uh you want each side challenging each other. Uh I think they do that. And uh and yet, you know, you go in with the offense, you go in with the defense, and and both sides are you're kind of pissed off with what it looks like at times, you know? And so, that's I think that's healthy this time of year. Hopefully, that's what these joint practices will be able to tell us is just a little bit where do we stand in relative to the rest of the league. And uh and that's why those joints will be big between Cincy and and Tennessee. And I'm not trying to look too far down the road and and get ahead of what we have this weekend. Um but it's as a as the head coach, you kind of you kind of get like, "Man, are we good you know, how good are we? How good can we be?" It's It's things like that that hopefully we'll get answered over the next few weeks. >> With Luther down, you've had some receivers get some extra opportunities. Who stood out to you? >> Oh, shoot. Um I think that whole room has showcased their speed throughout camp. And I know, you know, Luther's I I'd put him as a speed guy. He He's out. Zayvian's missed some time. And yet, you don't feel like the the speed level of that room's dropped at all. A guy like Cayden Davis has made plays almost every single day. Scotty Miller has made plays. Um those guys uh are really really fast. Gives them an opportunity to get more reps there with the ones and with Caleb. Um so that he can he can get his rapport going there. And And also, what it does, it opens up opportunities for the tight end room to get more involved in the passing game when, you know, Luther or a couple guys in the receiver room go down. >> What's your plan for Tyson on Saturday? >> Tyson will start the game and and uh probably play a half. >> Okay. >> One more, please. >> As you've dealt with some of these injuries, like Luther going down, how do you balance getting guys ready to fill in for those guys that are injured while also maybe not taking a step back in what their original role was playing to be as a third, fourth receiver or guy on teams? >> [clears throat] >> Yeah, I don't think it changes a whole lot. You know, we we end up going out there with the guys that we have and like I said before, it gives some guys maybe maybe they're catching the ball from Caleb as opposed to Tyson, but other than that we're we're still getting some really good high quality reps and uh I I just don't feel like we're really missing a beat from from that whatsoever. So, I think we're in a good spot. >> Coach, with >> Do you feel like you're seeing what you're seeing from him is similar to what you saw from the line and last season where it was just a lot of information and they kind of had to put all the pieces together before it really hit for him? >> Yeah, I think there's an element of that that uh that there is some thinking going on and and so the guys that have been around for a year and a half now certainly I do think the game slowed down and they're not having to process they're able to go out there and fly out of their stance and go and so we're working through that right now and yet you see with Jed you see the talent and uh you know, you can go on to one-on-ones and he does as good as anybody taking a set and punching and and keeping guys away from the quarterback and so um that's the balancing act is how how much does the talent outweigh the fact that may oh shoot, there's a couple things there we had a couple false starts the other day, you know, things that we got to clean up cuz he's he's thinking about it and so um he's he's in a race right now to to get comfortable. >> How hard is that to gauge on Sundays when you're trying to pick who's going to be the starting left tackle and you're like, I want the guy that has the most talent, but also you got to know where you're supposed to be. >> Yeah, I mean I think we got a great group of guys upstairs that that are doing the evaluations and um I think we're going to feel real comfortable about where we're at as a as a unit going into game one. I'm not I'm not too concerned about that right now. >> Coach, with Terrick Stevenson, I know consistency's been the operative word, but what have you made of the ball production over the last two and a half weeks? >> Yeah, no, I think he's he's had some big-time interceptions and which is great to see, you know, we've we've talked a lot about the focus level and just staying engaged and he's taken that to heart and so when you see the ball production start to show up after that, I think it's it's a great thing and and uh you know, I from an offensive perspective, you kind of hate it, but yet from from his side, I mean, it's it's awesome. It's it's awesome. So, um it's good to see that. Thank you.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 12, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: stuff about kind of callousing the mind and body has been something that you've been talking to the players. Can you talk about that and what you think the importance of that is during this time? >> Well, it's callous don't blister is really what it is and and the mindset being there is we're not just going to do work for the sake of work or beat guys up for the sake of beating them up. It's all with a plan in mind of getting ready for a a 17-game season and then more if you earn it. And in order to do to do that, I think you have to be physically ready for that challenge. I think you have to be mentally ready for that challenge. So, we're always going to be about putting together a program in terms of what we do on the practice field, what we do in the weight room to get our guys ready for the season. And I just believe in in making what we do out on the grass as close to football and as close to game like as you can. And in order to do that, you you you're going to have to practice hard. And that's just it comes with the territory of of what we believe in. >> What do you want out of your ones this weekend and why is it important to have a plan? >> Yeah, again just with the same mentality of getting our guys ready to play. We'll play like I mentioned, you know, a series 10 plays in this first game. We'll we'll go to Indianapolis and practice versus the Colts next week. I'll give you my plan our plan for Miami when we get to it, but it's all part of the plan in getting guys ready to play. I don't believe in showing a lot in the preseason and doing all sorts of exotic things and and and whatnot. So, what we'll do is we'll have a very simple game plan on offense, defense, and special teams so that our players can play fast. It's a great opponent that we're going up against which we're excited about. Good players. It's it's finally, you know, it's about time to see a different jersey and a different helmet and those type of things where guys are way past seeing each other right now. So, excited about that opportunity, but bottom line is we're just getting ready for the season. >> Realizing that it's about putting your guys in the back giving them an opportunity, how much prep will you look will you look at Denver? Will you look at some tape on Denver? Just to kind of familiarize with just kind of base what they did. >> We we will and uh it's not a full game plan, it's not >> [snorts] >> what it would be in in a season on a normal Wednesday, but we will watch what they did in their preseason game number one last season just to see different fronts that they're playing and coverages and offensively what type type of attack they're they're going with, but it's a very well coached team. We know they can jump in and out of anything really at any moment, but we want the guys to have enough information going into this game to understand the opponent, but at the same time it's really about us and in order for it to be about us, we have to keep it simple and let those guys just play. >> How do you handle Jack and Rush? Just like reps-wise after, you know, the I guess drive number one, so how do you plan to handle them reps-wise? >> Uh sure. Uh so Cooper will come in after Tua and then Jack will finish the game. >> Yesterday AVP was talking about Mike's under center work. Obviously, it's not foreign to him, but that there's been an emphasis on getting that better for him. What do you think about his development in that area? >> Yeah, very pleased in that area specifically and I think it's a credit to Coach Van Pelt, it's a credit to the players in in in working very hard and and there's a little nuance to to doing that and how you get back from center and and the drops and how they're incorporated when you're under center are a little bit different from the gun and again, we're very blessed to have Coach Van Pelt who's a veteran at that position both as a player and a and a coach and I think he's he's making those guys comfortable just by the amount of work that they put into it. >> How much do you really need to see from Tua and I guess what's kind of the concern level with putting him out there when you have Michael who's not even fully ready to go? >> Yeah, it's it's football, so we're our guys are ready to play uh and looking forward to Tua getting his first action in a game in this system. That's a you know, there's a lot of newness for him as well in terms of uh that type of thing. There's it's first time in the building for him as as a Falcon and uh just understanding uh you know, all the things that go with it. >> Is he calling all plays? >> Yes. >> You mentioned that the practice length. It feels to me like the practices have just generally been shorter during this training camp. I've seen the practices. Is that um are they short to you or is that something that you do by design? >> I'm I'm big on efficiency. Uh I don't want to waste time. So, uh we'll we'll go drill to drill very quickly. We'll we'll you know, a period will be 10 minutes, but if we've gotten the the number of plays that were in that period were and there's 2 minutes left on the clock, we're going to the next one. So, I I just believe in being efficient in what you're doing. We also uh you know, we'll start practice. I know it's not practice per se, but we'll start our walk-throughs and getting some jog-through stuff done before we start the warm-up, if you will. So, there's there's plenty of work that's also being done prior. >> How much more evaluation can you um do in a preseason game compared to training camp? And is there a position maybe that you can evaluate better in a game compared to out here on the field? >> I wouldn't say any one position's better uh to evaluate. I obviously it's full, it's live, it's tackle to the ground, quarterbacks are live, that type of thing. So, that's different than being out here where where we have our rules of how we practice uh when we're on the grass. So, that's very different. So, it's the preseason football will resemble uh the closest to regular season football. Uh obviously schematically it's not exactly the same, but the fundamentals and techniques don't change and I think there's value in in getting game reps uh with your fundamentals and techniques in mind. >> Throwing a lot at Ethan O'Neal on the walk right now. title: Trevin Wallace: 'Competition is always going to happen'
text: Trevan, how do you how would you view your recovery from shoulder surgery this off season? And how do you think you've performed this summer? >> Oh, I think you know it's better. Like it was a different surgery, so you know, more reconstruction in it, but way better. You know, obviously, like I said, it was more I feel like it was a more serious surgery, but this summer I had a great summer. You know what I'm saying? Just getting the shoulder back, getting my range of motion back, you know, just doing the stuff I need to do to just get my strength back in my shoulder. You and Claude are pretty close. You guys have been around each other for three years. What's this competition been like for you? >> Uh, I don't think nothing of it. Like I said, I only control what I can control. And same for him. Like we we knew what was going to happen. We talked about it. He said at the end of the day, bro, it's business. Like it goes on in the world in the real jobs. It's business. So at end is business. >> What What have you learned from Devin these last couple of months? >> A lot. You know, obviously one thing the strength of the ball cuz you know big plays happen when you run to the ball and those who run like you've seen the stats of him one of the leading the linebackers interceptions. He just run run all just trust yourself and just believe and just go. >> What what have you seen from him as the as as the main voice of the defense just calling to relay the plays as somebody who's done that before? Like how difficult is that to do when you first get somewhere but also how does he handle? >> Well, I feel like it was difficult. It's difficult when you first start but when you comfortable with it it's real easy. Different between me and him though, like people still don't understand what I be saying. So like people be looking at me like but with him he pronounced everything right. He's leading. He's very vocal. I you know I like that about him. >> Does that allow you to play a little more free not having that on your shoulders I guess? >> Yeah. Yeah. It it do it do cuz now you don't have nobody like just talking in your ear and all that you know but it do you know. Does that having that dot sort of make you I don't want to say play slower but one more thing to kind of think about pre- snap and all that. >> Yeah. You know obviously you know you have the dot you know you have a coach telling you like hey watch out for this watch out for this or like see this. So you got a lot going on your head. Then when you have dot you got to think your back is against the defense. So when they break you got to turn around just like try to key everything. We we've heard Dave talk about he was just addressing it at the tight end position bringing in competition and you guys are in a competition. Is that being stressed more this summer is do you feel like >> I feel like every year is competition like at end day you know nobody's spot is fulfilled you know like I say like I learned from my coach in college everybody name is written with pencil because you know you can't erase it. So at the end of the day you know competition always no matter what situation new day new year competition always going to happen. That's just part of the business. >> Did you come into training camp knowing that you would be you would be in this in this competition? >> I had like that's that's every year like no matter what situation was. Every year I always thought, hey, it's competition no matter what situation is cuz you got to have a first impression every single day. That's what I think of and I learned it from Shaq and Josie. Every single day is a first impression. Just go in there, put one foot in the other, and just keep going. >> There's pressure though that comes with that. How do you not how do you play freer or you say how do you not think about it when there's there's pressure that comes with competing for a starting goal >> at the end of the day I think of it like this you know put all things in God going to cover me take all the stress away just pray about it just keep going you know you have people in your corner that's taught you and like just see like hey at the end of the day and God control it's not in your hands let them have it just let go let God have it >> is that humbling is the right word is that something you kind of make peace coming into camp like obviously you know you said every day is a competition but kind of realizing >> uh yeah cuz like I said two years come off injury like you have you you sometimes I feel like you have to be like that cuz it's like two years coming off injury it's okay like like I said it's a business side of it you know like I look at it like hey come off injury it's like two years like what what can like how who can Trevon be is he confident in his shoulder and all that so at end day yeah like I said end day every year is a competition Who can Who can Trevvin be? >> Who can Trevon be? >> Shoot. Trevor can be anybody he can be. Only person that can stop Trevor is yourself. You know, at the end of the day, like that's how I look at it. The person that can stop you is the person you look up in the mirror. >> You and JT came in that same draft class and had to deal with injuries in your first two seasons. Have you guys kind of talked or bonded over that similarity? >> Uh yeah. You know, at every like I think what when I got hurt, we just talked about it and like we looked at each other like, "Hey, it's God's plan." And like I seen this thing on social media where was like sometimes you know guys keep you down for a little bit cuz he see like hey you getting too big headed. Sometimes you get need to get knocked back to the bottom and figure out how to get way back to the top. >> Did you get big headed >> me? No I'm just saying though like No, I'm just saying though. But like sometimes like I said God sometimes slow you down to see like what you can see and see how you can view yourself and see what you can do to make yourself mentally stronger and physically stronger. >> Another guy from your draft class uh Brooks has at his own test physically. Um, how do you think he's come through through that? And how how is he looking? >> No, Jonathan looked real good. You know, like I said, cut fluid and he's trusting himself and all that. Like he look he's looking real great. >> Thanks.

title: Michael Hoecht Speaks Ahead Of Preseason Opener | Buffalo Bills
text: you what's your perspective just on the preseason in general? You're like the perfect person to ask this because you were fighting to make a team, then you were more of a special teams contributor, then you kind of elevated your role. How do you just view the preseason? >> Yeah, I mean, it's a great guy for or it's a great time for young guys uh to showcase, you know, their skills. Um, you know, a career is never going to get made or broken during the preseason, but I think what coaches evaluate is like who can do football 101 really, really well and who can uh, you know, not that we really game plan, but like who can watch the Hall of Fame game and like look at a couple of Carolina's runs and just be able to like understand how our defense would go against a different offense. And it's just the most vanilla and basic thing. And uh, it is a lot of fun. like all the guys on the sideline cheering for these young guys, these undrafted guys, late round picks, guys fighting for rosters spots. And you know, the unfortunate reality is uh we have more good players than we do roster spots. Uh so there's always tough decisions that have to happen, but this is like where some of those like really good feelood stories start. Um you know, it's where I got mine. We went to Denver and I had a strip sack uh right before the half and uh they took me out of the game after that and that was kind of like a a like you're going to be on the roster and that was like an awesome moment. So, you know, those are the stories that, you know, if you find those, they're a lot of fun. >> You said you're not game planning, but what can a preseason game do for a defense that's in transition with the scheme? >> Um, yeah, like a lot. I mean, it's our first chance to run it against uh not Joe Brady. Um, so it's fun to just sort of like put that together, put some vanilla stuff out there, but you're also going to see like, you know, who can do different techniques because, you know, all of your techniques are sort of built into different calls. Uh, and then just when we get to the regular season, we just sort of move who's doing what. And so you just kind of want to see all that come together on game day. >> Michael, what's Bradley Chub meant to this defense and more specifically to your defensive end room? >> Yeah, I mean, he's been awesome. He's very charismatic guy, uh, vocal leader, you know, when we're up on the sideline. You know, TB is obviously like the guy that like goes out there and he's like our situational guy, get the defense together, but Bradley's been an awesome addition to that. and you know his I think he he cares a lot about having the standard be what it is. Uh and when we're not practicing to that standard, he's the first guy to be on it and be like defense come together. Like what we're doing right now is not great and let's like correct the ship and fix it. Having the red and blue game, first drive of the red or red and blue scrimmage didn't go how defense wanted. Bradley Chub first guy got the defense together, fixed it. Rest of day one great.

title: Owner & CEO Greg Penner ahead of 2026: 'Our goal is to compete for championships every year'
text: Welcome everybody to new training facility. I actually Carrie and I just had a chance to walk Dick Monfort through it and that was fun for for him to be here, but uh uh we're really pleased to be in here, excited about what we've seen at training camp so far and looking forward to getting on the field for some real football this Friday. So, any questions? >> Greg, because you mentioned it real quick, I know I've talked to you since you purchased your portion of the Rockies, can you start there before we get into all this? Just why that made sense and and what's your vision for >> Yeah, you know, Carrie and I had a chance to get to know the Monforts in the you know, four or five years we've been here and and really came about a series of breakfasts that I you know, I'd have with Dick every you know, probably two or three times a year and I think they were ready to bring on a partner and we've you know, couldn't be more excited about doing something here in the Denver market and and have grown up baseball fans as well and and as you know, it's a terrific fan base ballpark and we're really pleased to join the ownership group there. >> Is there an option to eventually buy a greater percentage of the Rockies at some point in the future? >> You know, right now we're just focused on being supportive minority partners and Monforts are in in full control and and we're going to do what we can to support them. >> Greg, we heard from somebody not too long ago, but what what is sort of the state of play in terms of various processes you're going through on the on the stadium front as you work towards trying to get a package of things in front of city council. >> Yeah, we're we're we're making some progress especially on the things that are are really in our control. So, you all saw the the property that we closed on yesterday which was an important step. Really good progress with our architect and and also the master plan. There's still a lot of work to do and the 2031 timeline is aggressive and and we can't do it by ourselves. >> Denver Water Denver Water in particular, is that I mean lot of them is that for for Denver Water view does does that make sense to put that you know 5 acres or so there in in that spot or what what is the challenge that sort of come up there? >> I mean Denver Water serves a obviously a critical function for the the city and and so it's important that their operations are are seamless and uninterrupted and anytime you're moving operations and moving to several locations, it's it's complex and and so we've got to you know we're doing everything we can to support them so that we can we can make that move help them make that move on a timely basis. >> Great news. >> Stadium built pretty much in the last 25 years has had some version of PSLs outside of maybe the ones that were almost 75 80% funded by taxes. It It just we're so focused on we've got so many steps before that. So really we haven't even gotten to PSLs yet. There's a lot of new projects in the league. I think it's really good for the NFL and and our fans overall. Um, now we're we're always closely watching what, you know, what others are doing, but we're really focused on our project here and and getting that right. >> It was just It was just a couple months ago that the Denver Post, um, made an analogy that the things that needed to get accomplished in the next couple months was akin to like a a Rube Goldberg and Councilwoman Torres, being her district, said the complexity of all this is kind of smacking us in the face. At some point there'll be a, you know, a judgment call, I'm sure, where not everything is done, but but we're not at that point yet. text: Let's not waste any time, Jeff, because you've been all over this. We'll throw the graphic up and let you just take it away in what was perhaps a sigh of relief for a good chunk of this Ravens fan base when you learned the following about Nate Wiggins earlier today. >> Yeah, it feels like they've dodged two bullets now in in about a three practice span. The Zay Flowers one was it didn't look see that serious at the time because it looked simply like a knee to the quad, which is what it turned out to be. You know, it's some of the stretches he was doing off to the side and the fact that he walked back to the to the locker room, which is a pretty long walk when you're on that third field. All those factors suggested it wouldn't be very serious with Zay, and sure enough, he misses one practice. He was back on the field today doing individual stuff, didn't do team stuff. He still was favoring it a little bit, but it's a it's a brew you know, it's a kind of a thigh bruise. So, it'll be a bit, but that one worked out. Now, this one did not look good in any way, shape, or form. Just to to go over the play, they're doing one-on-ones, and this was sort of the featured match-up. Nate Wiggins, the number one corner on this team, against Jacoby Lane, who set everybody talking with his play in in over the summer. And the shame of it for Wiggins was it was a it was a picture tech it was it was a textbook wrap, right? He was stride for stride with Lane down the far end of the field. And he had great position on him. And I don't know if they got their feet tangled or what or Wiggins just took an awkward step, but right away, you saw him writhing in pain on the ground. It was It's not one of those It was one of those things where you knew immediately he was hurt. It's not like he just came up kind of shaking up and then it got progressively worse. And they all kind of went over to him and tapped him on his way out. He looked pretty distraught. And then, you know, I they took the cart all the way to the field house.
