So, um I'm I'm I'm going to be relentless as well to make sure that that that happens. >> How about the fact that you you showed that dog in you, showed that fight, that spark that they were looking for in that push going to edge in the left tackle spot. What did you make of that whole thing? >> Um I just I thought that was awesome. I just I don't know. Every day I'm just trying to come out here and compete. And if that's what they wanted to see, then hell yeah. >> Spencer, I know the the first time we talked to you, we're well aware that going against Jarran would be a good challenge for you, that it would help with your development. Is it still kind of, you know, a part of mental toughness getting ready every day to go out there and, you know, accept, "Hey, I'm going to lose some against this guy, but I have to hold my own too." >> For sure. I mean, every day it's I have to get ready to go against the best player I've ever played against every single day. So, there's definitely a part of that. Just yeah, getting ready for that every day. >> What's that relationship like where we saw him after practice working with you the one day? And then even yesterday, it looked like you guys got into it. But at the end, you know, he kind of gives you a congratulatory congratulatory pat on the helmet. So, how do you kind of go back and forth between the battles on the field and then helping each other? >> I think at the end of the day, like we're both competitors. And so, all we want to do is win. And like we get really upset if we lose. So, I think that's kind of the way both of us are wired and we both understand that. So, it's just at the end of the at the end of a practice like at the end of the day we're still teammates and we're still here to get each other better. And then he's been getting me so much better, so I don't know. Just that whole answer, yeah. Move on. >> His His power is well advertised. That's his game. >> Yes, sir. >> Are there other parts to his game? >> For sure. >> you? >> For sure. I mean, he has a he has an incredible get-off. I mean, that's another thing I've been trying to get used to is just um um when he's able to time up that snap count and I have to get out of my stance faster. Um, things like that. He's good around the edge. He has great inside moves and he's a very very uh hard defender to go against. >> What do you expect from the uh the Bears guy you got to find you against a different team on Saturday. What will that be like? >> Uh, it'll be fun. It'll be fun. I'll I'll tell you that'll be my first uh real I'm not real test, but I don't I don't know. My first real test of uh NFL football. >> And how do you feel about Dawand Jones alternating with you with the first team? What did that kind of How did that sort of help you rise to the occasion? >> I mean, it was awesome. I think Dawand's an incredible player and he's a huge mountain of a man that can make really any block. Um, so, to be able to compete with him um every single day I I do think it really pushed me. >> How have you seen yourself just grow and grow in terms of your game that you can do from you started training camp really when you went back to the spring to now as you as you kind of been anointed that starting spot there? >> Um, I feel like I've improved pretty much everywhere. Just um just listening to the coaching that Coach Warhop gives me and um trying to what what I'm what I need to do is just try to get as close to what he wants every single play. Um, and as I continue continue to do that, I'll just get better. >> You know, our The has been a big buzzword for this camp. >> Is there >> talk a lot about that. >> Mhm. As We you know we see the lineman jump off side or false start sometimes, but there's obviously more to it than you guys just jumping. So, how has that whole process worked with the lineman with the quarter two different quarterbacks? >> Um Uh I think it's been really good and it's been great to go out there and practice it just cuz we have so many different cadences. Um I think a lot of the times um we'll just get hyper focused in on a job and sometimes you can forget about that cadence. So, every day it's about building that that mental strain of remembering everything that you're supposed to do um pre-snap. >> Do you have a sense for how much you're going to play Saturday? >> What was that? >> I have no idea. I have no idea. >> As much as you can you talk about what was it like for you to meet your idol Joe Thomas and then what did you also learn from him in your conversation? >> It was so freaking cool. I mean we had him in there in in the meetings and it's crazy just sitting next to a dude that has really done it all at the highest level. I don't know I don't think there's anyone that's done it at a done it at a higher level than him. Um and for him to give me some of his knowledge um and to help uh teach me while I was out here um was so freaking cool. It was amazing. >> What's what's one tip you picked up from him? >> Um I asked him a lot of the like post practice things that he'd work on. Um so I feel like like kind of his post practice drills was a big thing for me. Um just how I can get better every day. >> What What did you learn at Utah? You played with some mobile quarterbacks who you know move the pocket and maybe you don't always know where they are where they are. What did you learn about protecting you know Devontae for example that can help you with with Shador and DeShawn? >> Uh you just have to strain. Uh the strain is um the probably the biggest That's the name of the game is you have to strain. So, that's what I learned most there. >> What do you When you say strain, what do you mean by that? >> Um you can't just uh be content with like a you know, technically most plays the ball is supposed to be out in like 3 seconds. But, with those guys back there, it could take a six It could take 6 seconds for them to make an incredible play. Um, so you have to strain for those things to be able to happen. >> Good. >> Hey, thanks, Mason. >> Thank you. >> That's it. >> What's up, Shump? >> How you doing? >> you, man? >> Good, good. >> All right. Everybody good? How's everybody doing? >> Pretty good. How are you? >> Good, good. First, uh, want to apologize for um, how things was last time I came up here before y'all. Um, I think dearly I dislike when it's a lot of separation and when when something and when between the team and people get painted a certain way and all this different type of stuff, so that's why I get frustrated and I and I shut down, you know, because uh, this doesn't help us win. So, it's kind of like a option, but not a option. So, I don't I feel drained when I express myself, um, to people and places and cameras when it's not received and taken the right way or it's we're trying to divide the team or anything like that. So, that's where I was just trying to preserve my energy from going in depth with a lot of things. So, definitely. >> Shump, how do you think you played the last couple of weeks just in relation to how you started? >> Yeah. I think, uh, each and every day we we improved as a team. I got, uh, more comfortable within the offense. There's definitely still challenges every day that you got, uh, um, correct and focus on and, uh, be able to improve. >> Do you know when you'll be going into the game on Saturday? >> Nah. Coach Mike, and he he's going to tell you y'all how he told y'all. Y'all would know Y'all would know as soon as we know. >> Uh sure coaches talk so much about the pre-snap operation. Um and yesterday coach Switzer talked about that trying to save those eight seconds. Um how important is that in your role and how much improvement do you think you made the coaches all say that you've gotten so much better in that? >> Uh it's very important. That's why it's like that's why I talk about saving your energy, you know, so you got to throughout my day I find ways on how I can save my energy to be able to be a battery out there to be able to operate fast, you know, and uh do everything with a purpose and very quickly. You can't do all that when it's when you pulled in a lot of different directions, you know, cuz that's how I feel drained. I feel drained that way. And I tested it, you know, so I know what what what helps me, you know, what and what uh puts me in the best situation to operate, you know, how the coaches would like. >> Is there one Is there one thing in particular when you're in a game situation that you're really kind of looking forward to seeing where you've grown the most from last year, what you know, from that Cincinnati game to, you know, finally getting back out there in real game setting and and and seeing where it's it's improved the most? >> No, we approach practice like a game. So, it's the same amount of focus and seriousness that it is. Um so that's why I'm excited excited to to um feel is like how similar does it feel to practice, honestly? Because it's a different type of intention and a mentality, you know, that that we go out there every day with. >> I was probably going to ask you that, but I saw somewhere that you have a blister or blisters on your hand or something like that, which might make it a little bit difficult. Is there any truth to that whatsoever? >> No, that that happened this this past off season getting back into it. Um just from throwing a lot. Honestly, that's where it came from and uh they all healed up now. Yeah, but that was the thing like I would say at the start of um training camp and everything that you know, we just had to work through and uh be able to figure out. >> So, so what you doing? You just said that you treat practice like a game. What areas specifically do you think you've improved most in since that last game last season? >> I would say being a great teammate, especially to that guy right there. >> [laughter] >> All right, I got a question for you though. >> What's your question? >> If you had a walk out of the tunnel song, what song would it be? >> It'd be perfect timing. It'd be perfect timing. I hope yours will be that, too. >> So, should you go go ahead with the answer if you want to, please. >> Um, what was the question? >> What what You taught you said that you treat practice like a game. So, my question was what specific areas have you improved most since seeing in the last >> I wouldn't really say improved most. I'll say every area I try to improve. It's like it's like a chart within myself and seeing, okay, if I got 10 different areas to improve, like let's improve each area every day, you know, until it it gets to max threshold. Max threshold, that takes some time, you know. That's going to take a couple of years, you know, max threshold, but um I think I'm improving in every area overall. >> Coach Mack was saying the other day that he wants to see you and Machine in preseason games because it's a little bit different when quarterbacks can get hit. You there's a little maybe an extra layer of evaluation there. How if at all does the game change for you when you know you can be hit? you got to think of how many times I got hit in college. It It don't It don't really phase me at all at this point uh in life and obviously it's it's it's the league and I got hit multiple times last year. so I I like I like I like the challenge of going out there to to to be able to to get the ball out my hand so I don't get hit. You know, that's the challenge for me. Uh to be able to make the right reads, to be able to go through the progressions and get and figure it out. You know, and even in practice even I don't take it lightly. Um when I possibly could get hit cuz I'm I'm I'm trying to improve the process and speed everything up, you know. And that's and and and it's extremely tough, but it's definitely a challenge I look forward to every day going out there. >> You also mentioned switching up the practices with the ones every day. I mean, how do you think you've handled that so far in these first few weeks? >> Yeah. I think that doesn't even phase me or get to me or I think about that at all. You know, I'm just thankful to be out able to practice, you know. So sometimes you got to sit back and reflect on why would I feel negative in this situation if if last year was a totally different situation, so I think of all things that I'm thankful for in life and not that I that I really want. If you live in that want world, then you going to always be searching. >> Shady, there's there's been a lot of interceptions at this camp. Defense is playing great. I understand that. Do you have to feel as the quarterbacks, why is that? I'm not sure. I just try to go about the process every day. Make my decisions and not really second guess or not. and not really like I try to go through the process the right way and try to do everything I'm trying to do. So, I think I think as long as that's at the forefront of the mind and understanding situations, understanding down the distance, understanding what's going on then then you'll be able to know when it's time to force something and when it's not time to. So, I know being on the field for me the longest I'm going to be able to get a get a feel. So, it's like why put yourself in a situation where you could get taken off a field or anything. So, that's what I try to focus on and obviously it doesn't really happen like that. Some things are tip picks, some things are like just things happen. So, it's kind of if I know last year within the season everything, I threw some picks. then it's like of course it's going to be a point of emphasis to be confident with every decision I make. And that's just in life. Any decision I make I'm I'm fine with it and I got to stand by it and uh life and football translate to each other. So, even now the decisions I make off the field like I got to stand on it. I live by it and you know I can't regret it. >> So, a few days ago when you know you found out I guess maybe before the walkie did that you weren't going to be taking the one reps you know with the pads on that day. Did you I watched you step up with the you know 11 on 11s and sit like three straight passes right away right Did you take that as a positive and not let that become anything where you wondered why that was happening like that? >> No, I don't think I don't think with the coaches that we have you ever wonder. I think whatever is said is direct. Obviously it's like we was we was informed you know and everything the right way. So, it was never a miscommunication between us, you know. So, I don't know. I just don't really appreciate sometimes uh if things happen and and if things happen and y'all just jump on the cuz like he just tripping or something, you know, I don't I don't I don't really like that because it it creates just extra and I hope we all here to to want to win, you know, and be a team and be a franchise. So, it's kind of like we got to slow down, you know, if that's what we want. But if we just in here to just make money and get clicks then, you know, we understand that, too. that's why I just appreciate the team. I appreciate everybody that uh we don't let anything online or anything really get to us, you know, because we're all in our own cocoon. We're a team. So, anything outside of that don't really affect us within the building. >> It seems like since since Todd got here, you've been saying things like that, you know, whatever the coach has told you guys you trust and you mentioned at the beginning of the camp that he understood you very well. How did he go about [clears throat] building that that trust with you? >> I'd say by just letting everybody be theirself. Um that's that's how he is overall. He wants every player and everybody to be theirself and be able to cuz you know, that's that's the best way that everybody will be able to produce and be able to be theirself. So, I think that's what it is. It's just everybody has freedom each and every day. You could be how you want to be within the guidelines of the team and long as you're not like disrespecting or doing anything negative then, you know, you kind of have like freedom. >> You saw Last one. >> I I don't know what ones and twos are. Honestly, I'm telling you. It It switches every day. So, what's ones and what's twos? It's just work. What's What's work are we getting today? >> More so just uh with with Denzel and KC who's obviously looking up some good plays as well. Just how have you kind of developed What's What's your chemistry been like with them? What do you How do you kind of work with them on that? >> Yeah, I'll say it's good. I'll say the chemistry uh is definitely growing. With each rep that I take with anybody, I would say. because football is just a bunch of different situations that you know, in practice you may hit on one time. So, like each day, that's why I say you you growing and building in different areas because just cuz you practice it's a bunch of different situations that in practice. So, you look at things from different point of views, you know, and and it's way deeper than just it's way deeper than just it's first and 10, I'm going to throw a slant versus like it's third and short, you know, throwing a slant. It's kind of like it's a big difference, you know, between it because one like it's super on the line, the other one, you know, you may not be as aggressive in. So, it all it's all about um down the distance, it's all about uh managing the game, time on the clock, and I think that's where as a team and everybody we're trying to get better at each and every day. And being able to handle all the installs and everything that um it's put us on it's put on us is great and it's and it's ups and downs, it's strenuous sometimes, it's not, but it's good because that's how I said that I feel like the game when everything's more simplified, everything will be a a lot more smoother within us. >> Hey. >> Hey, thanks. >> Appreciate it. >> Appreciate this one. >> It's all right. >> Oh, you good, bro. >> Like I said, it's >> It's chaotic. >> It's Let's Answer the question last yesterday. >> you about this opportunity whether I don't know if Coach Monk has told you whether you're starting or not, but just getting out there finally and and and see and playing in a real game. >> I'm super excited. I think uh the hard work that I put in with the training staff, with uh my my team, my personal team to, you know, get to this stage has been uh tremendous for myself. Um so, I'm super excited, you know, for those opportunities and uh can't wait for it. >> Sean, can you talk about the way that just over the the past week, um at least from my vantage point, it seems like it's really kind of come together for you and your performance has elevated by you taking advantage of that week like last week and stacking good practices. Kind of what's going on here? >> Um just getting comfortable with with what Coach Monk is, you know, wanted us to do as a as a QB and as a, you know, as a team and, you know, what is he looking for, trying to get on the same page on how he calling plays in certain situations. So, you know, my my job every day is what I live by is just keep trying to win the day and every day I just take it one day at a time. Can't rush anything and, you know, I'll let let the football that I've been doing for my whole life just kind of take care of itself. So, again, I'm in a good spot and just keep keep trying to work and find ways to get >> Sean, what do you think the impact of some of those earlier interceptions? You know, around the last time we talked to you, looking back on them now, how much of that was maybe due to you experimenting, trying different things, like just like kind of like you talked about last time? >> Yeah, I mean, um I think every interception isn't especially at this time of the year. You kind of got to look at them differently. Certain situations, what what are we working on? What throws are we working on? Have I tried this throw before? Um you know, we we might have tried it in a live scenario and see if I can try it in a live period and you know, sometimes the defense make a good job and then also, you know, sometimes it might be a bad throw or a bad decision. So, you kind of got to grow from them and um it's better to have those moments now rather than uh actual game. >> I guess all of that, how do you how do you kind of go through the mental part of this last time you were up to? How do you kind of go through the mental part of it and say, "All right, this is the session where I should try some things. I can try some things versus this one where I want to make sure like I'm just going to take what the defense gives me and kind of go from >> Yeah, I think it goes back to, you know, in between periods, just making sure that, you know, I'm on the same page but what period we working on? Is it third down? Is it third and short? Is it fourth down? Is it red zone? Uh is it first and 10? Is it uh opportunities where we taking shots? Is it third and long where, you know, coach Monken is giving us a green light to test those throws. So, I think it's just really just finding those situations within the game and being smart and and then watching the tape and actually, you know, sitting down with the coaching staff and then, you know, reviewing it so we don't, you know, make those same mistakes or, you know, even if it does, you know, work, all right, we don't want to grow and have it living on those type of throws and situations. >> You said the other day that he wants to see you in Sugar in preseason games because obviously you guys can get hit. That's a different situation than when you have it in practice. Especially for you, you haven't been hit for in a couple of years now. What extra layer of evaluation maybe does that add for you in a preseason game? >> Um I mean, for me it's just really just being able to play live football against a different opponent. So, uh you know, I'm not worried about being hit or anything like that. You know, that's part of the game, so um but as far as me just operating in a live setting without being on the practice field and coaches being on the field with you, that's what I'm looking forward to and just getting those reps. >> LeSean was LeSean Sugar was talking about how coach makes practice very game-like. How I mean in what ways do you feel like he he he does that in having you know been in games before, what what can't you replicate no matter how hard you try when you're out there beyond obviously the the contact that you you know you you face you know from defense? >> I mean I think the biggest thing is just really I think what we just talked about is just those mistakes. You know, the interceptions, the the turnovers, the bad operation. You know, those those things get you beat. So again, that's I think that's the biggest thing where you got to take it with a grain of salt and you got to kind of again, you got to learn from it. You got to pick your spots and sometimes, you know, we might get a little too greedy and you know, try to do some things and it goes the wrong way and then we got to go back and watch the tape and know in this situation, these are the things that can lose you ball games and be able to check it down. So you know, you take that, you put it in your memory bank and then the next rep you try to improve from it. >> How about rhythm? How does a how does a game setting help you build rhythm differently from practice? >> Yeah, cuz the game is a lot faster. You know, a lot faster. People are thinking differently. You don't have those times where you kind of prepping on again, you know, this is third down. So you know, third down we're going to play the sticks rather in a game where you got to be locked in on the situation. You know, the the plays you're not really you're thinking about the last rep, the last play, but you know, and you forget that it's third down, second down or you know, you might play it a little bit differently in practice, so you know, all those things just got to you know, it takes time and and the more opportunities we get in preseason to be able to get those opportunities and reps is very helpful. >> LeSean, what do you think you learned most about yourself since training camp began? learn most about myself? I mean Nah, I already know who I am, so I don't I don't think anything. >> Well, I mean, as far as your you know, getting back in that football groove. >> Uh I mean, it's just you know, it's like it's like riding a bike, you know, it's just kind of getting back and just playing football, playing free. I think the biggest thing is just really mental. It's my mental side is really just coming coming in, taking it one day at a time, not worried about what's going on outside, and just focusing on my opportunities. >> I've never heard so much use of the word cadence than the training Well, every day it comes out from coach O'Brien. 10-year veteran at your position now, are you as frustrated about what's going on as he appears to be? >> Uh I mean, yeah, I think coach is definitely going to be frustrated cuz you know, he he wants perfection, and that's what we strive for. And you want a coach that is striving for that, you know, even one pre-snap penalty, two pre-snap penalties, you know, it might seem small in the grand scheme of things, but those things get you beat, you know, like I mentioned before, so um you know, this is very similar to how my training camps were back when I first got drafted with coach Bill O'Brien, you know, very aggressive, very intense, you know, he wants perfection, especially coming from the New England system with Brady. Everything was to the beat, to the you know, crossing the T's and and dotting the I's, so um you know, I'm very familiar with that, and you know, we got to stay on top of those things because you know, they're either going to help you or they're going to you know, help you lose lose a lot of games. >> I have two things real quick. How much do you think it will help you once you get to take those or once you do get to take those first team reps every day to develop that continuity day after day after day with the level of everything another one >> Um yeah, I mean, it's very helpful. I think when it's very helpful when you get to you know, speak with the uh play with the same guys, practice with the same guys, so you you kind of build that trust, and you build that okay, this guy is coming out this way. Everyone is different, everyone has different tendencies. Uh everyone has different ways of running routes, and how explosive they are, and you know, catch radius uh radius radius. You know, everything about that. So, you know, it's you know, it's obviously it's hard to going back and forth in different guys, but you know, you just try to you know, learn as much as possible and try to trust it as much as possible until that opportunity comes. >> The only other thing real quick is the fact that nine times out of 10 when I see you make a throw it goes exactly where you want it to go and it looks very accurate. It looks great. Occasionally it looks like maybe the ball didn't go exactly where you wanted it to go. Is that just typical normal practice for any quarterback or are you still kind of knocking a little bit of rust off or what what happens when you see a pass that looks a little off? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's I think it's not not every quarterback's going to be perfect. So, I I don't think it's it's just no different than you know, Steph Curry going to shooting a three. You know, sometimes it looks really really good, but he that's not the first time he's tried that. So, you know, a lot of times he he missed a lot of shots and you keep you keep repeating it until you get it perfect. So, um yeah, you know, sometimes it's going to be off. Defense give you different looks. You know, they get paid on the other side and we have a really good defense and they doing a lot of different things disguising and and making it tough for the offense. So, you just try to you know, time it up and the ball doesn't go that way and they be in the right spot. So, again, that's what the tape and and this this time period is for is being able to learn and and gain that trust and gain that experience so you you know, you can put it in your memory bank and and move forward. >> When you get back like in your mind you envision yourself playing exactly how you used to and you think that maybe you have to change your style a little bit just given the injuries and the >> Yeah, I mean I'm different, man. I think I think I I think ever since I've been here you know, early on I think you know, bringing up Houston was was you know, cool, but you know, I'm 30 now. So, I think you know, I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed, but the mentality and and how I play and and what I you know, how I approach it doesn't, so um I don't know. I think just going out there and just playing free and and let my, you know, instincts just take over, you know, so I think that's the biggest thing and, you know, I've always had a coach, you know, my Coach O'Brien always told me, you know, always trust my instincts, so um you know, I think that's the biggest thing is just go out there, play free and let the game come to me. >> That's your cue, we're going to wrap. >> Totally just fumbled. >> practicing better than you ever have as a Cleveland Brown. >> Uh of course. Yeah, of course. You know, I have a I have a clear vision. I have a clear mind, so I mean, I think the world know know what what I went through. Uh it's it's no secret, you know, off the field and then on the field also with injuries, so I think for anybody that had, you know, what I went through I think, you know, would be in a different spot maybe, you know, so I think I'm mentally tough and, you know, dealt with it as as best as I possibly could to be able to be sitting here talking with you guys, you know, so I think if I would have handled it differently, I definitely wouldn't be, you know, sitting right here, you know, in front of you guys on my fifth year. >> Deshaun, in in recent days you're really thriving with the passing and the scramble. Uh a good time. In recent days you're really thriving with the passing and the running and that's a central part of the game now. Thanks to having an injury, how's it been for you post injury with being able to rehab and being back now? That's your game and your comfort level has come from. >> Uh it's been good. I think being able to practice it and be able to get on the field and I know it's not live, but guys are chasing us, our defense doing a heck of a job of reacting and and being full speed to the point of attack. Uh it's been really good to be able to test, you know, my injuries and see where I'm at and my strength, so I think I'm in a good spot and confident that, you know, it's going to continue just get better and improve. >> What is, especially when you have a new offensive line, totally giving them plenty of time >> Um a lot of film study, um a lot of one-on-one time, and just a lot of just communication. I think just normal conversation, you know, when we're eating lunch, dinner, uh breakfast in the locker room, just kind of bringing it up, showing them different clips, and then once we get on the field, you know, just try to apply everything that we talked about off the field on the field and and see how fast we can uh you know operate it and and then see it and um just go out there and try to execute. So, um it's a lot of just talking and just watching it and just being on the same page. >> Good. Thank you. >> No, I think we're okay.

That's the the downfall of coming from a small program like Morgan State, but like the physical gifts, look, if he shows up on special teams in the preseason, I'm keeping Eric Hunter over Roy Reiter or or Joey Joey Iupati. Like, that's I I'm taking the upside over over a vet that's a one-year vet min deal. And so, I I want to see if Hunter can carry some of these practice performance traits to the preseason. >> Did you mention his hit stick on Meeks a couple days ago in practice, too? >> Woo! Lit him up. >> Yeah, dropped him with a shoulder. I mean, didn't even tackle him. Meeks Meeks caught a pass in the flat turn, bang. Blew him up. Um so, yeah, I agree. Eric Hunter has definitely popped up in the notepad a few times. You know, I was going to say Blake Miller for this one. I don't want to reiterate too much of what you said already, Justin, cuz I agree with all of it. I will take you guys inside a conversation that two the two of us had yesterday. I was sitting down writing about Blake Miller and I just turned to Justin and I said, "Hey, on a curve, all things considered, he's a rookie, he's repping a ton against Aidan Hutchinson, he's trying to to a new offense, how would you grade Blake Miller two weeks into camp? And your answer was, Justin? >> C. >> Yeah, and I I I I think that's >> C plus. >> I think that's fair. And then I say, okay, well, in a vacuum, if if he was just defined as what the Lions want him to be this year, which is a stable starting right tackle, the grade is probably more so far, again, so far, two weeks in. >> You know, a little bit more C minus. >> See, yeah, C minus. And so, I think I think tomorrow is a a good opportunity for him to show what he can do against someone other than Aidan Hutchinson that still is a starting caliber NFL defensive end. It sounds like the Bengals are going to play most of their guys. I I don't know if Boye Mafe is expected to play. I I would assume. And so, you you you know, you hope that you can see Blake get some some pass pro reps against a player of that caliber and hold his own. That's clearly what the Lions want to see him develop the most. It was no surprise when Dan said that a couple days ago based on what we've watched in training camp. It feels like, you know, he's got all of the attributes and ability in the run game that they're looking for. There's really no concern there, I don't think. But, Dan did say when I asked him like, where do you need to see him grow the most now that he's your guy by week one? Most of it's in pass pro. And, you know, maybe that's a function of just kind of getting taken to the woodshed by Hutchinson so often this training camp. But, um I had a chance to talk with Blake yesterday for a pregame interview on the radio that will run tomorrow night. So, catch that. But, uh I want to just tease something he said here because I asked him like, how do you measure your your growth in pass protection? What should it look like to you over the next few weeks? Uh and he said, and this is something like, you know, I'll have in mind when I'm watching him tomorrow night. He said, for me it's I got to have my feet planted, got to have a great base to punch off of, I got to be ready to punch, I got to be in phase, and I'm throwing those hands. So, you know, I'll I'll I'll be pretty intrigued to to watch how Blake handles himself tomorrow in those one-on-one pass reps, especially if or pass pro reps, especially if they come against a guy of of Mafi's capability. >> Yeah, those are That's a great one. Um I think I'll go with Just kind of going back and forth. Can I give you two names? >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. >> Yeah. Okay. I mean, Nic Whiteside is obvious. Like >> really all these cornerbacks that we're watching that are going to play tomorrow because the Bengals are playing Joe Burrow, Tee Higgins, and Ja'Marr [laughter] Chase. Yeah. So, right off off that alone, like if one of these guys can hold their own against those dudes and you know, show us something, that will probably elevate them over the other if they're neck and neck right now. So, curious about him. Those two Those two guys in particular. And then I go with Seth McLaughlin for a similar reason just because Dexter Lawrence is playing some snaps now as Justin mentioned. Don't know how many snaps he's going to play. It could just be [clears throat] like three or four. But, if we're going to see that match-up, you know, look, I saw McLaughlin kind of get get taken I saw him get a little burned by uh Alim McNeill the other day in practice. And like Alim does that to a lot of guys, so I'm not going to like hold it against him. But, if you're judging a potential player that could be a week one starter for this team, then I got to see how they do against other team starters. And if the team's going to play their starters against the Lions in the preseason, McLaughlin is going to be the starter. We'd like to see how he holds up. So, if he can hold up and just like not I'm not saying he's got to dominate Dexter Lawrence, but if he can just like not get knocked back into the quarterback, um then that's a positive sign and a guy that you can maybe start to believe in a little bit more as training camp continues. Um so, I go McLaughlin and I'll go with the the two corners. I'll go Ennis and I'll go Nic Whiteside. >> I like that. Can I Can I toss out a one more and but it's going to be in the form of two names? There's an interesting rise going on at running back with with Vakie having been sidelined for a bit with with the nose injury, obviously with with Gibbs having his hold in and Pacheco being sidelined. Sailors and Jabar Small have gotten a ton of run here, Probably more than they would even like, as Justin said [snorts] last week. It was funny when JaMycal was asked about that, he was like, "Hey, that's on me. My bad." >> I got to get back out here and spell these guys. But, I think, you know, one of those guys has a chance in the preseason and the rest of camp to potentially pass Sione Takitaki on this depth chart. And that's painful for me to say as someone who said he might have [laughter] more carries this year >> What is this? >> than than than Pacheco. But, you know, you you can prove yourself in on stages like this, especially to a a staff that puts a lot of stock in these games. So, you know, I I'd be curious to see what one of those one of those two guys can do. >> Did Will just hedge a bet? >> Completely. >> Yes, he did. >> I'm also not I'm not sure JaMycal Small is going to play tomorrow, Will. He was fighting through something. He didn't practice that last one. Um So, if you know what that means, a little bit more Kai. >> Yeah, baby. Let him rumble. >> I'm going to go with the guy who's handing the ball off to Kai. I'm going to go Luke Altmyer. >> Let's go, Will. >> They had to do it. >> The reason why I I I do genuinely like um the skillset he does I I think as the way he plays quarterback would fit ideally if he could kind of continuously improve with what the Lions want to do at quarterback because he can move, but he's a pocket pure pocket passer. Very accurate. Um I got to watch him a lot just watching college football games. And I really like Luke Altmyer. And I think he's got to go to Even though the Passtronaut is currently ahead of him. The Passtronaut, Josh Dobbs, which you know, that's it's a good sounding by the Lions there. I I just think this is the a good runway for Luke Altmyer. I know Dan mentioned it. He just needs reps. Well, here you go. Throw you out in the fire against the ones basically of the Bengals. So, I'm very curious to see kind of how he responds. He's only being 23 years old. Um and he's played at least for our start a lot of games in college. But, I am curious to see how that translates preseason. So, um I'll go Luke Altmyer. >> Dude, I have never heard that nickname for Dobbs. That is epic. >> Oh. >> The pastor Dobbs? >> No, I didn't know. >> Bring it up to him later. Yeah, everyone calls him that. >> Yeah, I definitely will. >> Did either one of you when Dobbs walked out, first team rep just drops one of the best passes of camp, just this corner route to Cedric Wilson between two defenders and I'm like, "Oh, I'm sorry Luke Schoonmaker, >> your chances just one pass done." >> I mean, you can't compete with a guy who's working with NASA. I mean, the the brain capacity that Josh Dobbs has, I mean, it's incredible. It really is. >> Yeah, Luke saw that pass and had the the face mask meme where it's smiling, but he's actually crying behind it. >> Oh, yeah, it it it'll be fun and we'll be here next week to recap it all. We appreciate you guys. Lions Collective, subscribe if you haven't already, hit the like button of course as always and check out these guys work. You check out my work as well. We'll catch you guys next week. >> and that last segment was brought to you by Dog and Pony Show. Just to be Just Just toss it out there. >> Which by the way, just toss it out there. Let's go. >> I'm glad you brought that up, which by the way, we did we did our pick for the preseason game. We each gave our pick. Your pick should be Dog and Pony Show Brewing, which by the way, if you mention Lions Collective, you get a dollar off, which I know it's like, "Oh, it's a No, it goes a long way." You go there, you have some beers with the boys or girls, you get a dollar off. It adds up. So, you say you you you watch Lions Collective, Cal will hook you up. They're great over there at Dog and Pony Show Brewing. So, >> The more you drink, the more you save. >> Yeah, there it is. Until next week, we will catch you all. >> Peace. >> Good.

title: Klint Kubiak, Fernando Mendoza and Kirk Cousins Postgame Presser | Preseason Week 1
text: Before we go, you know, BJ had a foot, so we'll evaluate him tomorrow. And then, uh, you know, obviously Max did not play. That was my decision. And I'll take you guys take your questions. >> Clint, obviously you have not had the opportunity to review the film, but your first game as a head coach. Just initial feelings on how you felt the game went from a logistics standpoint. >> No, I I thought uh, you know, I thought it was smooth there. I thought our coaches did a good job communicating on the headset. you know, the game itself, uh, you know, we have a lot lot to improve on. Really, you know, uh, really happy with what the offense did in that first drive. Uh, you know, Kirk leading us down the field. Um, I was, you know, very happy with what our defense did in the second half on third down after the first half. Um, but there's a lot of things that we need to improve on. >> What did Fernando tonight? Uh well, you know, he uh you know, I thought he, you know, let a he let a good scoring drive as far as getting in and out of the huddle and commanding the group and uh getting the play calls down. You know, I saw I saw the same guy that we've seen in practice. I see, you know, an ascending player. We just got to keep getting better. >> Uh excuse me, Clint, just your impressions of how the offense offensive line look, especially in terms of the run blocking. >> Yeah, I think I'll take a take time to peek at it tomorrow. You know, definitely didn't get to run as much tonight. We had to throw it a bunch in that second half. Um, but uh, you know, I'd like to like to peek at it first, but you know, it's something that that we're always trying to get better at is is our run blocking, play action, and making things look the same, but we got to be able to be in the game at the end so we can keep doing that the whole game. >> Hey, coach. Uh, what are your thoughts on Mike Washington's first game, and what did you personally take away from his performance tonight? >> Pleased with what Mike did? Mike did some good things. Um, you know, just like he practiced. I think he's this was the same player that we've seen in practice. You know, had a big run and um you know, just got to keep giving him more ops as this preseason goes. >> How valuable do you anticipate this tape being for Fernando in terms of teaching this next week here? >> Yeah. Him and him and all the all the rookies, all the veterans, our whole team. You know, it'll be really important for us to go improve as a team and uh you know, just go tell the truth and get better. >> Did everything go in terms of playing time the way you wanted, you know, divvied up the reps. Does that go according to plan tonight? >> It did. Yes. Fernando had quite a few I think more series than I thought he was going to play. Did do you have any thought process moving forward? How much more you plan to see him in games two and three? Is that plan already made? >> We want to get him plenty of reps in the preseason. You know, that was important for us to to see him get, you know, get lots of turns and, you know, as these games go on. You know, we're going to evaluate game to game, but you know, he's a young man that needs needs experience and needs reps and we're going to give them to him. you still have a really young defense, especially in that secondary, kind of having some, you know, tribulations throughout the game. You know, what's the biggest thing that you can tell them, you know, going forward that can help him improve? >> I just think we got we got a lot of growth to do, you know, as as a team. As a team, we got a lot of growth to do. So, starts tomorrow. >> What do you make of Fernando's competitive spirit? It seems like he was really trying to extend plays, but also some of that was, you know, maybe him holding on to the ball too long. just how do you balance him trying to make those plays but also just like he's an NFL quarterback and he's got to get rid of it at some point. >> Yeah, there'll be some good some good lessons, you know, uh that we look forward to attacking with the tape with him. He knows, you know, he can't take a sack and uh but those are things he's going to grow from. >> Clint on your left here, uh Jack Bash, couple big catches on third down. What did you see out of him today? >> Uh he stepped up, had a had an excellent game. He really has had an impressive camp as far as just being a guy that's continually straining and getting better and uh hasn't had all the ops in practice and then he came out tonight and was ready to roll. So, I was happy uh but not surprised with what he did tonight. >> Hey, coach, would you say the leaders on this team stepped up, you know, even during some of the rougher times tonight? >> Well, I think we know we lost by two scores, so we got to we got to get better there. Ready, guys? >> Um, how do you evaluate like preseason action versus what you've seen from these players in practice and in training camp? >> Well, I think we put a lot of value in practice. You know, we put a put a lot of value and and good on good in practice and that's, you know, sometimes just as good as a game. Um, so you know, these preseason reps are very valuable, but you know, our evaluation, uh, throughout the throughout the course of training camp, you know, has revealed to me that when we get on the field, you see a lot of the same, you know, so things that that show up in practice that are not good and the things that are that are positive, they they showed up here tonight. >> Uh, coach, I know you said earlier how the decision to name the starting quarterback for the regular season will be team based. So my question is how soon you you feel like the team is ready to name a starting quarterback or is this you know still early in the process for you? >> Yeah. Well, you know, Kirk's been getting the reps with the ones. I think he's had a solid training camp and you know it's his job to lose. >> That's good. Thanks, coach. >> Thanks. >> We start it and then I'll take any questions you have. Um, good to get back out there and in front of our fans and um, uh, you know, get accustomed to the stadium after the practice a couple nights ago and now tonight it's good to get these experiences and um, you know, there's nothing quite like a game. You know, especially as a quarterback position with the red jersey taken off, it's important that you get out there and get those live bullets. So, um, you know, it was good to get that experience. thought the team played hard and coaches gave us a good plan and um um you know we'll keep building from here and look forward to going going to Houston and playing against a really good defense in practice the next uh next week. So take any questions you have. >> Kirk, you had to feel extremely good about the one drive that you were in there. Just the way the huddle looked, the way the guys you take us inside just how how smooth did it feel for the first real rep in a live situation like that? >> It felt smooth. I was uh proud of the offensive line, the communication, the receivers. You know, we made a check at one point. Everybody got the check, did what they were supposed to do. Um I thought Clint did a great job of getting the play call in early, communicating well, so we weren't up against the play clock. Um and guys played hard, did their assignments, made plays, and um that's what it's about. And so u small sample size, but um always good to get out there and and move the football and score points. Kirk, I know you have a job to do and to continue secure QB1, but in that somewhat mentor role when you grabbed the clipboard and got a chance to see Fernando, what was your assessment? What did you see in in terms of what you've been working with him, communicating and and putting it on the field for him tonight? >> Yeah, he did a great job. Moved the football, um scored points, gave us a chance at scoring points and uh um operated well. Oh, I think it's it's valuable experience to get out there for all of us and play. And I think he'd say the same thing that was it was just valuable to get out and play. And um thought he did a nice job. >> Kirk, uh real comfortable first drive. I mean, really looked very professional, very uh uh like you've been doing it for a long time and uh I think everybody was pleased with that in the crowd. How did you feel the crowd reacted to you? >> I don't know that I was really paying too much attention. I tried to look down the black hole every now and then, you know, pretty iconic. um couple of those iconic fans that I've seen for years from a distance. It's fun to kind of be a part of it now. Um just taking it all in. It's a great stadium, great environment, and we got to they're dying to cheer for us. We got to give them reason to to get up out of their seats. And so, um that's what we're trying to do. >> Uh hi. Being back in Kovak system, what were some things that you realized maybe you missed? >> Great question. Uh, this is going to sound weird, but I enjoyed hearing his voice again, you know, in a game and being able to get um the play call. It brought back memories of 21 and uh it's kind of fun to be full circle back with him again. And um you know, he's he's uh very urgent, very intentional, very detailed. He's a great listener and um you know I felt that going into this game and through the game with the way he operates and um I think it was a big reason you know his demeanor, his approach, his preparation, his organization is a big reason why I think I played well with him in 21 and and back in 19 and 20 as well when he was a QB coach and I think it's a big reason um you know why we would be able to have success together this year is because of his approach. >> Uh Clint noted that Jack Bash hasn't had a ton of opportunities in practice but tonight seemed to play pretty well. what you see from him. >> Yeah, I'd agree. I I don't think the ball has found him as much in practice as we would have liked. Um what I've noticed of Jack is very strong hands and um as a quarterback, you know, there's going to be tight coverage in this league and so you need people who with someone, you know, right on them can still go grab the football, you know, and that's what the the great receivers I've played with have been able to do. And Jack has that trait. And so, um he showed it again tonight. And part of the reason I felt I could put it on him is because I knew, you know, Jack's going to be like a power forward with an entry pass there. And even though the the DB's coming, he's gonna have a strong hands and bring the ball in and hold on. And um he has a play strength that I really like and it gives me confidence to to drill the ball on him knowing that he can make those plays. >> What was your advice to Fernando going into his preseason debut? And what do you think of his game? >> Yeah, I just let him be. I don't know that I give him advice. I don't like pull him aside and say, "Hey, you know, come hear from my wisdom." I think he's he's a pretty smart, mature player and person. And if anything, I I don't want to get in his way. I think he knows what he's doing and has a good feel and I don't want to overload him. And so, if ever I am observing, if I feel like I can offer a quick nugget here or there, I will. He's a great question asker, so a lot of times he'll just ask. But, um, there's also times where I say, "Hey, nothing needs to be said. You know, go do your thing. You got it." So, um, he's, you know, there's a lot of good football up ahead for him. >> All good. >> Okay. Thanks. >> Go to Hondo here. First of all, >> Fernando, you got that first game under your belt. Just thoughts, quick reaction. I know you haven't seen the film, but for getting your first NFL game and fulfilled the dream. Just your quick reaction. Yeah, first I want to thank God and my teammates and coaches for allowing me the opportunity. Today was it was an invigorating experience where there's not many moments where you feel fully alive and on the field is when you feel fully alive, especially in the NFL atmosphere. So, want to give thanks to that. It It was great to get out there, get my feet wet. You know, at first, especially the first drive, felt a little sped up because so much anticipation and excitement. However, I feel like the team, my teammates around me protected me very well and they helped me, they helped slow me down. And I think as uh it was a good experience. >> You had that pass to Malik between three defenders. What gave you the confidence, I guess, to just pull the trigger on that play? Yeah, it's all about the timing and trusting your feet as coach especially as coach Janoko and coach Sullivan say is at that point in time I knew I was able to identify the coverage and I knew the spot Malik was going to be and that was a good timing and anticipation with the route. It was fantastic protection. It was a great fake by the running back and it was something that we've worked on of building that timing and anticipation. However, there's other throws and other, you know, passes that I made that did not have great time and anticipation throughout the game, but that was uh one that was was a good connection and it shows that there are some that, you know, I have time and anticipation. Like you see Kirk Kirk is just time anticipation. Boom, boom, boom. And so that's an area I got to grow in. >> Jack said in the locker room he's taking the ball. Who's going to get the ball? >> Oh, Jack. Jack got Jack Jack has it. He he risked his body and, you know, made a great catch. The offensive line made made great blocks and it was it was great. I actually didn't realize that that was Jack's first touchdown and evidently hopefully, you know, in looking forward in the future, him scoring many touchdowns in the regular season. >> I was ask a rookie right there when the jitters went out, but I'm wondering how much you were able to lean on when you think about the career you had and the game you played before tonight, the crowd, everything that was at stake. Were you able to lean on that mentally at any point to help get the jitters out? Did that play a role in any way? >> I believe that confidence is always a big part in how you play, especially whether you're an athlete, artist, performer, in everyday life, confidence is a big aspect in your eventual performance. And one of the sources of confidence is prior experience. So, I have leaned on that in the past. However, you know, Mr. Brady was able to talk to our team last night and he he said like no matter how good of a high school or college player you were, the NFL is a different level. And I felt that tonight and I have a lot to grow from. >> Fernando, just going in your emotions, were they what you thought they would be? Did you feel different before you ran on the field for the first time? >> Yeah, I would say they are what what I thought they would be. was able, especially as a quarterback, you don't want to get too emotional because you want to be able to process, make the right checks, make the right reads. And I felt that it was it was good emotion getting in the huddle with my guys in in a sense being able to break through and finally play a snap in the preseason, which is going to be faster than, you know, practice, just how it is with adrenaline, and then the regular season gets faster than that, and on and on. So, I think it was it was a good experience to get my feet wet, but I mean overall, >> yeah, overall it was a good experience to get my feet wet. >> And then what were you thinking when you ran off the field after your second series and the touchdown? >> It was great. It was great. You know, the first series I felt a little sped up. So, it was good to come back on the sideline, learn from my mistakes, and then the second series we were able to score. Third series, you know, I missed a read there. And the fourth series, I thought we had a good thing going and then unfortunately I missed a throw at the end. Uh, and then overall I felt that the group that I was in with, you know, they they blocked fantastic. They had great routes. The run game was good, you know, and unfortunately like I I let my teammates down today, but it's but it's a growing experience and, you know, I feel like we're all we're all growing and it showed me that I need to grow a lot. >> Fernando, you play more serious tonight. I asked Coach if he had a plan in place for you to play uh week two, week three. He said you need quote lots of reps. Has it been communicated to you yet? How much action you can see in Houston or week three? >> Do you mean like preseason, week two, week three? Okay, cool. Yeah, I I believe that reps is always the answer. It's like there's no secret. You know, it's the more repetition that you have at a certain craft that you're going to able to go closer to mastery every single rep that you attain. And that's something that, you know, I strive on the opportunity. I'm excited for the opportunity. Any opportunity of rep that I get, whether it's four series tonight, whether it's, let's say, how many series week two, week three, whether it's practicing against Houston, I'm looking forward the opportunity because I have a lot of room to grow and I'm really excited to get out there with my guys. >> Mike, Jesse, you seem to have developed a pretty good rapport with Benson. Uh you talked about the one pass over the middle to him, but just overall what have you what did you see from him tonight in the game? >> Malik's a fantastic player and throughout all of camp as as well as all of our receivers, we've seen something special in him. He is he's a great playmaker. He understands the game and I believe that our chemistry is both as rookies is evolving. And so to be able to to learn from, you know, to learn from him on what he wants from ball placement, timing, anticipation. I believe we're both growing together. >> Fernando, I know you're talking about, you know, getting your feet wet and just kind of getting used to the system, but what genuinely surprised you the most about the NFL speed and uh feel for the game? Yeah, I would say that the speed also not having played all of us haven't played football in a little while. So, I think the speed's always going to be a little amped up and I thought, you know, the guys did great out there today. There was there was one play where I scrambled to the right and you know, usually sometimes I'll be able to get the edge, maybe scramble for two or three yards, and it's like, "Wow, these guys are a little faster than I thought. I'm not going to be able to get around them." So, I had to throw the ball away and try to make the smart play to best serve my teammates. So, I would say definitely faster and they hit harder. So, surprise, but no surprise. >> Uh, Fernando, from third string quarterback at Cal to now walking off the field as a Las Vegas Raider in your first NFL game. When you think on this journey now, what did tonight mean to you? >> It's a great blessing and I'm very very grateful. However, being able to get to this point that third string quarterback at Cal would have not believed where we are now. However, now that I've been able to be blessed with great teammates, coaches, and given this opportunity, I need to take full advantage of the opportunity and make sure that I best serve my teammates from now going forward. >> Fernando over here. Um, you talked about having some good plays, having some not so good plays tonight. The coaches have talked about wanting to see you bounce back from adversity most in this training camp. How do you feel like you did that? kind of bouncing back from some of those plays that you weren't so happy with tonight and kind of what's your overall approach to that? >> I think the number one thing as far as gives a quarterback is adversity is always protecting the ball. That was a big emphasis and I believe that all three quarterbacks protected the ball well tonight. So I think that was, you know, a check mark in our room. However, there was a couple reads that I missed and you know, I let some of my teammates down, whether it was a missed throw or misread or, you know, missed check and on some of the plays that I'm going to need to learn and grow from to best serve them in the future. And it's all about having the composure whether it's you come off and wow I should have made a play better play on third down to you feel bad because you want to best serve your teammates and you don't want to let them down but at the same time you understand to be at your best you be composed and have a next play mentality and look at the next play as a new opportunity as a blank slate because it's the only one that matters and that's how you control the controllables and that's how you bounce back from adversity because whether it's the first play you know where I threw it away where I should have you hit the flat. It's, you know, that one play shouldn't be able to derail your entire game. So, it's having the mental fortitude, mental strength, and having your teammates believe in you and you believe in them in order to get back on track. >> How do you feel this coaching staff and working with with Andrew and Clint on the sidelines helped you stay composed in those moments? Yeah, it they have coach Inoko, coach Kubak, and coach Sullivan. They all have a very high standard and that's a standard that I want to one day get to and that I know our entire offensive unit and team wants to get to and like I did not meet that standard tonight, you know, uh I know a lot of our offensive players most likely did got to watch the film, but and that's a standard that I think that's the best type of coaching where I mean they're not going to they're going to they're going to hold you accountable and hold you to a high standard. Uh, Fernando, how valuable is having this tape tonight against an opposing team? And how quickly do you anticipate going into that tape? >> Oh, definitely right after this. I have nothing nothing else to really do tonight. Uh, but it it's great because in training camp, you're out there. I think I believe we had like I can't probably around 10 12 practices we've had against our guys. We kind of understand each other's schemes at this point. We got a lot of reps against each other. for the personnel, but to actually be able to go through a week of preparation, scouting, a little bit of schematics against, you know, Cardinals defense, then be able to get out there, call in the huddle, have the play clock, have the real refs with the flags, have real adversity where it's not practice where it's like, okay, incomplete pass, next play, boom. It's it's not scripted.
