Yeah, what else is in store for him? >> Yeah, this is his third year. Uh he's improved on his touch, on his pooch punts. Um he's he's really bombing the ball now. I mean, he's you'll see a lot of kicks over 5.0 hang time. If he can hang the ball up 5.0, it doesn't matter who we have at gunner, they're going to be able to cover him. So, he cleans up a lot, you know, as far as that goes and I'm I'm he's really having a great camp right now. I'm looking forward to seeing him in the game, too. >> Thanks, coach. >> All right, thanks. >> Before we get into football stuff, but how was your your wedding, the rest of your summer? What what's it like uh >> It was a it was a it was a fun off season, man. Um wedding was the best night of my life. Um and I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and uh you know, had fun with us. And um yeah, that's about all I really got from that night. It's a it was a it was a crazy night. It was it was full of a lot of celebration, but um it's football, baby. >> Last year you joked about spending a year of your life in the dorms. That'll be a year and a month, I guess. Is there something about it that you're looking forward to? >> I mean, it's always going to be my sanctuary. I think Saint Joe's got a special place in my heart. Um I I time in uh that that it you know, you need to have these days. You need to have these this time of grinding with the guys, being around them all day, every day. You start to create that chemistry and that standard of how we're going to do things. And uh this year it's ramped up even more. Um especially on the offensive side of the ball. And then, man, it it feels good to have the leaders out there, you know, all feeling the same thing. >> Travis, I've talked to a lot of guys in pro sports and they tell me when they get to the league, they want to do things. Win a championship, take care of their family, and stay healthy. You've been fortunate enough to do all three. What made motivated you to still come out here and still want to play football? >> Um you know, I still I still got a lot of love for this game. You know, I still think I can go out and play at a high level and and uh I want to go out there and and prove myself that uh that I can play at a better level than I did last year. And um I think that's probably the biggest thing for me is is making sure that I'm accountable for the guys in this room and every single play that uh that I'm out there. >> What motivates you James from, you know, year one to year 14? >> I mean, year one I was just trying to make the team, I guess. Uh So, I think this year not only making the team, but uh trying to figure out how I can bring guys along with me and uh and show them how to how to play championship football. I think that's a big thing. And then um being able to just, you know, enjoy these moments with the guys that I've built this uh this culture with, you know, and Coach Reid and and uh and guys like Pat and Chris Jones and and Jordan everybody. So, >> James, what was the biggest player improvement from when you did last year? >> All aspects of football, man. Being more accountable when the ball's in the air. Uh there were a few games last year that I felt like I put on myself. Um in the blocking blocking world and being able to get my guys so we can spring guys for bigger bigger gains. Um and then on top of that, just being a better leader, you know, and when we get stuck in a in a you know, with adversity hitting, uh who's going to be able to, you know, who's going to want you in that foxhole with you? And that's one of those things that I want to be one of those guys that that everybody counts on to be there and and get us out of that foxhole. >> Last year, were you already behind it or is it something that's still in your mind? >> The fact that we didn't make the playoffs, I moved on pretty quick. Um but I think once uh once we get back into OTAs and and right now, I think everybody feels everything's got to get turned up a little bit. And that's what you're seeing right now. >> All of a sudden, this is Patrick's 10th season and I was wondering if you might recall some of your personal maximums for him. >> One of the one of the most surprising things you'll ever you'll ever find out about playing with Pat Mahomes is the guy's got a good cadence. There's something with the frequency of his voice and when he SAYS "ALL RIGHT!" IT REALLY GETS YOU TO SO, EVERYBODY JUST got to mentally, when you're tired, you really got to lock in cuz that frequency can it gets you to jump no matter what. It's a good cadence. Um Everybody knows I love that guy. That's a brother to me. Um You know, I'm so proud of the way he handled adversity from last year to right now. Um obviously, we still got about a what, a month, less than a month till till the first game. But, um if you see him out here, man, you see him enjoying the enjoying the game, competing at a high level, not thinking about the knee. And uh and he's playing his his tail off right now and leading us is the biggest thing is when you get your leaders out there, your best players out there, and they're they're setting the tone, setting the standard of the team. Um as long as 15's out there doing that, man, we're we're going to be a good football team. >> Well, in so many ways, but do you see some uh parts of him that you you value cuz he's still the same guy? >> I would say I would say the accountability to everybody around him. You know, there's one thing everybody's uh you know, you can either, you know, lead by example or or lead with your voice. I think he's he's been more uh more prone to I've obviously he's always led by example. Um but, to hold somebody accountable man-to-man and try and get the best out of them without them turning on you and things like that, especially in the dog days of camp, you you can get real you can get real ugly mentally, but um I think Pat does an unbelievable job of that and it's it's it's been one of those things that's gotten better and better over the years. Just to as uh you know, he holds me accountable, you know. Feel ready to rock and roll. I mean third day in camp for I think ninth day in pads, third day in pads this week. Body feels good. I was able to finish it a strong uh strong way and uh just trying to make sure I set that example for the guys around me to know that you know this is the standard. >> What are your impressions of Cam Watkins? >> You know, Cam Watkins going to be a hell of a ball player for us. If you didn't know that already. You know, he was uh He's a He's a he He's got every trait you could possibly want at the running back position. And and on top of that his mentality, his how smart he is, his physicality, his his aggression and how he runs with the football and just plays the game. I can't say enough about him as a teammate. We got an absolute superstar on and off the field and I >> All right, try this. Eric Bieniemy back. We talked to you about that earlier, but now gone through some camp with him. What has he brought being back here with you guys, especially for the guys who haven't been around him this >> Um one, you got intensity. Intensity is the first thing and that intensity is is infectious. Makes you want to scream at everybody doing the wrong thing and and I love that It's one of my favorite things about him. I don't think there's enough of that in the in the world, let alone in this building and I think EB's one of those guys where his accountability is going to piss you off, but if you if you treat it the right way and you act the right way or respond the right way with it, you're going to become better off it and it's going to make the team a better better team because of it and that's it's one of those things that I think we really missed here in Kansas City. >> So now last year you talked about it was just kind of a weird year last year. Was that something that maybe wasn't there or not was there? >> And that's not to say that you know, it was on anybody specific. I'd put my hand in the air and I say you know, there were things that I could have done better in that regard. Um and that's one of those things that I'm working on. It's not just going to be being me out here holding people accountable. It's the guys that are doing it the right way holding people accountable, too. >> How excited are you to bring that connection back with Mahomes considering how last year went? >> Say it again. >> How excited are you to that connection back with the homes considering how the last season ended? >> I mean, we got a lot of great players on this offense, man. It's not just me. Um, I think, you know, uh, we got some young guys that can play in Cyrus Allen, uh, Jay Royals, um, obviously Quan is is coming back. He's looking great running down the field and we got Xavier Worthy who, if you see him in the off season, we just got to give him a little healthy right now, but that man's a he's a man on a mission right now and I and I love the way he's working and his attention to detail and how he's running his routes, um, and just, you know, the aggression that he's running his routes in. Um, when we get him back out here, man, we'll be a full arsenal and I think Pat has done an unbelievable job of not only getting himself ready for here, but but working with these receivers and making sure that everybody is, you know, living up to that standard of how we're going to play this year and you can't forget Rashee Rice, man. Rashee Rice is out here working his tail off trying to get right as well and we love Four for for getting out here as and and, you know, getting through these dog days knowing he's he's coming off a knee surgery. >> Last two guys, Nick, but Travis for you, what did the moment mean cuz you watched sports since you were a little kid? What did the moment mean to be in that venue, Madison Square Garden, the most important >> MSG, man. You know, I always told myself I'd go for a for a playoff game when the Knicks were rocking and my wife went when I was stuck in a train mini camp, so I could I didn't get my opportunity to go then, so, um, it's kind of cool to be able to, you know, live out my childhood dream of being in that venue and, you know, the the Mecca of all sports venues, being able to get married in there. Can't thank, you know, the owners of MSG for allowing us to get the opportunity to do that. Knowing that we wanted a private event and everything, so it was perfect and the AC was cooking, baby. That was the best part. >> These past few years with the podcast with your brother, I guess, what does it mean that you're going to have these memories with him and kind of discussing, you know, what could be the latter years of your career? >> Man, it's a it's a blessing and a curse. man. I I had no idea it would get to this point, that is New Heights and then how big it's gotten. I'm so fortunate that you know, my brother was, you know, on board with being able to do this because it's not only you know, giving us another avenue of way of life, but and it brought our audience and and things that we want to do off the field, but you know, it's brought us closer and given us a certain amount of time throughout the week that you just get to sit down and shoot the with your bro. So, it's memories I'll never forget. Every single time we we jump on, it's we're laughing and for 4 hours, two hours. Only supposed to be a 2-hour recording, we're laughing for another 2 and 1/2, so um you know, it's it's a beautiful thing. Obviously, the the first year we did it, we went to the Super Bowl, played each other in the Super Bowl, and that'll be the most magical year. Knowing that you know, we got to put our family on on display in a in a way that we hadn't before, but to be able to keep doing this and then get the guests that we're doing, we're just so thankful and we want to be able to tell everybody's story as well as ours. >> Last one, Sam. >> Travis, so >> Both. >> Sam, with your sanctuary, I just wanted to just being up here obviously flat out other times you've been up here, what have you >> Um I'll tell you what, I like to I like to play the old man and just say just tell everybody how good we got it when they like to complain about the calf food and and and driving all the way up here and what the what the conditioning test used to be to what it is now and how how many plays the long drive drill was back then and now what it is now and not that Andy's getting soft on us, but just a different day and age, man. But, it's it's fun to reflect in those kind of ways. Just to shoot the and then and kind of poke fun at the young guys for complaining about how things are and how hard it is to be a NFL football player and you know, the beauty of it all, so like I said, this place has a special place in my heart. A lot of it is due to the fans com- is coming up here and showing love every single day. Um know it it doesn't go unnoticed. A lot of times that that gets you through the dog days and the and the tough days and you know it's uh It's definitely some place that I'll always remember when I think about football. >> Thanks Jeff. >> Have a good one guys. >> [music] [music] >> What's going on? What was the process of improving in that area? >> Making that an emphasis and then figuring out the technique cues that helped me do that. Um Funny enough I had like a really important thought pregame of the Eagles last year. It's kind of weird to like implement it after figuring out kind of that short term but that thought kind of helped me throughout the whole year and the off season as well. >> Seen you do a lot of good things on I know that was a big thing rookie year to just >> Yeah, no that's that's a big emphasis and I've never been more excited for those punts in my career. I used to especially in college I hated them because I just wanted to hit the ball far. but after hitting kind of a lot of touchbacks my first year, second year having very few, kind of this year I'm looking to be a little bit more lethal in there. Still have the mistakes be rare but you know it's a game changing play if you can pin it inside the five. So I'm looking to do that a lot more this year. >> What about the operation you with Harrison and James have been together for a few years now. How's that gone? >> Yeah, it's good. I mean the longer you play with people you learn their tendencies. You you kind of learn where their mind goes on game day and stuff like that. So it's definitely helped our chemistry grow over the past couple years. >> Anything else? >> What's the trick in like in the fine What's the trick of kicking it different with kicking the ball far versus kicking the ball high and short? >> It's It's like two completely different swings. It's like in golf like a driver versus your 60°. I mean, there's different thought process processes on both of them because there's different outcomes that you want. So, um really it's kind of completely keeping them separate that's helped me. >> On the left. you got You and Harrison were out seeing at Top Golf this morning. Tell me a little bit about how you guys like to go out there and play golf and what you do out here for camp. >> Yeah, it's good. We We do have a little bit more time on our hands than than the other players because we have less less meetings and obviously less strategy and stuff. But, um it's good to get out and do stuff like that and as weird as it may sound, I'm a big believer that that stuff helps us. Like we're all We're going out there to compete. We're keeping track of who's winning. Comes down to the final hole like two dudes are in contention for who's going to win the day. Like that's kind of similar to what we do out here. So, um yeah, we like to do that as much as we can. >> Matt, what have you seen from Harrison so far out here? I know he's trying to change things and focus on He said 37 to 50 yards. >> Yeah, we change our practice process a little bit. Um we've been bouncing around specifically for field goal period versus just the traditional start close and finish with the far kicks. Um but, just continuing to learn and continuing to grow, dial in our process. Um yeah, it's been It's been a good camp so far. >> Thanks, Matt. >> All right, who is the best man? >> Uh me and Harrison are are tied right now. James has no wins currently, but >> I'm sure he'll he'll come back strong. He uh sent us a picture he was getting fitted for a putter, so that might help. >> Yeah. Thanks, Matt. >> Yeah, thanks, guys. >> Far away, guys. >> How is it that How is a starting lineman on a team that goes undefeated and wins the national championship somehow fly under the radar? How'd that happen to you? >> Oh, man. Honestly, man, just uh hard work and competition and uh and consistency, bro. And I think that's really one of the biggest thing I took and I didn't let the naysayers really say anything too much and then kept my head down and kept driving forward. >> How much fun is this camp? >> It's been really good, man. I think it's really helpful for all of us. Actually, um everything's been going good. I mean, I I see everything as beneficial, you know what I'm saying, with the team, everything that when it comes to the teammates and they're lifting us up, especially as rookies. Uh you want to be do the best as you can, especially try to keep the coaches how they supposed to be and uh and um really take those coaching points and really keep everything and everything and, you know what I'm saying, moving forward. >> Did you have any conversations with the Chiefs before the draft and what led to your decision to to try out with them? >> Uh honestly, man, I uh I just kind of kept my head down. I knew my time was going to come and really just stay humble and stay faithful and kept praying to God and just making sure that I was ready to be uh called when it was that time. >> What was that draft process like for you? And were there any disappointments at all? >> Uh not honestly, man, cuz like realistically, you I mean, whatever position you get put in, you got to take it on the chin. Uh I mean, being a football player, stuff happens, you know, and uh just being able to just move past one thing and then be able to put the one foot before the other one and keep going and making sure that there's nothing left on the table for you, so you know. >> You know, what were your feelings when you when you got signed and you didn't even get a chance? What what what was that? >> Uh honestly, man, you know, it was good. I mean, I know coming in here, you're going to be having like those type of eyes on you and everything, but being a football player, you know, you're going to you're going to have a lot of fans looking at you and then you got to get used to it and just being able to work and then be able to continue to work and being consistent in what you're doing, I feel like that's the biggest thing. So, it was it was honestly a good thing. So, yeah. >> It was It was really significant to you, obviously, just knowing you had the moment, the opportunity, cuz I guess there could have been a time you doubted you're going to get the opportunity. >> Nah, man, never. I mean, opportunity comes when we all work together, you know what I'm saying? So, as a team, man, we got to put our one foot our best foot forward and then do what we got to do, you know what I'm saying, to keep everything going straight forward. >> You haven't played the game or even a preseason game yet, but when did you feel like, yeah, I kind of I belong here? And was that very early on or was it when you got down here to camp? When did When did it click for >> I mean, uh like I said, like being a football player, it always has to click, you know? Um I think there's been a really offensive lineman as well, too, cuz you got to have it in the back of your mind of whatever quarterback's behind you, you got to make sure that they don't get touched at all. So, as a football player and as a offensive lineman, man, like our mind is always staying on the one goal and make sure the team does the best we can to make sure we get to where we need to go. >> We'll go We'll go Nick and then Pete. >> Julio, for you, what do you take pride in as an offensive lineman that you want to put on tape for the coaches to see? >> Man, um showing the humbleness, man, and the confidence and uh the coaches being able to win uh being able to trust you and uh being able to move forward when there's time to be corrected, being able to be corrected, and then being able to just go out there the next play and then do what you got to do the next play. >> You've been a little outside, inside, you know, these past couple months, I guess. What's been the most challenging part about shifting back and forth? >> Um I don't feel like it's really no challenge. Honestly, I mean, yeah, but you got to you got to be able to adjust when it's time to when your number's being called. You got to be ready to adjust whenever whatever happens, cuz you just never know what could happen. And then any point in time, you just got to be ready to be moved forward and then just have everything ready and your mental ready and then your body ready to go. So, yeah. >> Julio, a lot of these these guys you're playing with played as rookies and a lot played immediately. How has that been maybe helpful to you and your game? >> Uh I I would say, man, like being able to take those coaching points and from them and as well as from your coaches cuz you just never know like cuz anything could happen like I said like being ready and being being able to be ready when your number is called. Those guys that are our vets and everybody here has been making sure that all of us rookies have been on point and been able to have those coaching points when they so when their time comes and their coaches say something that we need to answer to, we know we'll be ready for it. So, honestly, man, I appreciate everything that's been going on here, man. They took us in and, you know what I'm saying, making sure that we're ready for whatever happens. So, it's been really good. >> Thanks, both. >> Thank y'all.

title: Chiefs Training Camp LIVE w/Mitch Holthus and Matt McMullen | AUGUST 12, 2026
text: [music] >> St. Joe today. While it's covering the sun, it's a beautiful day today. Hey, how are you? Nice to see you. The days get long out here in St. Joe. They can get hot. Coach Reid says it every day. He's like, "You just got to show up and push through." I got the last two. Thanks for coming out today, ladies and gentlemen. Until next time. Go Chiefs. >> It is day 20 of training camp here in St. Joseph, Missouri on the campus of Missouri Western State University. And yes, the Rams preseason game is on the horizon Saturday afternoon at Arrowhead, but they're not thinking about that at all here today. It's another day in pads and another day of grinding and another day where we have added to our roster. >> Let's go. >> Mitch Holthus with you voice of the Chiefs along with get this one you're ready this digital of editorial no, director [laughter] >> Try it again. >> of editorial >> I already said it out loud. >> director of editorial content and senior team reporter >> It's a heck of a title. >> And Matt McMullen by the way and the wolf of the west >> Yes. >> Arry Wollf your comparable he is back. >> Your preseason television voice for the Chiefs Kingdom. All right gentlemen, people think okay Rams preseason game None of that is being thought here. There'll be a little bit of a pivot tomorrow for sure on Friday, but this has been a grind Matt been another day in pads. They just keep pushing. >> This is a third pad practice in a row I believe. We had a day off before this stretch started and before that it was four padded practices in a row and it's hot out here. We got lucky a few weeks ago with like 70 degree weather, but it's hot right now. Truly feels like the dog days. I joked around on our last live stream. I have no idea what day of the week it is. I just know we're back at camp but the guys are grinding right now getting through it and like I always say these are the days you find out who your best players are going to be. >> Yep, for sure and who can power through this practice and again a lot of third down work again today and then a wait for it another long drive drill which the guys all love. So Arry, here we are 20 days into this and trying to you start to see some form and substance of a roster put together your observation. >> Well, both I feel like I'm looking from afar and a little bit from the inside now. This is when you build the culture right? This is when you build the toughness. This is when you build the camaraderie all the things that I love about Andy Reid's training camp are the things that build the foundation for the whole season. So, you want it to be hot, you want it to be hard. But at the same time, I'd say coming into this camp, there's more questions than there have been in other years. And that's not necessarily a bad thing, right? Who's going to step up in these preseason games? Who are the guys that maybe we're not going to talk about at either wide receiver offensive line today that next week we are going to be talking about. So, it's the time of year where someone's going to get a chance to make a play and maybe change the course of their entire lives. So, it's for me, that's the exciting part is what guys are going to go out there and make the most of the opportunity cuz yeah, this is the grind part, but showtime is on Saturday. And for a lot of these guys, it may not even be with the Chiefs, but this is their time to get something on film so the rest of the world in the NFL knows that they can play. >> Yeah, your points well taken. The different part of this camp coming off a losing season hadn't happened under coach Reid. Now in his 14th season here, uh the Mahomes injury return, but then also the 2022 draft class. Matt and I have talked, they've now splintered other than George Karlaftis and some guys for free agents, but then we're seeing these rookies start to emerge. We're going to look at two different position groups on this live stream and we're going to start at wide receiver. And to me, you guys, for Saturday afternoon's game, of all the position groups, this to me is the most important for Saturday's game in and of itself. We have got to find some definition and get closer to some decisions. Not just who makes it, but how many to keep. And we're going to go right down the line here with the probably top seven, I would say. And Matt, your thought overall on the wide receiver room? >> Well, I think it's a room that has a lot of talent when it's healthy. We want to see them go out there and and show off that talent though. And notably, Cyrus Allen is a player that I'm excited to watch. Still coming back off that injury. He's been out here. I think he'll play on Saturday, but either way, throughout the preseason, we'd love to see what he can do because before that shin injury last week, I mean, he was the story of camp. Just lighting it up, but that was before the pads came on. Still look good here the last couple days, but would love to see him in a game environment, see what he can do because he's an awesome route runner. One of those players where I talk about how the draft I think is over analyzed a little bit. Doesn't have the fastest 40 time, not the biggest guy, but look at the best receivers in the NFL. It's guys like Jackson Smith-Njigba, Puka Nacua, not big guys, not blazing speed, but they get open and can run routes. I think Cyrus Allen can be that kind of player. >> Kind of a crafty guy, right? Crafty guy. I guess for me it's Andrew Armstrong. He's the guy who during camp, I think he's flashed enough. We're curious, what's he going to look like, right? We're going to get out at Arrowhead, what will he look like out there? But boy, he passes the eye test. I mean, you're down on the field, you look at the guy, you're like, that that guy could play receiver in the National Football League. But I want to I want to see it, but I he he's got a lot of the ingredients, but can he be a guy that is really a part of the rotation? Because I do worry about the health of the top guys. You know, can Xavier Worthy stay healthy? Can Rashee Rice stay on the field? Because if they don't, one of these guys we're talking about at at five, six, or seven are going to have to have a significant role. So I think when you look at the overall wide receiver group, the most important thing to me is depth. If you put all these pieces together, Mitch, and they all have the best year of their career, this room's going to be just fine. But that's that's a big ask. >> Big ask. We talked about that. The ceiling is there, but can they hit that ceiling and do it on a consistent basis? This goes back to Matt, to your point. We're going to circle back to Andrew Armstrong because Matt had a chance to talk to him. But let's talk about the guys that people know about, including Tyquan Thornton. >> my thesis with this group. Um and this goes back to Matt's point. Somebody's got to have catch the third and six slant for eight. Somebody's got to be reliable. So Pat has that trustworthiness. Let me just give you some stats. Davante Adams last year, 85% of his catches were first downs. Now, those weren't all long bombs. Okay? Uh when you look at we talk about the Puka Nacua's, Amon-Ra St. Brown, 22 of his 28 catches on third down were for first down. Even Jamar Chase, you think of as a deep ball guy, 21 of his 28 third down receptions were for first downs. And I think that's the category where can Xavier do a worthy do that? Can Tyquan Thornton do that? And Rashee Rice, can he do that? And Matt, your thoughts on that alone because it to me that's the litmus test. >> Well, I think Rashee was that guy early in his career and before he got hurt, I think he was that guy. Think about that Ravens game in the regular season, the opener in 2024 is basically an extension of the running game. One-on-one against linebackers, it's no contest. We haven't seen him healthy like that in a while, still coming back off the injury last year. Had the cleanup surgery in the offseason, but I think throughout this camp we have seen him get better and better every day, look more comfortable out of his breaks. So hopefully that can continue because we know the kind of player Rashee can be when he's healthy. We've seen it before. I mean, do we win the Super Bowl in 2023 without Rashee? I'm not sure that we do. And he was leading the league in basically every category in 2024 before he got hurt. Now that he's back and and hopefully going to be healthy for this season, let's see what he can do. >> Yeah, I mean, you look at it. He's missed 20 or he's played 28 games of a possible 51 and only 12 of the last and a possible 34 in the last 2 years. You just want to see it over a long period of time. >> Yeah, but his skill set is there to be that guy, right? You can get him the ball on a 2-yard route and he can get you the eight or nine yards for the first down. He's someone who can make guys miss in space and he can run over a guy. Again, he's the guy to me is the most important part of that wide receiver room because if he can be the best version of Rashee Rice, he is your guy on third down. >> And who gets the confidence vote from Patrick Mahomes? And to your point, Cyrus Allen is working to get there. A guy like Jaylen Jaylen Royals, your thought? Two catches, but we saw the 30-yard kickoff return against Baltimore we're going, yeah, that's the guy we saw at Utah State blow it up. Um what about a Jaylen Royals and how he enters this picture? >> Well, I like him a lot. Look, you kind of drink the Kool-Aid. I had like five of his games at Utah State and I was >> why I'm asking. >> And he got the egg in college and he Like against college level competition, he was a total game-changer. Between not only just the speed, but what he could do physically after the catch. Not the biggest guy in the world, but he is physically strong. So, can he emerge as that guy? I think that Thornton to me is sort of he's the X-factor because I don't think that people's expectations are that he can be the the guy that's trusted by Pat. But why not? But that to me is a room that wouldn't shock me if it evolves. It doesn't look exactly the same week one as it does when we get to the end of the year. >> We've not talked at all here about Ika Rimehio because in this discussion where fans and sometimes we're even guilty of speaking parenthetically about special teams. We just throw it in. Hey, 30 seconds left in the segment and you go, [laughter] oh yeah, special teams. No, no, no. This goes to the top of the the first paragraph of this discussion. >> Yeah. >> How many do you keep? Six, seven? If you keep seven, five or six or seven, those guys, Andrew Armstrong, we see Ika Rimehio, the 63-yard kickoff return started the run in the playoffs against Houston. The 41-yard punt return led to a AFC Championship victory over the Buffalo Bills. But with that all in mind, a guy like Andrew Armstrong is exciting because again had nothing promised to him coming into this camp. Uh had to earn every opportunity. Uh a reserve future free agent. All right, down here with Andrew Armstrong. Andrew, it's your first camp with the Chiefs. It's just been been really amazing and fun. >> You've been making plays out here the entire camp. Looking really good. I'm curious though. I'm sure you watched Patrick Mahomes from afar when you were in college and your first year in the league. What's it like catching passes from him? >> Uh I can't even explain like like I said like I said a while ago that that this is this is my favorite team when I was little. Is it your uncle that's from Kansas City or what's the connection? >> Oh, my whole my whole dad's side of the family is from Kansas City. Like my dad, he grew up uh Kansas City, Missouri. Uh his brothers, my aunts, my cousins, my my big brother from here like it's really everybody except my mom's side. It was from Texas but my dad my whole dad's side is from Kansas City, Missouri. >> You're going to have some family at the game on Saturday? >> Oh, yeah, definitely. Definitely going to be there at the game. >> That's awesome. Well, you're making the most of your opportunity out here. I think your story is cool because you began at Texas A&M-Commerce, smaller school. You kind of earned your way to Arkansas. How's that prepared you now for trying to earn a spot on this team? >> Oh, it it's prepared me a lot cuz I know in my life like nothing is ever given. Like everybody's journey is different. So, if I'm looking at somebody else like, "Oh, he he made it in 4 years." Or he made it in 3 years. Like, I can't really um harp on that too much because I know my journey is my journey. So, when I got here, I just, like you said, make the most of my opportunities and just be the best player I can be when I get on the field. >> Good luck on Saturday. >> Thank you. I appreciate it. >> All right, awesome stuff there from Andrew Armstrong. Uh I always think it's cool when a guy like that has family in Kansas City. Like you look at his bio, it doesn't say he's from Kansas City, but you talk to him a little bit. He grew up a Chiefs fan because of all of his family here in the Raytown area or Independence, like right around the stadium. And now he's going to play at Arrowhead. Pretty cool. >> And he said well you know he talked to the media yesterday and he said, "Look, I'm going to have a ton of family here." I mean again, it's the preseason. I get that. But these kind of moments to me resonate. Cuz again, you don't know what the future holds for that guy, but he's going to get to play for his childhood favorite team in Arrowhead with his family there. Cuz you talked about Nico and being stability on special teams. I'll see your stability but raise you to explosiveness. There has to be some explosive plays in special teams. So, he can play in line because he's big enough. All right? That's not going to be Xavier Worthy playing outside the tackle. I think all across the board explosive plays are going to be key and if you can find it in areas where maybe the defense is preparing and you're not thinking about Andrew Armstrong, right? I can promise you that. >> And we can't just crop dust. You've got to find gunners in this room. >> Oh yeah, you do. >> You've got to find flyers in this room. Those are the DBs and the wide receivers. Is that Jalen Royals? Is that Andrew Armstrong? Uh nowadays the reality is some athletes kind of come into the league thinking they've made it already. Uh usually doesn't end well for those guys. Andrew Armstrong is not that guy. Khalen Benton shows up among 70 other tryout players with no guarantee beyond that weekend. 70 of them. Might be a closer to give the baseball analogy, but he's been really good at guard. When you look at Trey Smith being a pro bowler and you look at Creed being Creed and the all-pro center in this league, Suamataia, Kingsley is showing signs he could get to that level and get there very soon. If you're just a stiff big dude bulldozer guy, it's not going to work in this offense. Kingsley's showing us something. >> And he'll play this entire season at 23 years old. >> He's 23. >> So, let's go back to Andrew Armstrong. He's 26. >> Yeah. Yeah. text: Sean, is there any news on Puka? >> Puka's doing good. I mean, he just had a little soreness in his kind of soaz and so we were just being smart with him. Expect him to be back next week ready to go. >> From the uh the take that you guys were able to see against the Cowboys. Were you able to see some explosive plays offensively that you would like to see? >> Yeah, I thought there was some good stuff, you know, like like I talked about the other day. Um, you know, I was more interested in kind of our style of play, not necessarily, you know, testing our rules and different things like that. I thought our guys came out, they were ready to go. I thought there was a physical style of play. I thought there was a toughness illustrated really in all three phases and I thought, you know, I got a lot of respect for the Cowboys. I thought they did a great job and thought it was good to be able to go against somebody else. Some different things that you're seeing schematically on the offensive side of the ball defensively to be able to work punt and punt return versus them and um it was it was a really good day for us in terms of just learning opportunities, growth opportunities, and now we've moved forward. >> Will he play in the >> He will. Yep. He will play. start. >> He will. >> What are you hoping to see? >> I think I think really just, you know, good command by both those guys consistently making good decisions, playing within the timing and rhythm of, you know, whatever that play is that Nate decides to call and, um, want to see us get in and out of the huddle. You know, good communication. There'll be a lot of different guys that'll be kind of rotating in. But, um, you know, I want Stson to be able to do what he's done and I want Tai to be able to do what he's done as well. And it'll be fun to watch both those guys play. >> Nate will be watching. >> Nate will be, yes. No, I'll still be the head coach. [laughter] >> I think unless unless you know something I don't know. >> How do you assess the O line to this point? >> I think they've been good. You know, I I think um to be able to have the continuity that we have is is a real blessing. Obviously, big Rob moving on and he'll be calling the game the color commentary for the game. So, it'll be cool to listen to Rob Havenstein there. Um but what I will say is is I've been pleased with that group. I think Coleman Shelton's leadership in the middle has been outstanding. his command, his ability to see the game in the big picture lens and the rapport that he and Matthew have is really special. Kevin Dodson and Steve Aila have had really good camps as has Warren McClendon and uh and Alec Jackson. I think you know David Quenberry has played really good football as well. And so um I've been really pleased with that group as a whole. I think Ryan Wendell and Brian Allen and Zack Cromer do a great job. And so there's some other guys, you know, I think Bo Li's had a really strong camp as well as Dylan. And I'm looking forward to watching some of those guys compete on uh what is it? Saturday. >> Coach, Coach Ter has had a, you know, a good string of of practices. Yeah. When you look at his growth, what has stood out to you and what excites you? >> I think the consistency of how he's shown up in the production and really all phases, you know, whether that's asking to be used in protection, in the run game, uh, or as a pass receiver, you know, and he can play all over the formation. I think he's a lot more comfortable, even though I thought he got really comfortable with the amount of snaps that he played as the season went on. Um, and he's got a bunch of great guys to be able to learn from and and Scooter Huff, Tyler Higgby, Colby. It'd be great when we get Davis back out there, but uh, but T Ferg's been awesome. Uh, loved what he's done so far. >> This will be the first time that Tai goes against a real rush with tackling. So, you've mentioned getting in and out of the huddle, but are there any other things you're looking to see from him? >> Yeah, I think, you know, really both he and Stson, you know, you could get tackled now. So, there is a difference in that. And so, sometimes if the pocket breaks down, you know, sometimes it might be all right. Hey, the pockets's collapsing. Where's my quick element throw? Sometimes it might be, hey, the pockets collapsing, but there's an escape lane and I can make some plays or second reaction types of plays. And both of those guys, those were things that were parts of their game that we did like coming out of college, whether that be, you know, Georgia for Stson or Alabama with Tai. And so, I think those are some of the different things. And, you know, I I would imagine we'll move the launch point a little bit as well. But um you know I think seeing some of that stuff you know come to life will be will be important but I think it's got to occur you know naturally as you're not predetermined in those types of things and that's where you're just in the moment and you're reacting and playing within your rules and and then just go be instinctual as well. >> What did you see out of your defense against the Cowboys when you went back and watched it? >> Thought great competitiveness. You know I thought our front played nice and tough. They've got a great offensive line. Thought it was great, Nate, for us to see some different schemes than maybe our offense has given our defense. Um, and it was great to be able to talk about some different fits with stuff that they presented, some of the width of their formations and going against premier players like CD Lamb and George Pickkins. Um, but I love the way that they I thought they did a really good job. And then I thought there was some awesome learning things that, you know, I was more interested in how we showed up and then there were some things like, you know, we didn't game plan any of it. And so some of the coverages that we activated or some of the things that they presented, it was like, man, we know that we're going to learn and it was great for us to be able to apply it. We kind of had a walk through to be able to, you know, make some different calls or use some different tools within our coverages. Um, that I thought was awesome that it came up, but I was I was really pleased with just the overall vibe and the feel that I had from those guys out on the grass and then the silent tape showed the same. >> We haven't really asked much about it since first talked to media at the beginning of camp. But what have you seen from the special teams? >> Yeah, he's a stud. Uh, I think, you know, he he's got great energy. He's got great capacity. Um, he he makes those guys feel like he's in it with him. I think he sees the game live really well too. He's able to make corrections in real time and that's really important to me. Um, very smart. You know, he's passionate about teams. I think he gets credibility, too, because he played it at a really high level. I mean, when we introduced him, we showed some highlights. He looked like a kamicazi, the Tasmanian Devil out there doing his thing. So, uh, I love everything he's about, as well as Kyle Hul, and I'm grateful that those guys are here leading the special teams. >> How do you feel like Harrison Beas has approached this camp and try to carry over some of what he did last year? >> He's been great. I mean, he's just so steady, you know, it doesn't seem like anything phases him, which is a great trait to have as a kicker. Um, he's been really good in a lot of the, you know, the the competitive or the different periods that we've done. Had a really good day today when we activated the field goal unit in the middle of practice and, uh, you know, he's he's he's got a nice personality about himself and his demeanor and disposition is what you want from your kicker and, uh, we expect him to pick up where he left off. He did an amazing job for us last year. coach with that receiving group. We know you know Devonte and Fuko guys. What have you seen from some of the other guys so far? >> Yeah, I've seen really good stuff. You know, I think Jay Whit and Kannata Mumfield have done an outstanding job of you know, really asserting themselves. Um I've mentioned to you, you know, Xavier Smith's played a lot of meaningful football for us. And then I think guys like um you know, CJ Daniels and T. Scott have showed up. And so I'm looking forward to watching those guys play. Um you won't see you know Mumfield and and uh Jordan Whittington play in the preseason. Obviously, Puka and Dvonte won't, but it'll be a fun opportunity to watch some of those other guys go play with Stson and uh and Tai. >> Coach, I'm about to do a one-on-one with Byron Young, and I want to get your feel on what you've seen from his growth over the last few years, and you know, having the sacks he had last year. Yeah, this transition should be beautiful. >> Yeah, I think what's been great for by is he's just gotten better every single year. And when you know his backstory, I mean, what an incredible human being. I mean, you want to talk about a guy that's mentally and physically tough. I thought his best practice of camp was against the Cowboys. You know, we've obviously been smart with kind of what his workload looks like. He felt good. I thought he had some good quick wins, being able to counter inside. I thought he was stout against the run. Um, you know, did a really good job with what everything was asked of him the other day and um had another good day today and and just, you know, if you don't love by something's wrong with you. Um he's he's a special human. His story is incredible. Um I love everything he's about. It'll be a fun one-on-one, I'm sure. >> Given the roster continuity and established how many established roles there are on this roster. Does that change the way that um you evaluate the roster compared to years past throughout the preseason or not? >> You know what I I it's every single year is a new year. We've always taken a similar approach and I think the way that you really look at it is is you're not minimizing the importance of what the guys that are playing can get out of this. I think what we have seen is is guys that have played a lot of ball get better throughout the preseason. You know, repetition is the mother of learning. But if you've played meaningful football for us, um that means that we're trying to get you practice reps against us and in in these joint practice settings, whether that's against Dallas or against New Orleans next week, and then we'll have a big scrimmage, you know, that'll kind of serve as their three preseason games. It's going to be really hard to play as a rookie for us. Um you know, and that that's a positive thing, and I think that gives you the chance to be able to be patient. I'm looking forward to all of those rookies. They're all playing in this game and they'll play throughout the whole preseason. And so um it might be different just because we've got so many guys that are returning, but we still have guys that um you know are looking to establish roles for themselves and and everything nothing is set in stone. Just because they don't play means they've got roles carved out, but they earn it out here on the practice field. Um and just because we keep them, you know, away from playing in the preseason doesn't mean that anything's necessarily set. Do >> you have any update on Miles and his knee? >> He's feeling good. You know, I think it's more along al along the lines of getting to know him and once he gets back to that kind of return to performance, Nate, but making really good positive strides as far as when he'll be back, you know, we want to make sure that that's when it's like truly 100%. But like I told you guys the other day, I mean, it's it's pretty impressive if what we've seen when he's been out there is not necessarily 100%. Uh so when we get him to that, I'll be really excited to be able to watch what that looks like. >> Thanks, coach. >> Okay. Thanks, guys. >> How's it going, Stson? >> Good. How are you? >> Good. What has camp been like for you this season? >> Uh it's been fun. It's been uh a lot more playing football. U which I guess I played last year, but it was more with the ones this year and um felt more comfortable with the guys and it it was fun to compete. >> How do you describe your confidence building over the last few years and how you got to this point? You feeling a big difference? >> Yeah, for sure. Um, you know, and I think that just comes with, you know, being better at your job, uh, and having more ownership, uh, knowing the offense more, being closer with the guys. Um, but yeah, I definitely do. >> Do you work on something specific in the offseason to get a little bit better? >> Uh, I did a lot more core workouts. Um, but that was that's probably and yeah.
