But >> what did you see from the practice? >> Uh I thought we started well. I thought we could have done better, at least from me and our group could have done better uh later in the practice. Um but you know, it's always it's training camp and you know, we don't go out there and game plan. There's things to learn. Um and there was there was good things too. Stson, if your number is called at any point this year, how confident are you in in your preparation? >> Yeah, I mean, that's going to go week to week where you're going to come up here, they're going to come up with a game plan. Uh, we're going to practice hard and, uh, you know, I'm going to feel like I'm going to be able to give my best out there for the guys. >> You've been, you know, a couple years around Matt. What are some things that you've been able to to learn from him to develop yourself as a quarterback? >> Just his He's steady, right? He's not too high with the highs, not too low with the lows. um day in and day out he comes and uh uh you know does what he can do for the Rams organization and I think that >> How's the O line looking right now? And you know you lost a key guy but uh pretty steady overall, right? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean they I love I I'm I'm always partial to O linemen, you know, cuz you know they're they protect me and you know um but yeah, our guys are out there working every day and they're crushing it right now. Do you feel any different at all though? Is there a different chemistry to what's going on right now on that O line? You feel? >> There are some new faces, especially with the twos right now that I'm I'm thinking of. Um, you know, people are uh there's not so many of the guys that uh I came in with um are out there. You know, we got some new guys and but I I feel like we're we're all jelling and and getting together nicely. getting >> um I guess patience. Um trying to just do the best that I can for me, for the organization. Um and just taking a step forward every single day. uh you know, you're not going to solve all the world's problems today and it won't be tomorrow and it probably won't be you know for a long time and you know and uh just keep stacking days, keep getting better and trusting that one day it'll you know be better. So that's it. >> From playing so much college ball only getting to play games in August the last couple years. How's that been for you as a player? What what does it mean to get to this next level where you're going to play this year but there's also a good chance to play your season? It's definitely tough. You know, we get into this because a we love football and b we love to compete. And so, uh, it definitely was tough just, you know, watching out there. Um, and not really doing anything practice, not really doing anything on Sundays. I almost said Saturdays cuz I'm still, you know, those are my game, you know, but, um, you know, not doing not doing anything, right? Again, we we love to compete. So yeah, it has been a test of patience, a test of willpower and um but you know, Rags is it would have been tough to get through it without, you know, a coach that, you know, grabs me, you know, and takes me around the practice field and, you know, takes me through the script before, after we watch, you know, the little things that you can do when you're not on the practice field to get better. Um, you know, so >> your whole story has been about show me, right, almost since the beginning and you have. So, how much does that carry over into right now where you are in your career? It's like, okay, I still got lots to show, >> right? I um I don't know. I I just want to go out there and be the best that I can be. And if I'm not that, then that drive that irks me to no end, you know, kind of gets after me. Um and then if I am going out there and playing good ball, then that's enough for me. It's not really about the outward, you know, wow, that guy's doing good, you know, because if you rise up here with that, then you'll fall down here when they they're they're killing you. And so, um, really it's it's, you know, who's the man in the mirror, how are we doing today, and how are we going to do tomorrow? >> Stson, you you talked about the transition from playing on Saturday to now just, you know, watching, observing. How has you perceived the game evolved? Um, well, I think I've It's a different game than college. Um, but I don't know. I feel like the more you play, um, you got to play football to get better at football, right? So, the more you play, I wouldn't say the easier it gets, but the more familiar you get with the speed of it, with the, uh, complexity of it, um, all that stuff. So, I I think it's just, you know, a little bit better understanding of it. And it's hard to put that into words, but, you know, when you're out there on the on the field, it's a little bit better. Stson, we've seen your connection with CJ Daniels in that second team unit throughout training camp. What have you seen from him behind? >> I've seen a lot a guy who loves to show up, loves football, um shows up to work every single day and and and wants to go out there and, you know, cook whoever's on top of him. But, you know, he just he loves football and he's going to catch the ball when it's in the air and uh he he runs great routes. He's a willing blocker. Uh you know, he he studies offense. He's he's been great. You mentioned those conversations you've had with rags, you know, before and after practice. What's the value of having those now with uh you know, being able to incorporate the reps and and you know, the experience that you've gotten especially in this training camp? >> Yeah, I think it all compounds right over time. Um it's hard to point to any one thing that's like, oh, that was, you know, it's it's it's time on task. It's, you know, repetition is the mother of learning. It's everything that is just, you know, um and we're not there yet, right? We're not there yet. and we got to keep that in mind. But it's it's just doing what you think is the best thing that you should do at that moment and then just keep following that and hopefully getting better over time. >> Stson, you Stson, you said that CJ uh loves football. You often hear that phrase a lot. This person is a football player. This person loves football. What does that actually mean? >> I think it probably means different things for different people. Um but I can just I just see it in his eyes. Uh he's a he's a steady guy. He's not riding the wave. He goes out there. Um he takes he takes his craft seriously and uh whenever we do something good, you know, he he's fired up about it. When we do something bad, he's not he's pissed off. >> You either have passion or you don't. Right. >> Right. >> You've had the opportunity to start preseason games last couple years. As you go into this one, what did what did you learn from those experiences? And what if anything is different going into this one? >> Um I don't know. Um, I'm looking forward to it. Uh, going out there and competing. Um, uh, I'm excited to see Arrowhead. Uh, you know, that's a cool stadium. But, uh, I don't know. I mean, it's it's always good to, like I said, it's you got to play football to get better at football. Um, but I'm just looking forward to going out and executing offense with the guys. >> Thanks, man. >> What's up, Eric? How's everybody doing? >> Great. >> It's great. Um, blessed to be in LA, blessed to be with a great group of guys, um, top from bottom. Uh, learning every day, just trying to be, you know, the best version of myself. >> When we've seen you out there on the practice field in training camp, it feels like there's been more conviction and confidence in what you're seeing on the field and just the throws you're making. I guess is that something you would agree with? And, I guess, how do you feel about like where you are now versus where you were when you got here in the spring? >> Uh, yeah, I definitely feel like I've gotten a lot better since I've been here. um from the familiarity of the you know the offense um the relationships um the guys in general um and you know I'm really not looking for perfection just looking for progress so you know every day I just try to make sure that I'm the you know be better than I last was um and I'm going to mess up eventually I'm a rookie um and just understand that you know hey you know don't let it happen again right learn from it and move on >> Ty what are some things that you've kind of been able to you know learn from Matthew >> yeah uh to you know just be yourself right like uh you know one of the best things that really stuck with me is you know don't try to be somebody else. Um you know just do it your way. Uh and a lot of the times you know people get caught up in the in the mess [clears throat] of you know trying to do do like somebody else trying to be like you know whoever. Um but you know it's just more about just finding who you are and how things work and how you tick. >> Ty while you guys were at LMU after practice I'd often times see you staying after getting in some additional work. what what's motivating you to do that and and why do it? >> Uh yeah, you know, one I'm not getting as many of the reps um as uh you know, Stson and Matthew, so I want to make sure that I get, you know, those throws in that they got on the field. Um and just, you know, to be conditioned to be ready. Uh you know, it's something that I want to make sure that, you know, I I do. Um and not get caught up in just, you know, sitting around and and not being locked in. Um I want to be locked in me mentally and locked in physically as well. So getting those after practice with rags and just working on my body is uh you know something that will help me in the long run. >> Given that you haven't gotten a ton of reps, what's your excitement level for Saturday to go out there and play in a game setting? What are you hoping to show? >> Yeah, you know, I'm super excited. It's first time I get to, you know, play a game in a not only a Rams uniform, but an NFL uniform. Um and, you know, I'm just really ready to show just who I am. Um I'm not going to do, you know, anything that I know I'm not capable of doing. Um I'm just going to stick to my rules and stick to what I've been doing. um throwing with conviction uh and just you know having fun out there just football um just on a whole different level uh and I'm excited. >> Talked about what it's like walking field. What have you learned in that? >> Yeah. Uh you know I've learned so much ball from the cans um to the criterias that we have um to you know how the NFL defenses tick um how people call it and just how the offense works in general. You know him rags and Shawn have a you know great relationship. but they go back to another days with, you know, uh, in Washington. And so just, you know, trying to take nuggets from him and Matthew each day because not only the cool thing about, you know, Rags is not only did, you know, is he a quarterback coach, but he played the position. So he understands, you know, how hard it is, understands how, um, you know, the difficulty of the position, how much is asked. Um, so, you know, getting his point of view is uh, is very similar to ours. Kai Stson mentioned the word speed when it comes to the speed of the game, especially when you're a rookie. How much can you learn from that in practice as opposed to I I need game reps for this? >> Yeah, you know, certainly it's a it's a huge difference, right? Um just from the uh you know, college to the NFL. Um and then, you know, practice to a game, right? Like you don't get hit during practice. Um and so, you know, it's going to be a whole different lifestyle just you know, making making people miss, trying to make sure you get the ball out quick, right? those dudes are, you know, humming off the edges. Um, you know, I I remember when I was coming out talking to Bryce and Jaylen and other guys who I know who, you know, are starters in the league and, uh, and they were saying that, you know, one of the big things was the was the third down and was the, you know, guys off the edge. So, you know, it'll be it'll be fun this weekend to, you know, get my cleats on the ground, see how it is. Um, you know, there's going to be things that I mess up on. Uh, I just going to, you know, learn from them and move on and, you know, next week be able to learn from it and, uh, make sure it doesn't happen again. Ty, when you walk into the locker room and you see your game jersey for the first time, you put it on, you're getting ready to run out onto the field, even though it's a preseason game, what what do you anticipate your emotions being? >> Yeah. Um, it'll be a surreal moment for sure. Uh, not only, um, you know, one, playing in the NFL, um, but two, you know, playing for a great organization, uh, like the Rams that has the pedigree that it's had, you know, not only with quarterbacks, but championships and Hall of Fame players in general. Um, you know, so it's just it's going to be super fun. You know, I was talking to my parents last night just about, you know, how cool it was. Thinking, um, you know, my brother starting high school football, uh, and thinking about, you know, I guess it would have been what, eight years ago, I was, you know, in that similar situation, you know, being a freshman and, um, coming in and and trying to earn a spot. Um, same thing now, just, you know, a rookie. So, it it'll be cool. Um, and I'm excited to get, you know, after it. >> After you watched the film from the Cowboys scrimmage, what did you kind of learn? >> Sorry, can you repeat? Yeah. After you watched the film from the Cowboys scrimmage, what did you kind of see about yourself or kind of learn? >> Yeah. Um, you know, one, I got a lot to learn for sure. Um, you know, just how things operated. Uh, you know, how Matthew does it. Um, but, you know, uh, just how, you know, things take in general, right? Like, you know, it was different, you know, going against the same defense every day and then going against a good defense like the Cowboys of just, you know, different scheme, different calls, different uh, personnel. Um, just making sure that I stick to my rules and stick to playing quarterback, right? Like you getting the ball out quick, making sure that I know what my problems are. Um, and just, you know, making sure that I get us in bad situations. >> Sean and Nate have talked about the importance, especially for you getting a play call, getting everyone lined up. How difficult, if at all, has that been with their play calls and kind of going through that? >> Yeah, it's been very difficult. Um, I say that, you know, I I feel like Alabama prepared me a lot for it. Um, one of the reasons of why I think I was, you know, very attractive to this organization, um, because we did huddle, we did do the the can criteras and the checks at the line of scrimmage, um, is just new terminology. Um, and, you know, just making sure that I get the repetition of of, you know, just hearing it, uh, repeating it and then understanding, you know, what is the problems and what is the criteria for us to check the play. Um, it's just something that, you know, I have to do on, you know, my personal time to make sure that I'm ready. So, you know, for this weekend, right, of just understanding what's up and what's understanding what's the uh what the problem is and you know, why we're checking the play um and just making sure that we get our offense in the best situation that we can. >> When it comes to the mental idea of like, hey, I'm not getting the reps right now, how do you keep yourself focused and steady? >> Yeah. Um, you know, one, I think it goes all the way back to college, um, in a similar situation. um think back to the you know the South Florida game where I you know was was not as ready as I probably should have been um and uh you know I the team suffered for it um and I look back on it it's something that you know I had learned um and told myself I wasn't going to do that again of you know I always going to be prepared always going to be ready um and you know in this situation right it's very very similar um you know may not be out there physically but I'm you know sure as heck going to be ready mentally of just you know understanding of you know even though you know Matthew's play calls are different than um you know the twos group, right? Always understanding what the ones groups is doing and why they're doing it. Um and just you know doing it on my own time, right? Like uh you know everybody can just come to practice and then go home and do whatever they want, but this is a full-time job. Not only that, but especially playing quarterback at the, you know, highest level. >> Now, you talked about making mistakes, you talked about making mistakes, [music] too, whether it be learning from them or whatever that means and similar with the USF game. Is that something that you kind of instilled in yourself or is that something that coaches are also kind of considering? >> Yeah. Um you know I think it was something that I instilled in myself of just um you know things that I have done uh but also you know coaches along the way of just you know hey this is a great learning go you know Sean says it all the time you know learning opportunities um you know repetition is the you know big biggest measure measurement of growth um and you know just understanding that you know hey this is you know this is it right like this is you know making sure that you're uh you know you're ready to go just you know not making the same you know mistakes over again um and just you know always always being ready. >> You had mentioned staff and advis the best advice that you've gotten as a big opportunity since you come here. >> Yeah. Um the best advice I mean I've gotten so much advice from you know so many different guys in here because it's such a good group. Um you know I I I probably bother Matthew a lot um in a type of way to where he probably thinks I'm annoying. Um, you know, sometimes I'm like, "All right, maybe maybe that's the one for tomorrow." Um, but no, we actually talked this morning. Um, and he he asked me like, you know, "Hey, how do you feel about the game and stuff?" And I just, you know, told him I was excited and told him, um, you know, it's a great opportunity. I'm ready to play. Um, and he just, you know, the best advice that he gave me was just, man, you know, go go let it rip, right? Like it's nothing that you haven't done before. Um, it's just, you know, playing out there with rules, uh, you know, rules, you know, see the play clock, understand, you know, what your problems are and just let it rip, man. Um, so, you know, I appreciate everything that Matthew has done for me. Um, and Stson as well. Like, those guys have been nothing but, you know, great role models for me, great mentors in the quarterback for me. Um, and, uh, not only, you know, are we going to get better, but it's it's just, you know, a growth moment to where we can all come together and, uh, you know, help the team. >> Thank you guys.

title: TE Greg Dulcich meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: How did it feel to be back out there this this past weekend? I got a little dinged up last >> Yeah, no, it was great. Great to be out there with the boys. I mean, what's better? >> How did it feel going up against the Commanders today? Finally get to see what this new look offense and your team looks like against the >> Yeah, yeah, it's refreshing to get to hit someone else. I think everyone was excited about that. Um yeah, the boys look good. Um you know, we went out there, tried to grind, and yeah, a lot of good stuff. >> What's been your impressions of Malik Willis today? We got to see him scramble a little bit more than we I think we do back in Miami. What is that >> Yeah. Yeah, he's he's a guy that can do it all. And when you have someone with, you know, that multi-faceted of a game, it's huge for us offensively. And it's it's going to be tough for, you know, whoever we play. >> What have you observed about the guy we just spoke to, the Caleb Dunlap? >> Oh, stud. Yeah, he's making plays left and right. It's awesome. You guys saw it in two minute there. Yeah, he's showing up all over the field. So, we're we're stoked to have him, for sure. >> How's good? >> Where are you from the injury standpoint? Did the hand set you back? >> I'm practicing. I'm full go practicing. Yeah, I feel good. We have an awesome training staff, great doctors, you know, took care of me. We were, you know, real quick with things. And yeah, I'm happy how everything's going. Doing great. >> What's it like when last year you obviously get brought in, I believe mid-year, if I'm not mistaken. But to be seen as so from the outside as someone who's like leading this tight end group this year, what changes for you? >> It's cool. Yeah, it's it's an awesome It's an awesome feeling getting to be one of the older guys, kind of help set the standard with Cole. You know, he's he's been doing a great job this this entire training camp. And you know, Ben as well. And yeah, I got three rookies and they're all, you know, they're all responding. They're all making plays. So, we're very excited about the group we got.

title: ILB Jordyn Brooks meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: JB, how do you feel you guys did today? >> I thought it was a good day. Um, it's kind of hard to really assess everything without watching the film yet, but just the feeling off just coming off the field, I feel like it was a good day. Some things we definitely got to clean up, but um that's what we expect uh day one of joint practice. So, >> the overall feeling was good. >> What about the physicality? >> I thought we brought that. Um, that was the main thing that, you know, have really wanted us to come in with uh physical mindset. Obviously, we're not tackling, but thing up, stopping the ball carrier in the hole, uh being sound on the run game, that was the biggest uh emphasis, and I thought we came out doing that early. >> For a second straight year, you guys are going to have a few few rookies on the defense. Um how do you think they handled today communicationwise and just meeting the moment of seeing a new team for the first time? >> I thought they handled it good, man. They We got some smart rookies. Um these guys know their playbook. They know football. Um, I think for them they just got to get used to everything around, you know what I mean? The NFL, uh, going up against different players for the first time. Uh, but the communication, all that was, it was pretty good. >> Certainly helped to see Michael Taff make the play in the back of the end zone to save that late situational drive. Uh, what' you think of of seeing him make that play? >> Uh, it it was great. I mean, Taff has been great all camp. Uh, really really smart rookie. Really smart. Um, knows exactly what he's doing. um always in the right place and so I wasn't surprised him making that play to be honest with you. So it was good to see him make that play for us and um you know finish practice on a great note. >> You knew who Jacob Rodriguez was coming in but what do you think of the camp he's having and how he's putting it together? >> He's been great man. Another smart rookie. Um playing Mike, you got to be smart. Um I think he's been ascending each practice, getting better and better, getting more and more comfortable. Um, and he's also taking some leadership, you know, controlling and and um, and taking control of his huddle. Um, and that's the biggest thing I've been seeing from him lately. And so I'm excited to see his growth. >> Time for a few more guys. >> Obviously the secondary a little bit decimated by by a lot of injuries. Uh, could you just break down getting some new guys in there, uh, getting different guys looks at this point against a new, uh, opponent in front of you? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, NFL, it's always some somebody that's going to go down, so it's always got to be the next man up. Um, I think right now we got a lot of young guys, a lot of guys who maybe not haven't been proven or established in the league yet. And so competition is great. Uh, and so I think that group is doing great. You know what I mean? A lot of guys rotating right now. And so we'll see how it all ends up at the inner camp.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: off with 7-on-7 red zone, and then I think we're going to a team red zone. Then there's a bunch of team periods, a move the ball period. And then we're finishing up with a 2-minute really on the plus side of the field. I think it's going to be like on the plus 25. Um but talked to coach Quinn. I have a ton of respect for him. I've really looked up to him as a defensive coach becoming a head coach for a long time. Uh so it's actually cool to have those conversations with him. Um but just kind of let them take the lead and you know, I asked for a few things and and and they were great. You know, I know Adam Peters well. I worked with him in San Francisco. Have a ton of respect for him. Not only what he's done in his position, but just as a person. Great great guy. Great family. So it'll be fun to see him today, too. >> Coach, um in terms of >> I can hear you. >> Yeah. >> I mean, we're good. >> the physicality. We know joint practices sometimes get a little chippy. Are there rules the players have been given about fisticuffs and stuff and and aggressiveness? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's the same as what our players have answered from you when you guys have asked them those questions. I mean, we don't have time for that. We're here to practice. They're here to practice. The other thing is I have so much respect for everybody that plays this game, whether they're on our team or another team. I mean, this is their livelihood that we got to protect them, too. There should be no blind shots. There should be Is there going to be a scuffle or two? I mean, it happens. Should there be a punch thrown? No. If there's a punch thrown, they're out. And that's what I told the team. It's exactly what I've told the team throughout camp. And we've been we've been fortunate. There haven't been a lot of fights. We don't have time for that. So if there is, hopefully it gets broken up and we continue to practice, which is the main thing. And it's really really important and I told our team is I want to come out of this healthy, and I want Washington to come out of this healthy. I have Like I said, I have too much respect for all of these players to think anything differently. At the same time, I want to be physical. I mean, that's how we need to play, and I'll be disappointed if we're not. >> Coach, when when Sully comes down and tells you that you guys are on boarding somebody new, whether that's trade with Kaden Wallace or free agency, what's the process with you and your staff to kind of onboard them? You guys Is there a film session? Do you talk with Solly and the scouting staff? How do you get ready to bring somebody new into the fray this point of year? >> Sure, there I mean there's a lot of conversation, right? So, it's not like all of a sudden he comes in and he says, "Hey, we just made a trade." So, we're kind of he keeps us in the loop, which is awesome cuz our communication is outstanding and I think he's done an unbelievable job with myself, with the staff. Uh so, there's communication and then, you know, right before the trade is about to break, we know it and we tell the staff. As far as onboarding goes, I just met him in the hotel last night before dinner. So, it's not like It's like, "Hey, how you doing? We're going to get you caught up as soon as possible." Um there hasn't been a lot of that in this situation. Everyone's a little bit different, but then there's going to be a time on how we do things, the expectation, what the culture is all about, the rules, cuz just like in any other company, when you bring somebody new in, you want to kind of, you know, have that orientation of what it's going to be like here. So, that is very, very important. It's a good question. >> Jeff, from a a football skills standpoint, what did you guys see and like about Kaden Wallace that made you guys want to trade for him? >> Yeah, we had obviously Solly and um you know, a bunch of our guys were high on him coming out in the draft. And talking to our O-line coaches, it was the same thing. I mean, you know, I talked to Zach and and those guys and he really liked him coming out. Had a high draft grade on him. He had a big smile on his face when I told him the news. Um the versatility, the ability to play guard and tackle, which you know, we need some depth right now. We need competition for those spots right now and I think he brings both and you know, I think in our league, often times, you know, a change of scenery, a fresh start is helpful. And with the talent that he has and the versatility that he has, you know, we're hoping that a fresh start will help him and and he'll come in and compete. >> I noticed Zach Sieler wasn't participating at Monday drills. What's his status? Will he be back today? >> Zack Zack will be out today. Unfortunately, he won't be able to practice. And that I would say that would be week to week. >> And Josh Uche, we saw he at some point in practice he stopped he was running on the side. Where is he? >> He's good. He'll be out here full go today. >> Hey coach, what's up? I had a question for you about how joint practices might disrupt your typical installs. Is this going to be a continuation of what camp has been so far or do you kind of step back and try to see where you're at? Like what does today today look like in terms of where you are in the progression of this camp? >> Yeah, the installs are kind of starting to taper off. What what's happening right now in camp? Now you're getting into more situational work. Whether it's short yardage, goal line, backed up, certain situations at the end of the game, last play of the game, play before last play of the game, things that might come up at the end of game situations. There's some stuff that we kind of want to tinker with. I mean, just speaking from a defensive standpoint, there's still a bunch of pressure packages and thoughts that I have, but we've kind of put that on hold. So, there's no new install for today. Here's what's really important for me today, too. Today, at least for me, speaking defensively, this isn't I want to try to out-scheme Washington today. I don't want to try to send all these blitzes so we get a free runner. Like the stuff that's really important for me today is to see who can get off blocks, who can cover somebody, who can play base football with really good fundamental and technique so we can evaluate and see where we're at. I mean, if we scheme up a blitz and we got a guy coming through off the edge, it doesn't I don't know what that does for us as far as evaluation goes. So, it's going to be more base defense, base offense. Let's play with fundamentals and technique. Let the guys calm down and then see what we got. That's a good question. >> Um, we saw the first depth chart, saw Caleb Douglas up there. What has he done as a rookie that separated himself and allowed him to be in that spot? >> I I It goes back to what I've been talking you guys about. It's been consistency over time. He's been He's been really consistent. He's made, you know, he's made some flash plays and then he's made some plays where, you know, he needs to catch the ball. But he's just He's probably been one of our most consistent guys. And he's showed up every day. So, that's where he deserves to be at this point. As far as the depth chart goes, I mean, it's not like when I sit there and I'm watching film, I'm going he should be here, he should be here. It's a start. Okay? And I told the team the same exact thing. Cuz I just I want to be transparent with them. I want to be transparent with you. If anybody's going to get worked up about where they are in the depth chart right now, hey, come and talk to me cuz I could probably explain to you and and let's worry about that 3 weeks from now. >> I'm not as fired by the depth chart, but I'll just ask you about >> You're you're You're a big depth chart guy. Got it. >> Trey just Trey Moore. Just want to hear about Trey >> We got him labeled now as a depth chart guy. I'm just joking. >> Uh just want to hear about Trey Moore's camp so far and what you've seen from him. >> Consistency, versatility. Um He's done a really good job setting the edge. He can play inside of linebacker. He can play outside linebacker at Sam. And then he's got the ability to rush. So, he gives you a linebacker who can play all three downs. Um he can play in zones. He's good against the run. And he's got rush value to him. So, we'll see where he's at, but I like the way he's I like the way he's practiced. >> In the name of versatility with linebackers, uh earlier this offseason you mentioned the ability to play in space is premium ability >> Huge. >> Has that always been a core belief of yours or is that kind of a reflection of more athletic quarterbacks and kind of the way that offenses have have evolved since you first come into the league? >> It's the way offenses are making you defend the entire field. Um Look, in man coverage it's different, right? In man coverage, if I'm a linebacker and you're a running back, I can go match up with you right now. The way teams are spreading out and forcing you to play certain zones, if I'm 10 yards away from you and H-back catches the ball in space and I'm not good at playing in space, it's going to be a very hard down for me. So, the more you can get guys who can shrink the field with speed, with length, the ability to adjust laterally, right? So, all of a sudden we're playing in space, you go this way, I got to be able to adjust laterally, make that play. It's become really, really important at the position. Um and just the overall speed of the game with the wide outs, the running backs, the tight ends, it's there's a lot of athletes on the field right now. So, we need guys who can do that on defense as well. >> Jeff, we all we all know things can change, but at the moment, are you planning to get Malik Willis some action in the preseason game? >> I am. Yeah. And but like you said, things can change. >> What what what what do you like about getting some of the veterans time in the preseason? >> We're young. So, like when you say veterans, how many guys that we have that have been through this year after year? It's just not who we are as a team right now. I talked to the staff about that this morning and in a perfect world in these joint practices, you get your so-called 22 starters 30 to 35 reps, you give them tomorrow walk-through, and then they don't really play very much. But as you go through our team right now, there aren't many of those guys. So, we have to gain experience. So, we will carefully look, and I'm telling you this like exactly like I told the staff, we got to see how many reps those guys played today. How many reps do our starting O-line get today? Our so-called starting offensive line played today. Then what do we feel comfortable with them playing in the game? So, if a guy gets 30, 35 snaps, are we okay with them getting 10 snaps Friday night? Those are questions that we have to have today. If a guy gets 20, he's going to play more. but I want guys I want our team, which is new and young, and we brought in a bunch of as you know free agents, we've got to go like this. So, we need to experience practice together, we need to experience going into a game together, being in the locker room, coming out together, the kickoff, everything that goes into We got to play football. So, everybody should expect to play and unless something changes like you gave me the ability to keep true to my word now. We'll do that. >> What did you like in Nick McCloud in order to pick him up? >> Say it again. >> Nick McCloud, what do you like about him? >> Just gives us some more depth, which is what we need. you know, what watched I I'm going to be honest with you, didn't watch a whole lot of film cuz I didn't have time, but but just like what we saw, it gives us depth and excited to see what he can do. It's going to be, you know, not as much um some of the periods that we get into, some of the stuff that he really doesn't know right now will be a little harder, but some of the individual the one-on-ones and some of that stuff will be good. >> I want to ask you this question about the nickel cornerback. I love how you detail his responsibilities, responsibilities, roles, what you're looking for from positions. Nickel is one of those hard positions to play and learn. What do you need and what do you want to see from from your nickel? >> Oh, that's a question we could talk a long time about. I mean, if you're talking early downs, first and 10, second one to six, um you're talking about a guy who's got to be able to play the run. I mean, you're talking about now having a guy you trust to possibly cover a slot receiver, but at the same time, the way offenses are going to motion you and get you into the box, you could potentially be a B gap or an A gap defender if we don't protect him. So, that guy's got to be physical and he's got to be able to tackle. The ability to play in space. So, now So, think about it like this. You're describing a linebacker, which is really what I'm doing. I'm describing a linebacker who has to have the physicality to play the run, tackle, but then you're also going to ask that guy to do some stuff that the corners are doing, right? Are we going to play man in those situations? Are we going to play zone? Do we have a guy that can blitz? Cuz if you have a nickel that can do all those things, those guys are hard to find. Can that same guy be the same nickel on second seven plus, third and five plus, where now you got to play more man, right? You got to match up against some of these good slots or, you know, some of the outside wide receivers. So, that's a that's a lot I just described. Um in a perfect world you have one. Um, in a not so perfect world, which most teams are in, you have an early down nickel, you have a third down nickel, and you have different packages so you can get all those things done. The problem becomes is if this guy is in the game, are they really going to play man with him? If this guy is in the game, are they really going to want him in the box? So, it's a cat and mouse game. But, probably one of the most underrated positions and valued in our league. Um, it's a lot it's a fun position coach. >> Last question. >> We can go two more. >> Go ahead. Go ahead. Go ahead. >> You have a coach on your staff who played most of his career here, Liddell Betts. Um, what what made him someone you wanted to pick up on your staff this off season? >> Yeah. Um, I had a lot of coaches call on his behalf. And I didn't know Liddell. I was interviewing running back coaches, a lot of coaches called about him. Um, both college coaches, NFL coaches, and spoke to the world of him as a person, as a coach. And then just in the interview process, um, I really I liked him and I felt like he was the right guy. He's got this quiet demeanor about him. Um, he has the ability to connect with these players, relationship with A-Chan. He has the ability to be hard on the players in his own way. And he played the position. And I think certain times if you can get a guy to do all those things and he's played the position, it can be a benefit. Um, and I'm really glad he's with us. >> You've known Malik for a little bit now, but the past two months, uh, six months, whatever it's been, you guys have both had new roles. What's impressed you the most about Malik, not just over the months, but the past couple weeks that maybe has surprised you even? >> I don't know if anything's a surprise cuz I I know Malik pretty well, you know, I spent a lot of time with him in my two years with him in Green Bay. The thing that I'm most proud is in the last two weeks, and really in the last week, the leadership. Um a lot of conversations with Malik early on. You know, I I think it's important that Malik gets comfortable playing the position. It's like his rookie year. And a lot of times, I think if you try to be the leader and you try to be too vocal and you try to focus on your position and all that you're learning and all the pressure and stress that goes into being a quarterback, I think that's a hard thing to do. Um so, he's kind of been quiet playing his role, playing football. I I saw more more leadership this week, not just with you know, the wide receivers, but the whole offense. Um and I think that's a really big step and I'm really proud of him for that. Thank you guys for coming. >> Yeah, see you.

title: Head Coach DeMeco Ryans on Texans Preseason Opener
text: Good evening. >> Good evening. [laughter] >> Hey, what did you think about some of your rookies that got their first action tonight? >> And for our rookies, I think a few guys had really good outings just from being there on the sideline watching it. Starting first off with Marlon Klein. Thought he really shined today. Everybody saw the pass that he caught. It's where I see him where he can excel uh for our offense and just open the offense up for us. Just his his catch radius is just it's tough to guard him, right? and he definitely has the speed as well to run away from guys. So, he stood out for to me not only just to catch him, but watching him in line blocking in the running game. I saw him finishing some blocks there exactly how we wanted done. So, a ton of positives there for him. Anytime you take the football away, I think Kamari Ramsey did a good job of getting an interception there. Should have had a few more that we uh let go through our hands, but you know, I thought the backs ran well. Noah Whittington did a good job of running the football. uh Lewis Bond getting him back, doing some punt returning. I thought that was a lot of positives there for him. Uh something we can definitely continue to work more and he can improve on. So, uh just starting as we started the game with our first first unit, our offensive uh line thought they did a really nice job that first drive just having a positive drive, driving down and getting the score. Jared Wayne showed up making a lot of good plays. Davis made some good decisions there. So overall it was some it was some positive things there early on but just collectively it's not our style of play and uh so a lot for us to improve upon I got two two for you that starting off line was that more so about getting continuity between them >> as opposed >> uh you starting the entire >> Yeah we want yeah they needed to go out and play together and they did a really nice job what we gave them we gave them uh 10 to reps and those guys did a good job with those reps. >> You touched on Marlon Klein. Was that what y'all expected from him when you when you drafted him in April? >> Yeah, we expect that. And even he has more as well. I think this is just a start of Marlon Klein as he continues to grow and learn how we're doing things. Like he's a really good athlete, right? And he's strong and physical at the line of scrimmage. So that's what we saw from the Michigan tape and that's what he's been showing all training camp. Coach, did you get an opportunity to see uh Kate McDonald occupy the space that you that you wanted him to? >> I have to look at the film to see see it up close and see how he did. But overall, you know, I thought he we got him some good valuable reps. He needs to get as many reps as possible, right? To continue to improve his game and improve, you know, our style of play. >> I don't really coach, but do you have an update on Graham Mer and what happened on the play >> for the update on Mertz? you know, he was running there towards the the opponent's sideline and, you know, unfortunately non-cont and I think he'll be we're evaluating him. We right now is looking at a a knee injury ACL. So, we'll see get that update to see what happens. Anything else, >> coach? Taking everything in consideration without without knowing going back looking at the film, was besid guys that you just named, but a few other things that sort of stood out with you that you sort of just make muscle memory on when you want to go back and look at the film to see how they turned out in the course of the game. >> I really want to go back and really dive into the film to really get a a great evaluation of all the guys we had. But I like we had a lot of different guys playing tonight. So we rolled a lot of guys in. A lot of guys got valuable playing time. So for me I have to really go and watch it to you know see who I can single out from them doing a really good job. So um overall again it was it was some positive things but anytime you I tell our guys anytime you suit up and you're competing you want to win the football game. No matter who's out there you want to compete to win. So it didn't go our way but it's still a lot for us to learn and grow from. Dom, you talked about I asked you before what you wanted to see and you said you wanted to see the team play Texan style of play. When you say that, you're talking about the aggressiveness. Can you What part of that would you like? >> Castella played that. I wanted to see I wanted to see us play physical, right? And I did not see that the entire game. There were some glimpses of us playing physical, but the Chargers, they out physical to us the the the entire game, right? So, it was not our brand of football. When I speak of playing our style, that's a physical brand of football. And that was not up to par tonight. Coach, how valuable is it to have Davis Mill on your team? You know, having a guy who's a backup, but then when you call him in, especially after an injury, you know, he comes in and just poised throughout this game. How valuable is he to the team? >> Yeah, the backup quarterback is uh true very valuable position and Davis has done a good job of just always being ready. Whenever his number is called, he's ready to step up and not just step up and just to be out there, he's out there and he can make positive plays for us. as we saw him do right through this this past season when we were able to get on a winning streak there. Davis was the guy who sparked that. So, um he's very valuable to have around. We're happy to have him. >> One of the things >> one of the things that's overlooked in your defense is the way that how physical your quarterbacks are as far as attacking in the run game. Um tonight, we we got an opportunity to see some of those guys come down and stop, especially one of the hits I think that Jaylen Smith made. How important is that to have those type of um cornerbacks to be able to be physical like that? >> For us defensively, you have to be able to set the edge. And it's not just defensive ends who set the edge. Our corners are going to get challenged a lot because our defensive end are getting a lot of attention right from opposing offenses. So when that ball pops on the outside, corners have to step up and be physical and you have to tackle in this defense because you're going to get a ton of opportunities. probably different than other schemes, but in our scheme, corners are going to get challenged as tackling and also get challenged down the field. So, you have to have all right that mental fortitude as a corner to be able to cover, but also physical enough to step up and tackle whoever has the football and JRock did a really nice job there on their sideline of making a physical hit. He's been here for several years now, but for a guy like Jared Wayne getting a touchdown tonight and really been standing out throughout practice, have you noticed anything different about his game or something that he's done that just is making him kind of stand out a little bit more than usual this early in camp? >> Really not not surprising from Jared one. He does it in practice all the time. So, for him to go out there and make the plays he made tonight, I'm happy for for Jared because he's put in that work and he's done that on the practice field. So, he's a he's a tough cover always for our guys, and I'm happy that he was able to put that on display tonight. >> All right, appreciate it, guys. Y'all have a good evening.

title: Azeez Al-Shaair on DeMeco Ryans and His Texans Future | In-Game Interview
text: Aziz, you had a crazy off season. So many good things happened to you. You were talking about your Pro Bowl. Who was the first person you called to tell you made your first Pro Bowl? >> Uh my mother, of course. Um just something I've obviously been trying to accomplish, you know, throughout my career. Um something I aspired for or inspired for and uh so my mother is the first person I wanted to call. >> Congratulations on the contract extension. Your mother was also front and center for that. How surreal was it to share that moment with her? >> Um it was awesome. you know, I mean, it was no other person in the world I would have wanted to share that moment with. Um, but just being able to sign that extension, especially being here. Uh, Houston is like my home now and, uh, truthfully feels like a family. So, my mother being there and just everybody being there and supporting me, it meant a lot. >> How excited are you to stay with Demo? He's been there throughout your whole pro career. It's actually crazy because like for me like I guess now like I think about myself and I think about when he was first my coach. I want to say he was maybe 34 or 35 and I guess you don't even realize like I'm 29 now. So I'm like dang like that's he was only 5 years older than I was right now. Like that's crazy. Uh but it's amazing. I mean just a blessing. Great coach, great man. Uh love his family, you know, love him and just grateful that I can keep working with him. >> You were also nominated for the Walter Payton Man of the Year award. Why is it so important to give back to the community? >> I mean, it's huge. You know, it's a platform that we have. It's a great opportunity to be in the position that we're in. Coming from where I came from, overcoming so many obstacles, try to give people hope and you know, you only have this platform for so long. Uh, so for me, I feel like it's just it's just a blessing that I was given. So, I have to pay it forward. >> Fellow linebacker Henry Toato also locked in here in Houston. Now, what makes you two so great together, >> man? It's like I feel like what I love about playing with Henry is I don't have to even think like there's some things where like we're on the field and we just see the game the same way. So maybe times where I'm supposed to maybe make a call to him or he's supposed to make a call to me. We don't even have to say a word like we just pass off the routes or we just play it exactly how I know he's going to play or he knows I'm going to play it. So it's really just like the cohesiveness and just like knowing like how he plays the game and how I play the game. He's a great player. Fast, physical, he does everything the right way. Um, I'm so proud of him. I I genuinely love him like a brother. >> Thanks so much, Aziz. Good luck this season. Glad you're staying to Houston. >> Appreciate you.

title: Mike Tomon on the Texans’ 25th Season and Toro District | In-Game Interview
text: Chargers and we're happy to have Texans President Mike Tolman with us in the booth as we continue on through this third quarter. 25th season, Mike, of Texans football. title: LIVE: The Houston Texans address the media
text: What's up? >> Good evening. >> What did you think about some of your rookies that got their first action tonight? >> And for our rookies, I think a few guys had really good outings just from being there on the sideline watching it. Starting first off with Marlon Klein. thought he really shined today. Everybody saw the pass that he caught was it's where I see him where he can excel uh for our offense and just open the offense up for us. It's his his catch radius is just it's tough to guard him, right? And he definitely has the speed as well to run away from guys. So, he stood out for to me not only just to catch him, but watching him in line blocking in the running game. I saw him finishing some blocks there exactly how we wanted it done. So, a ton of positives there for him. anytime you take the football away. I think Kamari Ramsey did a good job of getting an interception there. Should have had a few more that we uh let go through our hands. But, you know, I thought the backs ran well. Noah Whitten did a good job of running the football. Um Lewis Bond getting him back, doing some punt returning. I thought that was a lot of positives there for him. Uh something we can definitely continue to work more and he can improve on. So, uh, just starting as we started the game with our first first unit, our offensive, uh, line thought they did a really nice job that first drive, just having a positive drive, driving down and getting the score. Jared Wayne showed up making a lot of good plays. Davis made some good decisions there. So, overall, some it was some positive things there early on, but just collectively is not our style of play. And, uh, so a lot for us to improve upon. I got two that certain offensive line. Was that more so about getting continuity between them >> as opposed? >> Yeah, we want Yeah, they needed to go out and play together and they did a really nice job what we gave. We gave them 10 to 15 reps and those guys did a good job with those reps. >> You touched on was that what y'all expected from him when you when you drafted him in April? We expect that. And even he has more as well. I think this is just a start of Marlon Klein as he continues to grow and learn how we're doing things. Like he's a really good athlete, right? And he's strong and physical at the line of scrimmage. So that's what we saw from the Michigan tape and that's what he's been showing all training camp. >> Coach, did you get an opportunity to see uh Kate McDonald occupy the space that you that you wanted him to? I have to look at the film to see see it up close and see how he did. But overall, you I thought he we got him some good valuable reps. He needs to get as many reps as possible, right? To continue to improve his game and improve, you know, our style of play. >> Do you have an update on Graham Mer and what happened? >> For the update on Mertz, you know, he was running there towards the the opponent sideline and, you know, unfortunately non-cont and I think he'll be we're evaluating him. We right now is looking at a a knee injury ACL. So we'll see get that updated to see what happens. >> Coach, taking everything in consideration without you know going back looking at the film was besid guys that you just named a few other things that sort of stood out with you that you saw just muscle memory on you. You want to go back and look at the film to see how they turned out the course of the game? I really want to go back and really dive into the film to really get a a great evaluation of all the guys. We had, what I like, we had a lot of different guys playing tonight. So, we rolled a lot of guys in, a lot of guys got valuable playing time. So, for me, I have to really go and watch it to, you know, see who I can single out from them doing a really good job. So, um, overall, again, it was it was some positive things, but anytime you I tell our guys, anytime you suit up and you're competing, you want to win the football game, no matter who's out there, you want to compete to win. So, it didn't go our way, but it's still a lot for us to learn and grow from. >> You talked about, I asked you before what you wanted to see, and you said you wanted to see the team play Tex style play. When you say that, you're talking about the aggressiveness. What part of that did you >> The style of play that I wanted to see? I wanted to see us play physical, right? And I did not see that the entire game. There were some glimpses of us playing physical, but the Chargers, they out physical to us the the the entire game, right? So, it was not our brand of football. When I speak of playing our style, that's a physical brand of football. And that was not up to par tonight. >> How valuable is it to have on your you know, having a guy who's a backup, but then when you call him in, especially after an injury, you know, he comes in and just be poised throughout this game. How valuable is he to the team? The backup quarterback is a true very valuable position and Davis has done a good job of just always being ready whenever his number is called. He's ready to step up and not just step up and just to be out there. He's out there and he can make positive plays for us as we saw him do right through this this past season when we were able to get on a winning streak there. Davis was the guy who sparked that. So, um he's very valuable to have around. We're happy to have him. >> One of the things of the looked in your defense is the way that how physical your quarterbacks are as far as attacking in the run game. Um, tonight we we got an opportunity to see some of those guys come down and stop, especially one of the hits I think that Jaylen Smith made. How important is that to have those type of quarterbacks to be able to be physical like that? >> For us defensively, you have to be able to set the edge. And it's not just defensive ends who set the edge. Our corners are going to get challenged a lot because our defensive end are getting a lot of attention right from opposing offenses. So when that ball pops on the outside, corners have to step up and be physical and you have to tackle in this defense because you're going to get a ton of opportunities probably different than other schemes, but in our scheme, corners are going to get challenged as tackling and also get challenged down the field. Um and we're trying to keep developing him in the pass game and uh run blocking and everything with scheme related. But I mean when you see him flash as he does, especially on vertical routes down the field. Um he can take the top off of defenses and create mis mismatches all over the field um with his size and speed. So uh big time play getting him on that that seam route we had early in the game. Davis obviously with Brad Burks getting hurt. You had to go back in. You never want to see anybody get hurt, especially in a preseason game, but how much does that help you to get that many more plays in live game action now? >> Yeah, first off, um, hate it for Graham. Um, I've been there. I've had some knee injuries in the past um, in high school and college and I'm wishing him the best. It's a long road to get back to recovery and get back to normal, but I mean, he's a good player, good great guy. Um, and I know he'll be he'll come back stronger um, starting off that, but I mean, yeah, it's the reality of the game. Um, wasn't initially expecting to go back in, but something happens that's out of your control and, um, I want to go back in there and compete with my guys, my teammates. Um, spread the ball around and let let a lot of the young guys make plays and, uh, showcase themselves to try to make a roster. >> He's been here for a couple years now. Do you notice anything different with Jared Wayne than what you see? >> Uh yeah, Jay Wayne's a stud. Um I mean he's been extremely consistent since he's been here. I love throwing him the rock. Um another guy creates mismatches with his size and his natural ability to go up and high point the ball. And uh he's a really easy target to throw to. So when I saw I had that match up, they were playing um some sort of match coverage down there and I knew he had to run away and I could kind of just put it up and let him go up and grab it and I mean that's exactly what he did. >> Davis, in regard to your performance tonight, how do you feel like you did overall and your teammates, how do you feel like they worked with you overall when you're >> Yeah, I mean obviously we didn't get the result we wanted. We want to go out there and play to win and I mean unfortunately we didn't do that but um I thought it was a positive. I thought um process-wise, everything was done very efficiently and clean. We were getting in and out of the huddle and communicating and um I mean some plays just don't execute or play out the exact way you want it to on the field. Um credit to the other guys on the Chargers for playing a good game and getting the win, but um it's definitely a great learning opportunity to go out there and get live reps for all of our guys and myself included. And um we're looking forward to the next one. Ashley, you can't speak for everybody except the locker room, but how much more comfortable do you and and do you feel like most of the team is with Nick's offense going into another year and another full off season where you can go through the infantry season of learning the playbook, but also the personnel that he kind of really wanted to implement last year. >> Yeah, I mean it's exciting to see where we're at right now. Um I think I mean even comparing OTAAS to where we were last season and last year during OTAAS, it's I mean it's a night and day difference. um kind of getting to that uh graduate level of the offense where everyone really seeing what what the uh objective of the play is. Sometimes you're calling something to set up something else and like guys are really starting to make that click and um keep pushing similarities between plays so it makes it hard for the defense to uh decipher what we're actually going to get to. And I mean I think just being being in the same scheme for a longer time makes everyone have more comfort. and um the recall process of putting in new plays throughout the season when you're game planning, it clicks a lot faster so we can go out there and play fast. And um it's exciting. Obviously, we're not going to show everything we're capable of in preseason. We'll save that for week one versus Buffalo, but um I mean, it's exciting. I think we got we like what we have in this building and um we're excited to see how it keeps uh keeps evolving. >> Well, obviously being the first preseason game tonight, a lot of normal game planning week, but I would guess that's probably going to increase some for the game against the Raiders next week. A little bit more detail. >> Yeah, I think uh too we have a crossover practice with them uh middle of next week, so we'll get a a lot of good reps during that. Um and you're able to game plan kind of throughout the week. I think our practice schedule this week, we're going to emulate uh in end week or in season schedule. So, we're going to kind of start prepping our guys to get ready for what our schedule's going to be like so we can start building that rhythm and routine um to come out and really just execute at a high level. >> Marlins are working. There's several other guys including some undrafted guys like Noah and then Lewis of course. What have you noticed from them and how quickly they've been able to kind of adjust to length and how impressive you've been with the short amount of time that they've been able to get the ins and outs of this offense? >> Yeah, I mean I think this is one of the best rookie classes I've been around. um just the professionalism they carry themselves with and um already building routines. A lot of them kind of early on were asking vets to help them with their routines and kind of give them a game plan to be a professional in this league. And a lot of them have really I mean hit it in stride and um I mean it's a good thing when you don't really notice you're out there playing with rookies. Um they're kind of just plug and play and a lot of them are uh doing big things. Thank you.

title: Houston Texans preseason lineup details, starters, key players to watch
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson previewing tonight's preseason opener against the Los Angeles Chargers. Some details about how the Texans will handle playing time. So I'm told that the Texans will start their offensive line including rookie center and first-round draft pick Keilan Big Red Rutledge against the Chargers. They're only expected to play about a series, which is very similar to how they handled the playing time last year against the Minnesota Vikings. With Davis Mills starting under center and then quickly giving way to Keeton Slovis and Graham Mertz. Slovis no longer with the Texans, but Mertz will play the majority of this game. So some other things to know. Running backs David Montgomery and Woody Marks, wide receiver Nico Collins and several other key offensive skill players are out for this game. Not because of injury, but because of a precautionary measure to not expose them to potentially being hit by maybe some overzealous young player that try to make a name for themselves, that kind of thing. So you just avoid potentially bad outcomes and exercise caution when it comes to the preseason opener. Next week it'll be much different against Las Vegas Raiders. You'll see C.J. Stroud. You'll see the offense. You'll see a lot of guys. But this night they do want to have the offensive line. They will start rookie running back Noah Whittington. We'll get into a little more about Whittington in a moment, but other key players that will not play the starting defense, meaning Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Tommy Togiai, Aziz Al-Shaair, Henry To'oTo'o, Derek Stingley Jr., Kamari Lassiter, Kaelen Bullock, Reed Blankenship, and Jalen Pitre will all not play against the Chargers. Not a big shock, but still you want to know. And it's considered unlikely that they would have three-time Pro Bowl defensive end Jadeveon Clowney playing this game. So, as I said, starting offensive line for about a series or so, including Kellen Mond, and I would think Eric Murray, Wyatt Teller, and Ariante Ursery. We'll see right tackle. Do they go with Tunsil Brown or Brandon Smith? It lists Tunsil Brown first on the depth chart. It says or Brandon Smith. Tunsil Brown is a very large player, the biggest offensive tackle in the NFL, and an older player. Would you want him to play in a preseason game? I would think no, but if it's just for a series, maybe that makes sense. Among the injured players that are sidelined or coming back from injuries or slated to miss the game, that includes running back Dameon Pierce who has a strained hip flexor, and British Brooks who broke his hand and had surgery. Tight end Brevin Jordan who has a knee injury, lingering knee injury. Tank Dell coming back from a major knee injury two years ago and still not in full contact. You saw him in a full team drill, yes, but no one was going to hit him. It was as if he had an imaginary red jersey on protecting Tank from contact. Safety MJ Stewart is still on the physically unable to perform list. He tore his quadriceps tendon last year. Linebacker E.J. Speed as reported during the offseason, he tore his quadriceps tendon lifting weights doing a split squat in the Texans weight room, and unfortunately, it is a season-ending injury. He partially tore his quadriceps muscle, fully tore the quadriceps tendon, and that's why it's a season-ending injury. He is walking again and working his way back, but it is a tough blow, and we'll get into the third linebacker competition because this is very important to know. So, a year ago in the preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings, Davis Mills started at quarterback. They had wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson and running back Dare Ogunbowale and fullback Jakob Johnson starting along with tight end Cade Stover. And the offensive line, and they held out some veterans, but they started some of the other players. Ariante Ervin, Juice Scruggs on the left side, Jake Andrews at center, Ed Ingram at right guard, Blake Fisher at right tackle. They rested Tytus Howard, Cam Robinson, and Laken Tomlinson. On defense, they started defensive ends Solomon Byrd and Jerry Tillery, defensive tackles Tim Settle Jr. and Tommy Togiai, Jake Hansen, who is out with an ankle injury for this game, and also, you know, >> [clears throat] >> E.J. Speed. And they started Jaylen Smith and Niazi Ross at corner, and M.J. Stewart and Ross Yeast at safety. And whoever's on the field, DeMeco Ryans expects a high standard. He said he's looking for the first time out there, are we displaying our play style? That's the main thing he wants to see, no matter who you are or when you touch the field, are you repping the Texans brand? So, DeMeco Ryans pretty intentional about that and very direct. He wants to see guys play fast, relentless, and finish, and find details. When the lights are on, are you going to be consistent? Can you go out and perform under the lights under more stress? How do you guys operate? So, with that said, here are some key players to watch. Everybody wants to watch Keilan Robinson, right? He's your first-round pick. You want to see him compete against another NFL team, especially after his run of confrontations, bruising blocks against the Texans' top-ranked defense. He got into it with Will Anderson Jr. He's gotten into it with Danielle Hunter, Ali Gaye, Kaden McDonald. So, there's a new sheriff in town, very feisty competitor. His college coach called him an absolute psycho. An NFC West scout told me, "Great guy, great football player, really great guy off the field, but a total d i k on the field. Does not mess around. All business. And as DeMeco Ryans said, he loves the scrappiness. Obviously, you don't want to see him get penalties, but as I brought up in my live chat, he only had five penalties in college. So, it wasn't like he was a heavily penalized guy. He was someone that, was under control. So, when I think about Keelan Rutledge and how I think he'll play, that I think he will be feisty and play to the whistle. I don't know if he'll go as far over the line as he did in practice. You know, this is a game. So, actually, I misspoke about the penalties, but it is not a ton of penalties. It was five penalties last season, rather, not five overall. 15 official, 16 total in 3,019 career snaps for Keelan Rutledge. So, he played a lot of football in college and did not incur a lot of penalties. That's something that most teams, five penalties in a season, and especially if they're not a lot of false starts, would accept. And I would say, especially if it's going with a physical brand of football and a high blocking percentage. But, you look at him overall, year by year, and it's not like he had a ton of penalties at Middle Tennessee State or Georgia Tech. So, I think he can play under control. I think that he's, you know, I haven't talked to him in a little bit, but obviously, looking to establish himself, prove something, because that's what it's about when you're a rookie. You want to show what you've got and that you are, you know, really worthy of being out there. So, I think he's more than deserving, and he is listed as the first-string center on the unofficial depth chart ahead of Jake Andrews. And I've had a lot of questions about Andrews and about trades, and I think it's too early for that. I can see Andrews still sticking around. There's some scenarios where you might want both guys. So, let's go to the second round. Caden McDonald former Big Ten Conference Defensive Lineman of the Year at Ohio State played with a low pad level. He's had a powerful charge. He was regarded as the top run-stopping interior defensive lineman in the draft and could have been a first-round draft pick. The Texans considered him in the first round. They went up getting both, so they're really happy to get Keelan Riles and to get Caden McDonald. And they said that he's shown how strong he is. He's kind of bullying these you know, coaches when they're holding the pads and you know, trying to be tough as DeMeco Ryans said, but he's showing his strength. He just wants to see if he pull it all in consistently play with proper footwork, proper hand placement in terms of how you hit the opponent's pads, their chest plate their shoulder pads. And so far, so good. I know that Riles has gotten the lion's share of the attention as the first-round draft pick, but I'm here to tell you, Caden McDonald looks very good as well. So remember when he was playing for the Buckeyes he was often getting the first hit. He had 65 tackles and three sacks. And this is on a defense that was headlined by some real blue chippers. Caleb Downs Arvell Reese, Sonny Styles first-round draft picks, all of those guys. And he could have been a first-round draft pick, too. But as McDonald's told me, I bring power and he's attacking what he needs to work on and you know, I think he's here for a very specific purpose to bolster the middle of this top-ranked defense as a big, strong anchor. And they're excited about him. So on Whittington starting against the Chargers in his first NFL game the Texans made a commitment to him that included 267,500 total guaranteed, 20,000 signing bonus, 247,500 of his first-year base salary is guaranteed. Three years, three 3.12 million. But that's all well and good, but you've got to show it on the field. He has shown me vision, explosiveness, and a little bit of power. And Western Kentucky transfer for the Ducks, he rushed for 829 yards and six touchdowns, average 6.4 yards per play. And as DeMeco Ryans says, this guy seems to make a play every day. Has a good feel for pressing blocks, for vision, knowing when to cut, when to take the ball outside, when to cut it back up inside. And he sees great feel and he as he says, when you see guys lower on the depth chart these preseason games, they're going to make some nice plays and he says, Noah will not surprise him. Neither will Jacob Peterson Burger. All right, third linebacker. Main competitors for this job, Wade Woodaz, Marcel Dabo. Woodaz is the prototype at linebacker at 6'3", 236-lb converted safety. He's run a 4.52 in the 40-yard dash. He was very decisive and quick reacting in the past week. I think he's getting more comfortable. He's starting to really get his legs under him and find his way for the defense. I think understanding the defense, getting comfortable, that's a big thing when you're new on any job, but especially as a rookie. He is a young guy. 217 career tackles at Clemson. And he had 20 and 1/2 tackles for losses, nine sacks, three interceptions, a touchdown, four forced fumbles and a blocked punt. And Dalton Schultz was talking about him and he says, these he's kind of following the trend at linebacker with defenses more athletic at the second level. So he says, you know, in the the old days you had your DeMeco types, your 250-lb haymakers, fill the A gap, but now there's guys like Wade who's as big as the tight ends and just as athletic. More pass coverage, more athletic than the guys were kind of league when he was a rookie. So, it's not over though. He's got to perform in the games and Marcel Dabo will be heard from in this competition. They acquired him in a trade from the New England Patriots. He's a converted safety, former third-round draft pick and Big Sky Conference Defensive Player of the Year for Sacramento State. They like the versatility and the athleticism. He's had interceptions in actual NFL games. He has started, he's played safety and linebacker. And as Matt Burks says, you know, he's someone that has really, you know, looking at you know, everything he's done has great vision. Uh so it's like, you know, finding the ball, great length, smooth athlete, really good fit in terms of the profile they seek. Uses length to close windows. Excited to see him keep growing. All right. What about Marlon Klein, their second-round draft pick? 6'6", 250 lb pounds with a big catch radius. Native of Germany had to pay his dues behind stand-out tight ends with the Michigan Wolverines Colby Parkinson Loveland. He has caught touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud in recent days, including twice on Monday. They're encouraged by the size, the catch radius, the speed, improving blocking skills. And as we hear Ryan says, trajectory pointing up. Arrow up for Marlon Klein. Seeing him in the passing game, you're seeing him make a lot of plays, learning, throwing a lot at him. And for a rookie at this point in camp, they're very encouraged. So, they're pleased with where he is, excited to see him continue to progress. They've done a great job at the line of scrimmage seeing him do a good job. And thinks they think he can be a big threat in the passing game. Exciting young player to watch for this year. All right, we've talked a lot about Colin Wright. As Demeco says, he finds a way to get his hands on the ball in some type of fashion. Sticky coverage, they like what they're seeing from him. And another rookie to watch, Louis Bond.
