And then coach is going to be really upset. >> When it comes to the game and possibly after it, look at the playing time, how much do you want to see the backups you're mentioning the other day, but as far as like also protecting starters in those early preseason games? >> What's the question? >> How much do you want to make sure that you're resting some of the guys maybe that are your first string? >> Well, during the during this game against the Chargers we'll sit out a handful of guys that have been designated sit out for this game and the other guys will get a ton of the reps. >> Very competitive practice today. Was it due to the fact that you all said, "Okay, so this is a game time situation." >> I think the guys were a little fired up. And I had had to get after them a little bit yesterday. It wasn't our best practice yesterday by any means. That wasn't who we are, how we come out. That wasn't it. So, you know, everybody needed a reminder just of what we're what we're trying to achieve. What What are we trying to accomplish, right? To do what we're trying to accomplish, it takes persistent work every single day. We can't have letdowns. We can't have setbacks. Like we have to continue to press forward. We have to count on guys to be relentlessly consistent in what they're doing, in their approach every single day. Yesterday we took a step back. It wasn't good enough. But today guys responded really well. All three phases did a really great job, right? Making plays, doing what they're supposed to do. So, I'm really proud of the work we put in today and we're ready to go for game day. >> What does the coach want to see from a running back on the back end of the depth chart as far as making the team and what have you seen from Noah Whittington who's kind of in that battle? >> Noah seems to make a play every day. He He has a really good feel for pressing blocks and his vision. Just knowing when to cut, when to take the ball outside, when to you know, make a cut back up inside. Just you feel a guy. I see a guy who has plays a really great vision, great feel at the running back spot. So, when you see guys that are lower on the depth chart in these preseason games, some of those running backs are going to shine. They're going to make some nice plays. Noah won't surprise me. Pittsburgh won't surprise me. Those guys have have done it all camp. So, excited to see them play. >> How would you assess the ramp up in physicality? I know you're always trying to tow that line between intensity and making sure players are staying healthy, but are you pleased with that balance? >> This is probably our best year with that balance of keeping guys healthy, but also playing our style, right? It is a lot of give and take there. But, I can never sacrifice the the mindset and the play style that I want to exhibit. When we we play ball, you want everybody to continue to talk about how physical we are, how relentless. Like, man, how do you Why do your guys run to the ball like they do? How do you guys finish that way? That's our brand. That's who we are as Texans, and we will always represent that. But, the fine line is we have to protect the team. When we're practicing against each other, we are on the same team, no matter how upset guys may get at each other. And it's that point of camp, right, where I'm tired of going against the same guy over and over again. I know his moves. I know everything that he's going to throw at me, and I'm just tired of going at it. So, Thursday's game is coming right on time for us. >> On the competition for spots, how is third linebacker shaping up, and what do you hope to see from some of the guys that are trying to get filled in that role? >> We have a lot of great depth at It's We have a lot of capable guys who can go out and play our defense for us, but also that that third, fourth linebacker spot, it comes down to special teams, right? And how valuable are those guys being able to play it all four special teams for us. So, it it'll be important for those guys in this game to go showcase that. >> It feels like this year, more than in recent years, we've talked about the undrafted free agents, especially the rookies. What have you seen from Trayvon Sanders and how he's been impactful? And what do you like about him when he was coming out? >> Trayvon has done a really nice job of just you know, being smart, always aligning in the right place. We throw a lot on the receivers when it comes to alignments and motions. I feel like he's handled that really well. He's fast, explosive guy who he can make some plays with the football in his hands. So, we'll see how he does on tomorrow night. >> David has been, you know, pretty effective pretty much all training camp. How impactful was it to see him make that play today and score that touchdown? >> It was a huge play, huge momentum boost for our offense to see David is what he's done a really good job of is his his route running, right? And him and Henry have had a lot of battles so thus far in camp. So, it was cool to see, you know, David make a big play for us and that's the type of player he is. That's why he's here for us. He can spark an offense, right? He can lift us with just making those plays or just by him being a leader, being vocal, right? Encouraging the other guys. >> All right, thank you, coach. All right, thank you, guys. I'm going to go. >> [music] >> Do you want to get off? I mean, just come in short, work every day. I mean >> No, I'm not a guy that really sets big goals. I'm I'm Hey, every day I'm going to show up, come and do the same thing over and over again, and all them goals will come. >> You and Tytus Howard have you become quick friends that are kind of helping each other out? What's that like, that rapport? >> Tytus is cool, man. All All the rookies, undrafted rookies, everybody. Whole rookie class, we've got a good good class, so bunch of good dudes and people that love football. >> So you throw the pitch that went well. What was it like the reception from the fans, and how did that feel getting to fans getting to know you and see >> Yeah, they just kind of taking me in. I've loved every every second I've been in Houston. Second home, and I've loved it, so just welcomed me, and I was I was grateful to be there, getting to do that. >> What's the favorite place you've been to eat so far? >> I've been tons of places, man. I I I can't throw one out, but >> Couple highlights? >> Just a lot of good barbecue, a lot of good steak places. I mean, I've been Obviously, you know you know me, I love to eat, so I'll eat anything. >> All right, and uh training camp will be here right around the corner. You guys have set high goals as a team, not just individual, but they're all talking about Super Bowl, which is great. You want to be a championship caliber team. >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, I think that's any competitor's goal, is to win. You want to be the last person to win anything, you want to win a championship, and I think, you know, we've established that over these last couple years, and that's what we'll continue to do, and hey, we've got a lot of steps to go take that, but we've got opportunity to. >> Last one, competition, that's all about football, so as you and other guys compete for center, guard, all that stuff, how much do you embrace that and love that? >> Oh, yeah, I mean, it's it's the reason why I'm here. I was one of the big recruit out of high school. I had to scratch and claw for everything I want, so I I wouldn't want to come in and be the day one starter. I would want to want to go win it. >> Mentoring from Wyatt Teller, what's that like? What kind of What are some things you learn from him specifically? >> Oh, yeah, man, he's he's been huge. Kind of plays the game how I like it to be played. He's finished, he's nasty, mauls. He brings so much in terms of that and that, you know, that kind of swag, that kind of mentality he brings that I love to see, and then, you know, just so much stuff, just how to be a pro. You see it every day. He's He's had a really good career, and he's getting up there in age. You you how he operates and it's been great to learn from him. >> So how are you liking your transition so far now that the vets and everybody are all together? >> It's been great. Um learning so much every day. Um just in terms of the scheme, understanding that and then there's so many good vets in there that you can pick up from. Um kind of, you know, the pro habits they have, how they come show up to work every day. So I mean it's been great just bouncing around doing everything he needs. >> Do you feel pretty comfortable snapping now? Do you feel like that's kind of a natural Frank Heats told me he thinks you could be an all-pro center one day. >> Yeah. I mean I I think definitely as you get more reps you get more comfortable. I have done that before but you know, when you have your hand on the ball more, there's going to be some growing pains in that and I'm you're just working those out every day. Same, you know, I didn't play offensive line till I got to college so you get there you're going to have to learn some stuff. So once you learn it, comes second nature you'll be fine. >> Frank, uh how's Keita McDonald doing so far? >> You know, I think the the biggest job he's done well is just trying to get acclimated, uh learn our scheme, learn our system. Um what you really see though is a guy with a good physical presence, uh ability to knock back, control the line of scrimmage. So we're excited to continue to try to develop that, to continue to grow and evolve in this defense and this scheme. >> You got back most of the guys so you've got a good rotation. Uh what do you like about it? Just see maybe quick hit on each of the main guys that are in that rotation. >> Yeah, you know, it's always good when you can kind of bring back the whole group that kind of finished our season and so you know, kind of starting interior it's good to have Rankins, a season vet who knows this game inside and out that can really help a young guy like Keita develop and grow quickly and develop in this scheme. Thomas brings the consistency so it's it's a guy that we know our young guys when they figure out what to do we can just say, "Hey, this is what I would do before you." The type of preparation work ethic and style he works with and then obviously got the the maniacs off the edge and then Will and Denell that that can take over the game any second and so the encouraging thing to come back is we kind of got our first look at Denell just obviously he's in shape but the presence and the and the professionalism that they bring back to our into our scheme and our defense, that's what's really exciting. >> Logan Hall, uh some three-tech and things like that and I I think different body type but uh even bigger than Autry but he can swing out and uh you know, go over the tackle. >> a he's a guy that you kind of look as a versatile piece that you can move inside and outside and you can kind of create matches based on what each offensive line we have for that week where he can be best used at. So, a guy with his kind of experience, his skill set, excited to get a chance to work with him in the in training camp. I think the sky's the limit for him. I think he has a chance to have some of the best years of his career. >> I just bring power. Um like I said, powerful guy. I'll come in and help them. And um like I said, focusing on what I can and cannot do and the things I need to attack on that I need to work on, build off those and like let everything else handle itself. >> You mentioned when you were drafted that the coaching staff, when you met with them before, they just want you to attack and not to react. Why is that important to you and why does that sort of bring out the best in your game? >> Uh we got $90 million on the outside. That's all I can say. So.

title: Texans' preseason game preview, rookie watch: Keylan Rutledge, Kayden McDonald, Marlin Klein & more
text: How you doing, man? Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. The Texans open the preseason Thursday night at Reliance Stadium. Here's what you need to know. The starters, this will be a night off for the majority of the starters, including quarterback CJ Strad. The Texans are expected to start Davis Mills. Last year he played one series, threw a touchdown pass to Braxton Berios and then he was out of there. So we expect a big day for Graham Mertz, their third quarterback who's made some improvements this year. Further removed from the torn ACL he had at Florida. I think he's delivered the football better and he's improved. And these are some auditions for him. What if Davis Mills ever became a trade candidate? What if he decided to leave in free agency perhaps to pursue a starting job? You know, there's definitely some teams that have high opinions of Davis. What about Graham Mertz? Okay, so while Graham Mertz is certainly of interest, all eyes will be on the offensive line and we'll see. Last time they did play a few of the offensive linemen when they were in that preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings. So that was a year ago and you know, one thing we've seen with Miko Ryan is he's something of a creature of habit. So looking back on that lineup, yes, left tackle Aron Ters, he started Juice Scrugs, who was projected as a backup at that time, he was a starter along with Jake Andrews who became the starter. So sometimes they play some linemen. They also started Ed Ingram and Blake Fischer. So they sat out a lot of the offensive linemen including some really proven vets like Titus Howard or guys that didn't want it panning out but at the time were projected starters in Lake and Tomlinson and Cam Robinson. So something of a mixed bag and that brings us to Keelen Big Red Rutled. They'll want him to get some game action. I believe he will play. We'll find out more as we get closer to the game. But yeah, that's the expectation that they would want to play Rutledge a little bit and have him snap in a game. So, Rutled has been the talk of camp with his feisty nature. He's been in four physical confrontations. Not really like where they trade punches, but I mean, there's been some tempers flaring. First, you had, you know, him planting Aziz Alshshire. That didn't lead to a fight, but he tangled with Ali Gay, Denil Hunter, Kada McDonald, and the latest confrontation, Will Anderson Jr. And Deik Ryan likes the feisty nature of the rookie. He's a gritty, tough dude. Brent Key, the Georgia Tech coach, told me, "This guy is an absolute psycho. I talked with a scout from an NFC West club and he said that at the Senior Bowl, thought he was a great guy, but he said on the field, a total prick." So that is the book on Rutled so far. And only real question is, you know, is he going to snap very well in the game? He's listed as the starter on the Texans unofficial depth chart. Jake Andrews listed as the backup. So, we'll see what they wind up doing with that, you know, situation. But to me, Rage has checked a lot of boxes so far as he pursues the starting job. Before we get to Marlon Klein and some of the other players, I want to talk about Wade Woodz. So, Wade is someone that the Texans just loved in the draft process and he's converted safety. He's 6'3, he's 236 pounds. He runs the 40 yard dash in 4.52 seconds. and they're starting to feel like, you know, there's a chance here. Could they develop him as a third linebacker? It is neck andneck between him and former Patriots linebacker and safety Marte Mapu. There are some pluses with both players. Wood is more of the prototypical linebacker because of his size and he's got a football temperament. He is a aggressive young player and he's starting to now that he feels more comfortable on the field. I'm seeing more instinctive play from him. They signed him to a 4-year $5.482 million contract with a $1.102 million signing bonus. And yeah, Woodz, um, while the Brian Cushing comparisons are unfair really to him and to Cushing, who was an NFL defense rookie of the year and a Pro Bowl linebacker and a firstround draft pick, nonetheless, I feel like Woodaz is, you know, just a good prospect. Big, fast linebacker, as he describes his own style of play, fast, physical, and violent. and they had been on wood ads for a long time. There was a formal meeting NFL scouting.com that I reported on and then they had follow-up work on the Clemson campus. They had that virtual interview with the Texans linebacker coach Bill Davis. So, they've been on him for a while. And Davos Sweeney says this is one of the best guys that he's coached and at Clemson very productive. 217 career tackles, 20 and a half for losses, nine sacks, three interceptions, a touchdown, four or four fumbles, a block punt. In the words of Dav Sween, he's coached a lot of good football players. He's a baller, fun guy to coach, fun guy to watch play because he plays the way you want everybody to play. So that's the book on him. Uh he gained roughly 40 lbs at Clemson. Lots of pizzas, Gatorade protein shakes. You drink 400 calories. They are 12 of those a day. But yeah, I feel like he's maintained his mobility from his safety days. And he has a little bit of that sideline to sideline skill that you love to see in a linebacker. and definitely uh has that temperament. That's a big deal. So, Colin Wright, undrafted rookie, has been the best defensive undrafted rookie so far this year. He's had several interceptions at camp. He's been challenging Traremon Smith for a spot on the roster. Really needs to get past Smith and how he plays on special teams will determine a lot about whether they're comfortable exposing him to waiverss and try to get him on the practice squad. but he'll be around and he's pushing so many other players whether that's Brandon Codrington, Steven Hall, Elijah Huzzy and I feel like he's done very well. But yeah, he definitely has a absolutely viable chance to make this roster. So, we're talking a lot about rookies. He's from Manville High School, had four interceptions at Stanford, was expected to be drafted in late rounds, but instead it's a fine line between being drafted and going undrafted. And as Deikica Ryan says, "This guy finds always a way to get the hand on the ball. Sticky coverage, attacking the ball, breaking up passes, and really good qualities as a corner." All right. What about Marlon Klein, who many thought was drafted too high in the second round? I know a lot of other teams told me they thought that he would be available after the second round, but the Texans really liked Marlin, and they felt like this German import, this Michigan man has all the physical tools. And while in the spring, yes, he had the strained hamstring, he has made up for that lost time. He is the biggest tight end on the roster. 6'6, 250 lbs. He's caught a touchdown and no, he didn't have a lot of pass catching production at Michigan. He was behind some great players including Coulson Loveless and a bunch of other guys. And you know, you look at, you know, other people. There was AJ Barner, there was Shunmaker, but they're putting him into a lot of situations and they said the trajectory is up. That's in the words of Deo Ryan. I agree with that. So, he's fighting for time behind Daltton Schultz and Foster Maro who's been installed as the second tight end. And you see him pushing and I believe he's going to get in front of Kate Stober. Brevin Jordan remains sideline with the knee injury. Uh it's not a season any injury, but it is uh tough to not have him out there. So, that's what's going on. Of course, we'll be watching punter Kai Krueger had a good day. I was able to report that the other day. Kai Krueger had a good day inside of the Reliance today in that indoor practice. That was impressive. And I think because he's not probably thinking about this competition that he was in initially with Jack Stonehouse. Now, Krueger can probably relax a little bit. Not relax too much, but this is a prime opportunity for him to win the starting job. If he has a good game Thursday withholding, then he has a chance. As I reported before, they would sign Chris Freeman. Chris Freeman is undrafted kicker from Connecticut. He is here to give Kaim Fairburn a break and he is expected to kick in this game even though he just got here. Uh he's been here for about a day and a half. So they brought him in, flew him in from his hometown of Indianapolis. He was at their rookie mini camp on a try out basis and then he recently tried out for them along with Will Ferren. So they try out him and then they sign him. He was 20 of 23 and last year Connecticut made all his extra points. It was a Luke Rosa award semi- finalist. All right. I don't want to bury the lead because you know we talked about Rutled. We talked about Rutledge a lot. Let's talk about Katie McDonald. Katie McDonald big, tough, strong, very stout at the point of attack. Controls the line of scrimmage. Someone that I feel like has vast potential. was the Big 10 Conference defensive lineman of the year. He was making the first hit and a lot of tackles. He had 65 tackles and three sacks last year for the Buckeyes. Guess who was on that defense? A bunch of blue chippers? Downs, Styles, Arl Reese from the Giants. So, you look at what he did and being able to make the first play, you know, and get to the football that fast as a bigger man at 330 pounds or so, that's impressive. that shows you he has mobility, has a good nose for the football. So, they're excited about Kayen McDonald, another player that I feel like has had a good training camp. When you're in the trenches like him, you're, you know, playing there, keeping, you know, blocks off of the linebackers, I feel like you're not going to get as much acclaim and you have to really watch closely to see, is he controlling his gap? Is he using his hands well? Is he able to get off the block and make the tackle? So, we watched him closely and what I see from him is a good young football player that has a real chance to be impactful as a rookie next to Logan Hall in the rotation. So, it's a big day. Naqucoin Jones is going to play a lot. And of course, you know, he has to be very impressive in the preseason to keep his spot on the roster. He's competing with Mario Jr. Mario, of course, signed a fully guaranteed. It's a small contract. It's less than 2 million, but it's still fully guaranteed. Sin Davian Clowny's deal and you know most of it is guaranteed as well. Five and a half million base value 8 million is the upside the max value. So when you think about the Texans and you know some of these competitive situations as we said Colin Wright traumant Smith Traant Smith good at returns we would expect to see Trumont Smith get a long look. Uh normally he would start. So, going back to a year ago and the roster is not that much different in terms of, you know, some of the defensive players, uh, one of them that's pushing for a job again. He started last year against the Vikings, that's Solomon Bird, but I would expect it to be Dominique Robinson [clears throat] and Dylan Horton this time. And last year they started Daryl Taylor. Last year they started Tommy Tig, Tim Settle Jr., so probably the backup defensive tackles. I would think Katie McDonald if they want to put Logan Hall out there. He's a vet. He doesn't necessarily need to play, but I think Nquon Jones is going to play a lot. I don't know if Roy Juniors needs to play. They started at linebacker last year. EJ Speed, of course, is out for the season this year. Jake Hansen, who's got an ankle injury, and Nick Neman, who did make the squad. So, what should we probably expect this time? But Wade Wood and Marte Mapu, I think that they'll sub in, you know, the Jamal Hills and, you know, Jake Hmel, etc., and Aiden Fischer. So, we'll see where this goes. And they started the third running back at the time last year, Dario Agamo. So the third running back is not available, Jawar Jordan. So this could be a big night for Noah Whittington, the undrafted rookie from Oregon. And we've been talking about Noah a lot. We feel like Noah has had a really good run so far with the Texans. And I'm impressed by him. Uh and so is Deik Ryan. He's got good open field ability. He's got ability to make people miss. He has deceptive power. And they signed him to a three-year $3.12 million deal. They guarantee 267,500 of the contract with a 20,000 signing motives and 247,500 portion of his base salary guaranteed. Honorable mention, all Big 10 Western Kentucky transfer rush for 829 yards, six touchdowns last season. Averaged 6.4 yards per play. finished career with 2,950 rushing yards, 21 touchdown runs, and he has completely overcome the toe surgery he had in the off season, and now he's 100%. So, one of the guys that is in the running cuz George is going to miss this game with a strained hip flexor. British Brooks will miss this game and a few more weeks with a broken hand that required surgery. So, those are some of the injury situations. Brevin Jordan not expected to play, of course, because of a lingering knee injury. And when you think about the Texans and where they're at, obviously, you know, you rest a bunch of guys, and these are some of the ones I would think will not play in this game. Nico Collins, why would he play in the first preseason game? Jaden Higgins, Jaylen Null won't play because of his pinky injury. They haven't put him back into the full team drills. They're easing him back. He missed a lot of time. If you play the starting offensive line of Aranti Urser, Wyatt Teller, Keelen Rage, Edingham, and Trent Brown or Braden Smith, you play them for a series or so, then you're gonna have to sub guys out. I would not expect Dalton Schultz or CJ Strad to play. David Montgomery, Woody Marks, maybe maybe let him play a little bit, but I would think there's a chance he doesn't have to play. I think Foster Maro would play and of course Marlon Klein and Kate Stove. So, when you think about some of the backup linemen, we're talking about Jake Andrews, Evan Brown, Blake Fischer. I would think Blake Fischer would get a start because, you know, why would you want to play one of these older tackles in this kind of game? Should have mentioned him uh earlier, but a showcase kind of game for Lewis Bond. And Lewis Bond has been another one of the camp heroes. Someone that has made a lot of catches, a lot of touchdowns, has shown an understanding of space. and to me has been a guy that is pushing pushing pushing Justin Watson for a job. Jared Wayne will play a lot. Jared had a good camp so far. And then we're talking about the backup line. We're talking about James Neil the third. Sam Hagen, two good undrafted rookies that I penciled in for the practice squad. Eli Cox even better than last year, but I think he's pretty good. They restructured Jared Patterson. It's affordable now. You want to have him on the roster. They cut Montreal, Washington to create a spot for the aforementioned Chris Freeman. So, they've done a few things to try to get some guys onto the roster. And, you know, it's going to be interesting situation. This reminds me of when they had Jake Bates. I've talked about before when uh had him on the roster. So, yeah, looking at you know, some sleepers here, it's tough, you know, watching the depth chart. Someone that I know can play but has not had a ton of opportunities is Brandon Codrington. Good return man. It'd be interesting to see if he gets some chances um at some point in this game against the Chargers. Chargers will do the same thing. They're going to rest, guys. This is not the really most exciting part of the pres. I know everybody's happy the football's back, but I like to be very honest with you guys and transparent and maybe temper your expectations just a little bit knowing that this is not really the day that you're going to see all the topline guys. And that's understandable. You do not want your top players being exposed to uh some sort of Rudy type guy that's out there trying to make a name for himself. You can't have that. That's how you It's really a recipe for disaster. And smart coach like Ryan, they don't do They know how dangerous the first preseason game can be. Often times coaches will have a bit of a discussion. Hey, what are you doing? We're thinking this. Sometimes there is conversations like that. Don't know if he talked to Jim Farbaugh or not, but it's a similar approach that a lot of people will take with these preseason contests knowing, you know, it's about avoiding injuries, survive in advance. I know everybody wants to see CJ and the offense and they want to know all the plays and they want to know where's the 13 personnel, where's all this stuff. I'm just telling you, why would you show your good plays? You wouldn't. And you're also going to play this team. Not that that's a big consideration, but you'll see them again in during the season. So, when we go to Los Angeles and so another trip out to Sofi for a game against the Chargers, a good game last year. They strike deep early with Jaden Higgins and Jaylen Null. So the rookies getting it done and CJ Strath run some good footballs. One of CJ's good games last year at least. He started off pretty hot in that game and they hold on. They win. So you're going through some of the other situations with the team. I'm just watching and not expecting like Javian Clowny. Why would he play in a preseason game too? It just doesn't make sense. So what might we see? Dominique Robinson and Dylan Horton, Solomon Bird. Um, further down the depth chart, Sebastian Harsh, good name for a football player. Uh, good player. Dominique Bailey, Keonte Hamilton, Naquon Jones, I think, u, you know, there's no real reason to play the Mario, you know, guy, but no, might you, but Naquon Jones I know is playing in the game. I've, uh, been able to check on that. Of course, MJ Stewart still in the physical perform. So, there's opportunity for the depth safeties, Jaylen Reed, Kamari Ramsey. Uh, both of their moments. I think the third corner that makes sense to play Jaylen Smith, who's had a good camp. I'm going to, you know, I don't know if everyone saw this interview, but I'm going to attach the interview because he's had a good camp. JRock they call him from USC last year. Torn meniscus. He was having a good season, but now he's healthy again and he's made a lot of plays. You saw that clip where he rips the football away. Just a good player and I think that someone that the Texans can be excited about. Jaylen Petri missed the last two practices. So obviously as a starter he's not going to play along with Kamar Lasser Reed Blankenship, Caitlin Bulick, Dary Stingley Jr. who's in the top 25 for the all um [clears throat] NFL top 100 and then you know Aziz Alire, Harry Toto, Denil Hunter, Tomati Sheldon Rank as well Anderson Jr. not expecting any of them and I extend that to like I said Javian Clowney. So, it's going to be the backup bowl and that's what these situations go to. Special teams, yeah, you're going to have Chris Freeman kick. You're going to have Austin Breman snapping. You'll have Kai Krueger, you know, getting some chances to punt and hold. Uh, if they have those situations as far as returns, if Woody Marks plays, then yeah, Woody Marks and Traremont Smith on returns. I would expect some punt returns, you know, for them to try to move that around, divvy that up to a few other guys. So, we'll see where this goes, but it's going to be a very interesting night and might be the kind of night where someone like a Lewis Bond, maybe they stand out. I I could see that happening. It's always fun. The game isn't everything. A lot of it is hinges on the practice performances and the game. You want to see people stack both. Whether it was JJ McCarthy, Carson Wentz, or Kyler Murray, I think it comes down to who's going to operate the offense the fastest and the best. We know KC loves to have a a long play call in that headset. He loves for the quarterback to get to the line of scrimmage and be able to change the play. But also, if you look at last year under Carson Wentz, there were some RPO moments. There were some moments where, you know, play action mattered. But when he's on the move, he's a dual threat. Like the defensive ends and the outside linebackers has to have to honor that. You know, we've seen that happen a ton where somebody starts off as the leader. By week eight, if that person's not getting it done, they move on. So, you know, hats off to JJ McCarthy for handling it the way he's handling it. A lot of people would have taken it a different route, but he's been a consmate pro and he's, you know, accepted that role, whatever it's going to be with his team. >> Kyler Murray uh has been taking the first team reps this week, ever since the announcement. Again, a blessing. Um, you know, I think we got some special talent in that room. Um, from top to bottom, guys can make plays and I know there a lot of young guys eager to make plays and show uh what they what they're capable of. Uh, but again, just I mean, you you everyone knows what we have in that room uh from top to bottom. I'm excited to go out there and execute on game days. >> Well, Ron, it's a wealth of receivers with tons of experience. If you look at the top, you go Justin Jefferson, who has been here the entire training camp, healthy. Number two, Jordan Addison, who is stronger and faster this season. Number three, the free agent acquisition, Joan Jennings, with his ability to block and just a big body type of receiver. And because you are a former receiver, this is the perfect topic to bring this up. When we look past that number three, who are we who do you want us to keep eyes on? >> Well, I mean, first off, you got to go with Miles Price. And and when you think about this offense, first of all, I want to say Kyler Murray is right. Like, if everybody that loves Christmas, waking up to a Christmas tree with Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson under that tree, like that is the gift that every kid that's the Sega Genesis, the Xbox, the starter jacket, whatever it was. Like, that's the gift for 16-year-olds. That's the car they wanted. But that that he is that is a wealth of of receiver just tandemness. And then you add Jawan Jennings who is another big body in the red zone. We saw a lot of that during training camp where they're utilizing him in the red zone. They're forcing teams to if you want to double up just Justin. If you want to put a linebacker over the top of Jordan, take away that inside slant. Now he got a big body outside. But if they go four wides and and the fifth receiver being TJ Hawinson, Miles Price is a great little jitter bug in in the slot right there when they went four wides. I think he offers uh an ability to just on the jet sweeps if they want to do some cool things, some toss sweeps to a receiver. Like I think it gives Kevin Okonnell so much more he can do with that offense. And then of course you have Ty Felton who's right there with him as well. I think Ty Felton's biggest thing now is getting more reps with the ones. Like when he has a chance to catch a ball from Kyler Murray, make it matter. You know, for the most part, I think him and Miles Price have been with JJ McCarthy, but now I'm pretty sure they're going to work them in with the ones, too, just to see what that looks like because we know probably not going to see a lot of Addison and Jefferson in the preseason. So, those guys will need to be a little bit more familiar with Kyler Murray cuz they're definitely going to want Kyler in there for at least one or two series. And so, that's the question is, can they get that speed of offense down with them, but those two right there, I think, are doing a great job. Um, >> yeah. I mean, Miles Price's special teams ability really gives him a good place on this roster. And then you look at someone like Ty Felton who is able to now battle through contact. He's so his his route running has improved. He just has to be able to catch the ball a little bit more. But like you said, it's it's getting used to the quarterbacks, their rhythm, and and meshing your your game to what's going on with the scheme for the next couple of weeks. >> When Kyler Murray can trust like a guy like Miles Price or a guy like Ty Felman, that's going to get you more reps on the field. But that corner route was just truly what Kevin Oonnell wants in this offense. There was another deep ball. I think Kyler Murray threw to Justin Jefferson going across the field. Same thing. He had to trust Justin was going to climb and get to 18 because he's letting it go before he gets over there because if he waits early on, that was the interceptions we saw. And I think that was just rust of a quarterback not really having time with the receivers and then learning their speed at which speed they're going to run it. And now you're seeing more Chris routes and more on time passes. Well, switching to defense, there is a hitmansiz hole in that side of the ball. Harrison Smith is currently not on the roster. They are really going to miss their anchor safety, the guy who's been back there for so long providing basically being the quarterback of the defense. When we look at the communicators and the leaders on this team, let's hear from Josh Matelis because he's giving us some insight on how that whole operation is working right now without Harrison Smith. I could be blitzing and I'll get, you know, Justin Jefferson to line up right in front of me. I'll look at Cash, he'll know like I'm switching my blitz to him and let me play the coverage, you know. So, it's uh stuff like that that you build through reps. So, uh, I would say me, me, Cash, and not only just me and Cash, but me and, uh, a lot of the guys who've been here, we built up that, you know, that repetition where we just feel like we know each other like the back of our hands. >> Well said, Mr. Matelus. Of course, he's going to be one of the biggest communicators on this team. How do you see them being able to replace a veteran like that? >> Well, I mean, I've watched a lot of clips lately of safeties, right? Ed Reed, the guy I played with, Troy Palo, and and you might have saw what Ryan Clark said that he allowed Troy to be who he could be, which means I'm just gonna watch you do what you're not supposed to do and hope it works out and I got your back. Well, that's what Harrison Smith was. Harrison Smith could come up to that line of scrimmage every once in a while, Brian Floyd said it, and he would see something and he's like, he looked back at Josh and be like, I'm going like, I'm just I'm going like, I'm just, you got to back me up. Trust me, I'm I got this. I see something. And so now Josh has to figure out where he falls in that. Blake Cashman is going to be the green dot. The green dot's going to relay it back to the safety. The safety, which was Harrison Smith at the time, it's going to get everybody lined up on the back end. Well, now it falls on Josh Matelis, but he did learn a ton from Harrison Smith. I want to see a guy like Jamal Adams fit in where Josh Matelis was, which is the true Swiss Army knife. This is a guy that, you know, played safety his whole career, was one of the top players um at the position, had an injury, was asked to play a little bit of linebacker, but he says he's a true safety. So, but you you I asked him I said, "Hey, can you come off the edge? Can you blitz through the C gap or the B gap?" And he's like, "Oh, yeah." He's like, "I can get after a quarterback." So, I think that's where you're going to see him fill in that Josh Matellis role. And now Josh has to feel kind of more of the like Harris. I don't think Josh is going to have the autonomy this early on in the season to be able to just cowboy it, as they would say, and go off and do his own thing. But I I really do think he's going to use Jamal Adams along with Jay Ward, some of these other guys, but use Jamal Adams as the Josh Matelis where he becomes that Swiss Army knife. And then every once in a while, like we know Jamal said he can play back in safety where Josh falls back into his spot, say, "Hey, I'm going to go. You're going to drop back and be the deep safety." So I think that was the main reason why Brian Flores wanted to bring him here. It it gives them that true feel of like we can rock and roll our two safeties. And neither of you is a true free safety. Both of you are box safeties, but I think you're both smart enough and good enough that I can drop you in that back half and the other one can get out to the quarterbacks. >> Yeah, I love that Jamal Adams is here. Just that veteran presence like you you lose that in Harrison, but then you have this guy that comes in here and he's finally feeling like he's in the best shape of his life since his injury. He feels like himself and now he's getting to play the position he wants to play in safety. I love the other day he said that this is >> it feels so good to have someone believe in him again to do that. And I don't know, those kind of stories just get me every single time, Ron. Oh, yeah. They really do. >> All right. Well, let's get to the other side of the defensive backs room because we're going to talk the quarterback position battle. And if you look at look the list, well, if you look at the first official Vikings depth chart, which you can find at Vikings.com, there is Isaiah Rogers and Byron Murphy Jr., the two starters for the second season in a row. And then there's some new names that you're going to need to to write down some numbers you're going to need to remember. James Pierre, the free agent acquisition over the summer. You have the class of 2026, Charles Demings, who has become a quick fan favorite, Mr. Chuck D. And Dwight Mcloth Jr. still in the mix of all of this action. Someone who has been on the team for a season or two and has some familiarity with what's going on. So Ron, as we look at this position battle, what is what how do you see it shaking out? >> Yeah, I I think James Pierre coming from the Pittsburgh Steelers, you know, proven he can do it at a high level. I talked to Ryan Clark about him as well cuz, you know, he's a big Steeler guy, follows follows the team a ton. And I said, what do you get in James Pierre? And he said, you get a guy that's truly just a cornerback. Like he's not going to act like he's anything else. He said he has a lot of range. Um he can come up and bump you. He can play on the deep half. So he is a guy that again these are guys that Flores identify because there are guys that like Dion Sanders for instance he was a true just locked down man corner right where Flores would have been like the other 10 of you guys you do something Dion you just stop that one guy you go stop Tio or you go stop Jerry Rice everybody else do something else right they don't have that so what James Pierre gives them is the ability to play man but he can also drop back and he's he's got the size to be a backend safety when they do that weird kind of rock and roll with the corners where all of a sudden Byron Murphy and James Pierre safeties. Your two safeties are coming up and playing the half field with the uh the the flat routes and it like it's a it's an inverted cover two I guess you want to call it. Um it's a it's a total Frankenstein defensive look. But I like James Pierre and then the one honestly right now in my feelings just watching it again this is all feelings. It's not coaches. I'm not sitting in the film room. Chuck Dimmings is moving himself into that fourth spot. Like I feel like the way he's playing in practice, and this is what I always learned, when the GM and the coaches and the scouts are making comments about, man, that kid looks good. Man, this guy's making plays. >> That's a guy that if he does this through this first three preseason games, by week one, you might see Chuck Dimmings in that four when they go into that quarters look where it's four cornerbacks, two safeties, and it's just Blake Cashman or Ivan Pace, and then you got two or three down linemen. I feel like Demings is kind of putting himself ahead of McGlover, but McGlover early on will get the nod because he's been here, but you know, Chuck Demings has played I mean, he's he doesn't care and that's the one thing I love about him. If it's Justin Jefferson, if it's Jordan, if it's Ty Felton, he's playing all the guys the same way. He does not care who he's guarding. He's not here to make friends. He's here to make a roster. And that's what makes a really good competitor. And one thing I noticed, too, is like when he makes plays, you you even see guys like Justin Jefferson, you know, give him a little fist bump or something because they're like, man, like he is technically our teammate. So like, yeah, he's stopping us, but man, we need that on Sunday. And so that's the cool part that he's earned the veterans respect, too, because you don't see that a lot early on. >> They have he has earned the respect and and I think he is here to also make some friends on the side, too, because eventually he is the friendliest person I think you will ever meet in the locker. Josh Mattel calls him the prophet just because of all of the great quotes that he comes up with. He is uh as someone as coach has described him and many other people, energetic. Brian Flores calls him that dude. Like I it's been a while since I've seen someone's personality and style of play make such an impact on veterans and this coaching staff as Chuck Demings has. Well, Vikings fans, you don't have to wait too much longer to see your team in action because the preseason game is on Saturday. It's Vikings and Giants. Kickoff is at noon. I know you you you know, Ron will be scrolling on TikTok over here for sure. And uh and of course, there's only three practices left to come see your Vikings at training camp, but they're going to be good ones. What do you think, Ron? >> Yeah, the Ravens no matter who's the coach, it could be hard ball. The same way like the Las Vegas Raiders fans, they've moved from Oakland to LA, Las Vegas, and they're the same. Like there's certain things that remain the same. >> And the Ravens >> and the Ravens defense has always been tough. And Lamar, I mean, here's the thing. >> We haven't even talked about Lamar Jackson coming to town. That's what's cool to me. Like to watch Lamar Jackson operate, see how he plays, like he's a former MVP, has a chance to win another MVP this year. Derrick Henry, one of the biggest, best running backs. You just ruined Derrick Henry's NFL career because he rushed for 395 carries that season. They won a national championship and he said that would take time off of Derrick Henry's life. Well, >> he's now headed into I think it was 10th or 11th season and he's in the top 10 of all time NFL running back. So, he really is. It will be a fun practice, but for the linebackers, they're lucky there's no full goal because that would be a long practice to have to deal with Derrick Henry every day. >> Well, if you want to hear some of those names, make sure you visit vikings.com. title: Minnesota Vikings Team Press Conferences | August 13 | 2026 Training Camp
text: What's the feeling getting ready to potentially play in in a somewhat real game? >> Uh, honestly, you know, we we never take take these games lightly because, you know, it's still in a NFL game no matter who's out there. So, you know, it's it's the same feeling that that I go through throughout a regular week throughout the season. So, I'm take taking it very very seriously. I don't know how many plays I'm going to play, but, you know, every every rep counts for me. >> How have you kind of approached this camp and how do you feel it's going for you personally so far? >> Uh, honestly, I feel like camp is going good. But uh I've I've kind of approached this as like you know what can I uh get better on from from last year and then I kind of went from there and then I'm just just trying to apply it dayto day. >> What's it been like playing working with Jamal Adams new guy in the group and and sometimes coming in and out of your position and >> honestly working working with Jamal it's a lot of insight like very very smart guy like I asked him questions uh like he he's been you know the highest of highs you know what I'm saying? So I just want to get get to where he he was. So, so I'm constantly asking him questions and then he's giving me me points as well. So, it's been great. >> Excited to go play an opponent this weekend. Uh, tighten up those details and it's always fun when you can, you know, go hit another opponent after hitting uh your own guys for a couple weeks. >> Yeah, I mean, it's not a game week. I guess it is a game week. How do you approach a preseason game? >> Uh, I treat it like a game, exactly like a game. Um, you know, I think it's important that you prepare for any game the same way. And when you're preparing to play a long season, you want to have a routine. And this is part, you know, dialing your routine in. done and we're going to be doing during the year. So, it's uh it's important to prepare the right way. >> And well, Kevin Kevin's talked about how you guys are mostly going to get out there and play most of the starters. Just do you feel like you're physically capable of going out there after missing a couple days? >> Yeah, definitely. I feel good to go. Um no problems, just, you know, a little uh little hiccup, but we're all good. >> Okay. And what are you most looking forward to seeing with Kyler out there, most of the starting offense out there? What are you most interested to see just how you guys do? I >> was just excited to see us cut it loose. You know, I think it's uh it's time we go out there um you know, play with no fear. Um go out there, do what we're meant to do. You know, we train all all off season um all training camp, and it's time to go, you know, show what we're all about. Um you know, there's still a lot of growth to go, but it's, you know, a step in the right direction in terms of going to play another opponent, seeing some other guys for the first time to uh you know, prove to each, you know, yourself and your teammates, you know, what what you did all offseason. >> What's your guys' confidence right now in the run game? I know it's been such an emphasis this camp. Just how are you feeling about it? Uh, you know, the, uh, I feel great about it. You know, I think we have a great plan. Uh, you know, the way that we've trained, uh, all OTAAS and all summer, um, the run game is going to be fun this year. So, I'm looking forward to it. >> Until you got to camp feeling like you had anything to prove or it's just business as usual this camp. >> Um, it's a good question. Um, I think I don't know if it's you prove it to anybody else, but you want to prove to yourself, you know, um, you what you're doing all those, you know, long training hours for all summer, big all the sacrifices you make to be in this position. Um, you just want to prove to yourself that, you know, um, everything that you did is worth it. Um, and and it is like you're very lucky to play this game and, uh, you want to do it at a high level. You want to do it for yourself, your teammates, uh, you know, your family. You want to you're proud of the name on your back, your jersey. You want to, you know, show your parents, you know, it was worth it, you know, taking them, you know, all those college visits, all that stuff. So, uh, yeah, I don't know. I I feel like there's always, you know, kind of something to prove to yourself and being the person that you want to be and the player that you want to be. >> He's like a chess master when it comes to this defensive stuff and I love playing in this defense. >> So, what does he how does Brian Flores challenge you the most to get ready for the game, whether it's the the game plan, the plays he's putting on your plate. How has he made you a better player? >> Uh, by challenging your mind. Um, when he sees something, a little hesitation, he's going to be like, "Hey, you got to you got to get here. You got to get there." You know? So that's definitely good that he challenges all of us like that because it's only going to make us smarter football players. >> Defensively, I know you guys look at the depth chart. I know you look at the big board and see the talent you have on this roster. What is this defense capable of in this season? >> Man, I this this sky's is the limit for us honestly. You know, we just got to keep trusting the coaching, keep trusting our technique, and we can go as far as we want. >> First taste of preseason action this weekend. What are you expecting to get out of Saturday's game? >> I'm the best version of this team. you know, it's everything we've prepared for, you know, up until this moment. And so, um, we go into each practice playing like it's a game. So, us going here that it's just another day in the office Saturday. It it isn't anything that we're expecting from this game other than come out, be the best version of ourselves, and the results going to be the results as long as we laid it down on the line and executed to the best of our ability. >> Seems like you're becoming a fan favorite and somewhat of a team favorite already. How do you embrace that spotlight and kind of stay humble within yourself and kind of take it to the next level so fans know who you are? Really >> just hoping everyone gets to see God through me. You know, I have a purpose which I believe is everyone's purpose and that's to hear God and express his heartbeat. So within doing that, you know, fan favorite comes, team favorite comes, but it's being that every day on and off the field at the locker room, away from the locker room. And so looking in the mirror, if I'm able to continue seeing that man that shows up through this building on this field, that's what keeps me humble. That's what keeps the joy and the happiness and it just keeps me fulfilled because it's not me. Like even talking to the mic right now, it is God, you know, he gives me the allowance to do it. He gives me the grace to do it. And so that helps me keep that helps keeps me humble. >> Where did your belief in God come from and all this positive spirit that you have? Who instilled that in you at an early age? >> It was It actually wasn't instilled at an early age. You know, my parents took me to church. We all Well, our whole family went to church. You know, but I didn't have a personal relationship with God. You know, I'm a kid. I'm just going cuz I had to go. And it was actually a specific date, April 14th, 2022 when I was a sophomore in college. You know, I had broke down in my room crying. Felt I had no direction. Even though I was blessed with a full scholarship, but it was just personally I wanted clarity over my life, you know, and the things that God was doing. And so cried for about 10 15 minutes, man, and was just asking God why. And after that, I wiped my tears and said, why not, you know, why not be in this position? And so from that day forward, I decided to not live for me and live for everyone else, serve for everyone else and find hear God and express his heartbeat. And so within doing that, I found my own personal relationship with him. Not only that, I was able to let him use me as a vessel, whichever way he needed, whether it was through adversity, whether it was through triumph, whether it was through congratulations, or whether it was through tears, you know, I just allowed him to use me in every phase of my life possible. And I've just accepted it for what it was. So, that's where that started and that's what continues to happen day in day out cuz every day I wake up, it's a spiritual warfare, you know, between you can't serve two kings. You either serve God or the devil. So, it's a choice I make every second with every breath. >> Last question I have for uh last question I have for you. >> What would be your message now to the younger Charles that was in that room in that dorm room that broke down about how things can be better if you just see it through? >> You don't know what's on the other side of a committed yes. If I was able to go back in time and talk to my younger self in that room crying, that's what I would tell myself. You don't know what's on the other side of a committed yes.

I I try to be very very calm and chill about it and kind of get out the way and and go about my business, but I'm a big believer of being a chill forgiver. You know, they they said it in the Bible, being a chill forgiver. You You got to be a chill forgiver and I give when I feel like it's on my spirit to give and that was one of the moments that I did and I kind of got the way and she she found out who I was in the parking lot and I thought somebody was chasing me at first. I looked behind me like, "Whoa, what's going on?" And she was like, "No, I'm sorry. I found out who you were. I just want to I want to I want to get a picture with you." And I was like, "Okay, cool." I was enjoying myself. Next day I'm in the facility. They're like, "Bro, you're going viral right now." I'm like, "For what? What I did?" I was scared for a second. I'm like, "What I What I did?" So, it's a blessing just to see people see that see people like us we do good deeds all the time and we don't just we don't need praise for it. I'm not going to say we don't deserve it, but we don't need praise for it because that's what you're supposed to do. So, it's a blessing. >> Is there someone in your life that kind of taught you that or that you saw and kind of wanted to emulate your own way? >> Man, I'm I'm so favored and so grateful I come from a very loving family and they always teach us like you give like give you give. So, >> First week First week you've been in here, what do you feel like are your strengths and what areas are you trying to work on in this level now? >> Um I feel like my strength is my is actually my strength. title: Everything We Learned From the Saints Joint Practice Against the Jaguars
text: All right, so we had some questions. We had legitimate real questions about a lot of things after 11 days of training camp. And today is day 12. And the Saints just practiced with the Jacksonville Jaguars. And there were three big things on our list. Could they score in the red zone? Could the two-minute offense start executing? And three, is the defense for real? Let's put a little question mark there just just because. Just because it's needed. Those are the three big questions. Well, they scored four touchdowns in the red zone today. Two by on Tyler Shuck throws a third that was nearly caught. A one-handed grab by Chris Ave. Foot on the line. Scratch it off. Two-minute offense. Saints get the ball at the end of the practice. They go down the field. Shuck spikes the ball. Charlie Smith comes out, hits a game-winning field goal. Defense gets like six sacks throughout the practice. Chase Young said he had six on his own. They get an interception. There's a bunch of pass breakups and they hold strong all throughout the session, which is a good thing because we've been wondering what's been going on with the offense and maybe the defense is just playing way better than anybody expected it would. Does that take all those things off the list? Not necessarily, but it takes them off the concern list for right now. And that's where the Saints are at. So, I guess the question is, are the Saints actually good? We're going to talk about that more on today's episode of New Orleans Football. What a day. Best practice we've seen the whole entire year. So many questions at least partially answered or not unanswered, which is important. There are things that you need to see and you need to see them sometimes. You don't need to see them every single day, but at some point we needed to see the offense just kind of go off and dominate a practice. And today we did against a really good Jacksonville team. So a major positive that we are going to get into all the layers of it on today's show which is presented by Loft 18. And Loft 18 has four locations. If you want to watch a team play on a Saturday or a Sunday, that's the place to be. All four of their locations. Got 30 TVs. And if you're going there, do it in the car they got from my guy Matt Bowers. Best car dealer in the whole world. And of course, we're coming to you from the Ashner Andrew Sports Medicine Institute podcast studio. So, let's get started out here. Camp Review presented by PJs. Huge day for the Saints. Incredibly important day for the Saints. Let's preface this by saying nothing is as good as it seems and nothing is ever as bad as it seems throughout training camp. So, right now you might be saying, "Hey, where's the Super Bowl this year?" I'd say pump the brakes on that. And if you were somebody that was like, "Oh my god, everything's a disaster. Burn it down." Pump the brakes on that. I think we saw an important piece of information today, but honestly, it's just another day. And I'm not trying to sound like a coach here right now, but I've been around enough of these things to know that not everything means everything. Now, a total disaster probably means more than a good day. And I'm not trying to be Debbie Downer here. I'm just trying to keep it in perspective that as good as they were today, they got to do it again next week against the Cowboys. Then they got to do it again against the Rams. Think of it like a game. you know, you see a team win a game and play great, it doesn't mean they're going to play great every week, but playing great one week might mean you can play great the next week. So, in that sense, it's a very important step. And I am more positive on this team than I have been at any point this summer because they did go out there and they did do it against another opponent. And it it really was like going down the list like red zone two minute off the list. Defense looked great. Tyler Shuck looked great. Chris Ave looked great. Jawan Johnson made plays. Devon Bailey looked great. Most importantly though, the run game against a Jacksonville run defense that I believe was depending on whatever metrics you want to look at, you could say number one or top five, whatever you're valuing. They were one of those groups last year. I think they allowed like 85 yards a game or or something like that last year. And the Saints ran the ball well today. Now, there were a couple things, you know, I think there was some stuff with the offensive line that could have been a little bit better. Obviously, um there were a couple plays where there's a guy in the back field and the pass still goes off. I'm more interested in evaluating the passing game right now. I I just kind of feel like the offensive line has the guys and they're going to be good and you still look at it through that prism. We're going to talk more about the offensive line stuff, too. So, I'm putting the pause on that. Um we're doing a another video with with Tron. He's breaking it down. We're going to get together tonight after I'm done with this and talk about all that. So, I'm going to let him go off on the offensive line and share his thoughts on all of that. I thought it was fine. Look, you run 90 plays, like there's going to be a few um that don't show up positively within there. And um you know, it's just kind of the way it goes. But I thought they were really good today. Tyler Shuck had an excellent practice. Um, we needed to see it and the red zone was the biggest part for me and he hit a really good throw to to a great throw to Devon Bailey. There was a throw in the back corner of the end zone to uh Bryce Lance where he went up and and caught it. It fell out of bounds, but boy, the throw and the catch on that were great.
