I feel like we been in the classroom just working on you know little things that we can get better at. >> How excited are you just to get out get some preseason action too and also what do you want to work on? What do you want to get out of that >> man? just to get out there and just play ball, just to, you know, you know, feel the real life game atmosphere. Uh, be in the huddle with my guys, you know, have the clock running down, be out there in front of the fans back in Metife. Uh, just all the the things of real football, you know, not two-hand touch or thud, you know, just to feel the feel the game again. >> Frank Reich told us last week that he thinks that physically you're in your prime. Do you feel like you're in your prime physically? >> Yes, I do. Yeah, I feel great. Um, I feel like our uh our strength staff, our training staff, they've done a great job at preparing all of us, not just myself. And uh, you know, hopefully I can I can keep it that way. >> Said yesterday the offensive offer to start. Did you guys discuss that meeting and today did you feel any differently about how you guys started? >> Yeah, I think um, whenever you go to practice, uh, football in general, there's going to be ups and downs. That's just kind of how the game goes. Uh there's es and flows and the main thing is you got to be steady throughout. Um good things happen, not so good things happen, but you know, you got to stay calm. And I think that's what happened. You know, no one bad than an eye yesterday. Uh we didn't start as fast, but we finished strong today. I feel like we started a little bit faster and, you know, made some plays throughout the day the day. Um I think overall we just got to keep getting better and just stay focused. >> How do you feel about the two-minut drill there at the end? Uh yeah, I feel like we could have made a few more plays, but overall it was good work. >> Out of Kane as he's, you know, gone through OTAAS and now through training camp, now he's going to have a chance to play game on Friday. >> Man, I think the world of Kade, I think he's uh, you know, he's he's he's learning. Um, he's making plays out there. You can see the talent. Um, you can see it. It's it's evident when he's on the field. I think his process is great. He's doing a great job of picking up the offense and going out there and executing. Um I I look forward to seeing him play, you know, some live action, but I you know, I expect him to do well. >> C I'm curious your thoughts on just Isaiah Williams and just how he's performed throughout training camps. >> Yeah, I mean Isaiah's like that he's a dog, man. Like I mean, and to keep it short, man. Like just the way that he works, he's playing multiple positions. Um when he gets the balls ball in his hands, he is uh a special player. And that's something that again, we want to make sure that these guys, you know, all of our, you know, assets are able to touch the ball and do what they do well. But, um, you know, Isaiah is one of my favorite players, man. He works hard. Um, he doesn't complain. He just goes right in there and does his job. >> You've obviously known Todd for a long time. Did do you know his son Junior? And he was a coach out there. Did you get to >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Uh, it's great. you know, seeing seeing everyone growing up, you know, it's uh reminded me of, you know, I'm getting older in this league, but uh you know, coach Coach BS has always been a great coach. Uh he was good to me when he was here, and I have a tremendous amount of respect for him. Uh it's also good to see his, you know, his son out there coaching with him. I know that's uh got to be a special feeling for him, and um you know, that's pretty cool to see. >> What did you think of uh Jeremy's catch over the top during that two-minute drill? >> Yeah, that was that was spectacular. Um, you know, he's a guy who's been making plays all camp. He's a guy who I think highly of and I think he's always going to, you know, be be there for us. He's like a safety net. You know, all the tight ends have done a great job at getting open and making plays. And that's something that we, you know, we appreciate from those guys. Uh, they're they're kind of like the Swiss Army knife. You know, they can do it all. And, uh, you know, I appreciate a guy like Jeremy going out there and making a play for me. >> Start with questions for Gary. >> How y'all doing? >> Good. how you uh how do you think these last two days went uh joint practicing with the Bucks? >> Um they went well, you know, just to get that that environment and that that level of competitiveness in a training camp practice, it was good for us. I know we got a lot out of it. So So um with that in mind, I feel like it was good. >> J says everybody's playing on Friday night. Just how excited are you to kind of get back out there on the field? >> Yeah, I'm excited, man. Just um have it feel real. Everything about it will be real leading up to it and then get that game-like atmosphere. um get get prepped up for a game. You know, it's been a while for me, like I like I said before. So, um I know I'm looking forward to just getting back in that head space and and um kind of kind of prepping myself for what's coming in a few weeks here. You know, >> how much did you miss that? >> A lot. Missed it a lot. You know, I grew up my whole life playing this game, loving this game and and um all a sudden you're not able to play and you don't realize how much it really meant to you. So, you know, I've always known, but it it kind of just humbles you, brings it back into you. um into perspective. So, I'm just happy to be back healthy, feeling good, and ready to go this season. Man, >> we were talking to Sean Jefferson yesterday and he said he thinks you become more of a vocal leader this year. He's noticed difference in you. Is that something you've thought about? Is that something you wanted to do in your fifth year? >> Um, no, it's just more just feeling comfortable. You, you know, you you feel like when something needs to be said, you got to say it. You know, you don't want to miss your moment. you don't want to, you know, miss a chance on on success because we feel like something didn't didn't didn't get said when it needed to be addressed. So, uh maybe just getting older and having a better idea of what needs to be said, what what can't you know, I'm never going to be that that vocal guy to the extent of uh I don't know, someone might like to see it, but but when I do think there's something that needs to be said, I feel fully comfortable saying that. And um you know, and hopefully my teammates respect what I do enough and how I've been to to respond to it. So, you know, that that's just comes with time and and I feel like I'm there now. >> We've seen Isaiah make a lot of plays here. [clears throat] What have you seen from him difference last year to this year? I mean, obviously, he didn't have a secure spot last year. Now, he looks like >> he's pretty good. >> I mean, just that comfortability level, like, you know, there was a a diff an edge to him when he got here. You know, like you kind of said, not knowing what they were going to ask out of him. And and u I'll just say he hasn't lost that edge at all. you know, some guys might get comfortable once they know they they're spot a little more solidified and and they get, you know, named a team MVP like Isaiah, you know, stuff like that might get to someone's head. In Isaiah case, it did the opposite, right? And um I think that says a lot about his character. Um and and just about the way that he goes about his business every day. He's a one of the most consistent guys I've ever met. You know, just comes in, same energy every day, practice- wise, G, let's ride today, let's go. Same thing every day, which I appreciate the hell out of. and and I know all the teammates do and and um it doesn't surprise any of us to see him just going out there and making plays every day because that's just he's a playmaker, you know, whether it's on the field or or in the film room. He's he's bringing value to the team and, you know, that's kind of just what we uh what we know him as. >> What have you seen out of Ken so far, you know, from OTAAS to now? And obviously he's going to get a chance to play on Friday. >> Yeah, I mean just confidence is the main thing I would say with him. uh from day one honestly I was like man he's he's he trusts his uh you know his training his arm to make some some throws where it's like man wow you know and and uh you know we actually kind of grow up down the road from each other so uh we got to sling it around and you know he he he's a really cool dude you know he just kind of gets it um the quarterback the way of quarterbacks in the league he's he's like a a carbon copy of what they I feel like they would put out there's he's got it all And so I'm excited to see him every day feels like he gets a little bit more comfortable, a little bit more um just knowing the speed of things. You know, it's his first time going against another defense and and I feel like each rep we saw him grow, but man, he uh he definitely flashes and it's fun to watch him. >> Just as a quick follow on that, is there a fine line between, you know, some some young quarterbacks come in thinking they know everything and you know there's a they have to be confident in that position, right? Is there a fine line between, you know, being a guy where the veterans look like, hey, dude, you know, you know what you, you know, or somebody that has the confidence that you believe in, if that makes any sense. >> Yeah, I think it's more of like everyone hopes to build confidence level to where you could throw or or make that catch or go for anything, right? He kind of came in with it and then it's like, all right, let's see how it works out for him, I would say. And and he's made some special throws, man. Some that you're like, oh, oh, oh, don't, you know, and oh, good, good ball. like he's had a few of those and it's um I don't know. I don't really know how to answer your qu. I feel like there is definitely a fine line. I don't know. I never played quarterback. You know, the ones that are not at this level. So, for me, it's like you got to be confident to play that position at a high level cuz cuz you know, us on the outside, us at up front, we all want you to be confident in what we're doing. We're confident in what you do. So, it's just a I don't know. But I I feel like he's he's confident and and it rubs off on the group he's in there with and the receivers know that ball can go up at any time. So they're running the route a little bit like looking up for the ball because you he you he g you know he might give you a shot at it and that that's cool to see and it's uh it's been fun to watch and uh he's probably one of the best ping pong players I ever met. >> We'll take a few more. >> We've seen it's it's actually pretty routine here in practice where a team period ends and you and Gino get behind together while the second unit goes in there. What are you guys talking about when when you're going back there and how's the chemistry growing between you guys? >> Um just just trying to clean up things that we might have missed on throughout practice. You know, we're we're uh >> we're still early in this thing. We feel like we're in a good spot, but but there's always something to be cleaned up on. So, there's some plays that show up throughout practice that we want to, you know, get each other's two cents on or hear what he's thinking, the way they're guarding me, whatever it may be, just so that we do have a plan when when Sundays come. It's never too early to start getting those reps having those conversations in. And um you know, we learn how to beat the look. attack the look. I like to just say win the look now, no matter what look it is. I think that translates into the season versus just go by the script of the plays and just run through, you know, no, no, how do we find a way to exploit this whatever whatever they may be in and and those are the the kind of conversations we're having and and uh Gino is just like super cerebral. So, um you know, it does a lot for me knowing what he's thinking just help me speed up my route, slow it down, whatever it may be. But at the end of the day, my job is to be there for the quarterback and um you know, make plays when when he comes my way and and you know, after practice today, I got to do a better job of that. So, just trying to clean things up, you know. >> Gary, take one. >> If you pay attention to this at all, but during July, like the dead period, ESPN does positional rankings where they talk to coaches and executives and rank the top 10. You had been in the top 10 receivers. This year, you were not. This year, you were dropped down to also receiving most. Do you use that as motivation at all? And do you think people might be overlooking you after, you know, you had a kind of had a weird year last year with the injury? >> Um, I mean, honestly, I think a lot of things, right? And and I think other people do, too, right? So, everyone entitled to to their opinion. I I think um, you know, it's my job to to make it in inevitable, undeniable, and and um, you know, I look forward to the opportunity to do that this season. But, uh, bro, I think a lot of things, you know, I'm my job is to go play ball and, uh, you know, maybe whenever I'm done, y'all will know what I think or something, but until then, you know, I don't I don't really care. You know, go play ball. My teammates, they know they know what time it is. Um, that's all that matters to me, you know. I appreciate it, though. You know, thanks.

title: Geno Smith JOINS Training Camp Live | Breaking Down Jets-Bucs Joint Practices
text: This is today with a Wednesday morning workout here in Florham Park. The Jets and the Buccaneers will meet Friday night as the preseason opens up at MetLife Stadium. Aaron Glenn and company taking the field today against a Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers. And football is a kid's game as we saw a couple of youngsters out there getting in the mix. You love to see that. The Jets and the Buccaneers nearing the preseason opener. Welcome in the training camp live. Eric Allen alongside Quincy Enunwa. We are presented by Honda. Today a lot of situational work, a lot of stuff in the red zone and practice ends with a 2-minute situation on both sides. >> Yeah, yeah, it was exciting. I think you always love to see those 2-minute situations. It was an end-of-half situation where, you know, the the Bucs did a good job of driving down the field. Then on the opposite side, they put in a lot of pressure. And that's kind of been a theme of today is that the Bucs were willing to to throw a lot of pressure to show their pressure looks, practice that against the Jets. And so, the Jets want to figure out, "Okay, how do we make sure that we prevent that on Friday?" >> Yeah, Baker Mayfield, he showed why he's been a such an effective quarterback the last three seasons starting uh with the Bucs because in that 2-minute situation, he had more than a minute on the clock. It was 10-10. He had the ball at their 32-yard line. He quickly marched down the field 68 yards and throws a touchdown pass. >> Yeah, the Jets had an opposing view, right? They were more so uh depending on their pass rush to get to the quarterback. And we saw David Bailey get back there, and he got back there a few times throughout the day. I think on the other side, though, the coverage was easy for him to read. And when you give Baker that much time, you give him an opportunity to find some of his favorite targets. >> All right, coming up, we're going to hear from Geno Smith because he's going to join us right here on set. With that being said, offensively in that 2-minute drill, a little bit on even. There was a drop there uh from Braelon Allen. There was a penalty. There was a another drop. Jets were not able to establish rhythm. >> Yeah, I think all ultimately though the Jets were going out there just practicing some of the stuff that they want to do throughout the season. You saw Garrett Wilson kind of static in one spot. That's not something we're going to see throughout the season. So, I think when you come out today, you got to take it with a grain of salt knowing that it's going to be so much different. You're going to see Garrett Wilson being able to move around and not have corners sit on him with with coverage over the top. >> Yeah, and I thought all in all Geno Smith again a very accurate day >> Yeah. >> at the office. There were a couple incompletions out there that may have been drops and we saw him throw a couple touchdown passes in seven-on-seven work and then one in team as well. I thought he had a solid afternoon. >> I think so. I even even the pass that we saw uh I think it was either the two-minute or one move the ball period where he throws to Isaiah Williams. It was a great pass, right? Just a little bit out of his reach, but I think the timing is what you like to see, right? Step on that back foot, get that ball out there, and they're they're going to hit that in the future. >> All right, let's hear from Jets head coach Aaron Glenn and then on the other side you're going to hear from Geno Smith. >> Really good uh day of work. Um obviously we have some situational work. A lot of red zone, going in two-minute. Um It was a battle against a good team. It was it was a intentional to get a two-minute against this team. Uh Baker does a really good job in that situation and I won't say exactly how our guys operate in that situation. So, um It was two good days. Two really good days. So, looking forward to the game. Um looking forward to some of our young guys go out there playing and see exactly how they've improved. Um and then we'll go from there. >> You're watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen alongside Quincy Enunwa and Jets starting quarterback Geno Smith. Geno, how much are you guys going to benefit from these two days of joint practices with the Buccaneers? >> You know what? I think we're going to benefit a ton. Um Coach Bowles he's always, you know, had a good team and had a great defense and um they're a team that's perennially perennially been in the playoffs. Um they've been in the playoffs every single year. Uh, they always have a good team and they always produce and so we feel like having these two days of work, um, is going to make us a better team. We got a lot to learn from and a lot to get better at. >> Yeah, um, you know, I want to kind of take it back a little bit, right? I think obviously we played together. It's been 10 years since you've been here, right? And so you think about you're a Jet, Danny, you're a Jet now. What's one thing that you feel like you appreciate more now than you did before? >> Man, uh, so many things. I can't just name one thing. I appreciate standing here next to you, man, seeing your progress. Um, the last touchdown I threw in MetLife was to this guy right here and, uh, it was all his work. I didn't do any of the work. It was all his work, but just the camaraderie with the team. Um, just being around the guys in the locker room, uh, being the elder statesman now, being a veteran, being able to share my wisdom with the younger guys and help them elevate their games and become, uh, pros. Uh, that's something that, you know, I really believe that's the reason I'm here. You know, Demario and myself, we talked about coming back and really, you know, helping this team establish itself again and so I'm I'm I'm really, um, happy about being here and I look forward to, you know, each and every day, each and every opportunity. >> What did you think about today's practice overall? A lot of situational work out there, a lot of red zone and then we saw you guys finish with some two-minute work. >> Yeah, I think, um, overall, you know, there were some great moments and then there were some moments we can learn from and I think that's the reason for these practices is to see where you're at and where you can get better. And, um, you know, that's the best part about it. I I saw guys making plays all over the field. Uh, a lot of a lot of great plays were made, you know, on the outside, a lot of good-looking runs. You can't really tell because it's a third practice and not tackle, so, you know, a 5-yard run, it could be a 5-yard run, a 15-yard run or a touchdown. You know, um, it just depends on how we how we run the ball, but I thought that the spirit was there, competitive spirit, the competitive effort and, uh, great situational situational work, as you said. >> Yeah, definitely. >> Frank Reich, I was talking to him about you the other day. He said, "Geno, wicked smart." How quickly did you pick up the system? >> Mhm. >> You know, um I study I study hard. I study every single day. Uh I'm tedious with my note-taking. Coach Wright is a great teacher. We have some great teachers, uh Coach Musgrave as well. Um I think the offense in itself, it makes sense, right? So, it's it's easy uh to pick up and learn. And then just the amount of repetition we we're getting out here on the field, in the classroom, the walkthroughs. I think uh AG has done a great job with the schedule so that it's it's really, you know, helping us helping us all. And for me um I don't like to brag on myself. You know, I'm just one of the guys and I'm just learning as we all are. >> Yeah, I'll brag on you, bro. Uh don't worry about it, man. Listen, I remember 2015, man. We were out in Miami. We're out in LA. And every time we're out there, man, he always helped me out. Like I Miami, I was a young guy. I didn't have a lot of money. So, he helped put me in a hotel. We were working out. All right, that's where I really learned work ethic, right? Going out there, working out with him. We had Antonio Brown out there. All right, so I see it today, right? But I think outside of opportunity, something else has changed for you that's really shown the maturity of who you are today. What do you think that's been? >> I just think um you know, experience, man. The more experience you get in life in [snorts] sports, the better you are. And and that goes for all of us. EA, I'm sure, you know, your first time doing this, you know, there's a lot that you learned over the years and you gotten better at. And so, as long as you take the right approach, and that's something that I I continuously do. I bring my mind every single day. I bring my you know, have the right attitude when you walk into the building. Making sure that you're here for the guys. And just be one of the guys, man. That's just what I'm here for, just to be one of the guys, help lead and when it when game day comes about, that's when I bring that fiery competitor out. But, you know, as of right now, man, it's just about learning. >> How do you weigh risk reward? Because I've enjoyed watching you thoroughly throughout camp because you make them defend every blade of grass. There is no throw on the field that you cannot make. And you're not afraid to throw it vertically. With that being said, you've talked about, "Hey, listen, one thing that I want to cut down on is the turnovers that I had last year." >> Yeah, you know, some things are out of your control and you have to understand when you're making decisions, right? The decisions I make not only affect me, but everybody in the franchise. And so, that ball is most important. But, I know that I'm a sound decision-maker. I know what I'm looking at on the field and my teammates trust me, my coaches trust me. Um if something doesn't go right, you know, everyone doesn't know what happens, but you know, at the end of the day we move on, right? You have to have a short memory. Um when it comes to being aggressive, I believe in myself, I believe in my arm, I believe in my teammates, and I believe we're going to make the plays when it when when it's time to. >> You you spoke about it a little bit before and Quincy and I were taking in practice. Bowles, we know he's going to dial up the heat. The different pressure packages, how did you guys handle them, you and the offensive line over the course of these 2 days and what can you improve upon? >> Yeah, it's all communication. It's all communication and you know, it starts up front with the center making the call, the initial call, and then the quarterback has the trump card. And so, that's my favorite part of the game is, you know, going up against those really good D coordinators. I had to do it against AG for so many years and I love that. You know, they're going to bring certain blitz packages and with film study, with communication throughout the week, we'll have a plan. I thought we handled it great today. Um we weren't a lot of free hitters, weren't a lot of free guys, and we get the ball out of our hands and and we see what happens. Let our playmakers make plays. Uh you know, but you know, all in all, man, we just got to make sure we put the guys in the right position and that I get the ball out of my hands and make the right decisions. >> Yeah, speaking of playmakers, man, you guys got a lot, right? Not just at receiver, but also tight end guys are making plays. Yeah, Johnny Woods is showing up a few times, right? Running backs are making plays. How excited are you for that? >> Super excited. You know, uh it makes my job a lot easier when I got guys like that, guys like Q. You know, throw them a little dump off and they take it up they take it to the end zone, man. Like, that's something that I enjoy about playing football is seeing everyone succeed and um we have a lot of great guys, as you said. >> Yeah. Man, you are so competitive. Um what's it like when your head coach says, "You know what? Everybody's live in terms of playing preseason games." Is that something that you welcome? That like, "Hey, listen, anytime we're playing, whether it's preseason, regular season, get me out there." >> We could go play in the parking lot right now. I love ball. I love ball and I'm going to play it until, you know, until I feel like I can't anymore and God has blessed me with the ability to keep going. So, when coach tells me to go out there and play, you know, I'm front line, I'm ready. >> Yeah. Yeah, um how is the rookie coming along? Uh Cade Klubnik and how are you helping him out because you've been in issues before. If it feels like not too long ago. >> Yeah, I know. >> [laughter] >> Uh Cade's doing a great job. He made some tremendous throws out here today and he's been making them all camp. Um he's got a great skillset. Uh he's super smart. He's picking up the offense. You can tell he he understands football and um he's only going to get better as we go. >> What do you think in terms of once you're able to get Kenny Yeboah and C.J. Uzomah on the field as well. You mentioned the tight ends and we can go up and down the list as far as the playmakers you guys have. You know, you can speak about the options and how unique that guy might be in the National Football League. >> I mean, just in the few practices I've gone with them, um he's made plays and you can see just how dynamic he is um with the ball in his hands, with his route running and his blocking. Um I think he's going to be a special player, man, and um he's he's in a great room with a lot of great guys who are going to teach him and and show him how to be a pro, but he's already well on his way. >> So, we got to get you out of here with this one. Do you like being called the OG? I can't believe dudes are calling you the OG. That's what Pre-Season referred to you as. >> I guess, you know, >> I guess I'll take it. I'll take it. >> Geno, thank you so much for joining us. >> Thank you guys. >> New York Jets mini plans are on sale now for the 2026 season. Choose between the green or white plan to lock in the same great seats for four exciting matchups at MetLife Stadium. Get yours today at nyjets.com/miniplans. You're watching Training Camp Live Quincy Enunwa. All in all, two days of, as Aaron Glenn defined it, good work. Is that what we saw out there? >> Yeah, definitely. I think it was a lot of good work. I think the biggest thing is that they were weren't running their stuff, right? They weren't running to say, "Okay, we're playing against the Bucks." Because that's not what matters right now. This is still training camp, and you still got to know the basics of what you're going to be running during the season. And so, you saw them running some of those basic things, and guys were executing when they were were supposed to. >> Who's popping out here for you when you watch the Jets? >> Uh when I think about the starters, cuz it's easy for me to go offense, but I'm going to go defense here. And I'm really liking what I'm seeing from AZ Thomas, right? You're talking about a guy that's playing out there. Um I've continued to talk about him, but he's locking down the the Bucks players. And in the times that they do make some catches, it's really not his coverage, right? A lot of times it's cover two, some of the situations where he's playing in the spot that he needs to play. But when it's man coverage, he's locking down, and I'm excited to see what that looks like during the season. >> Man, I'm really glad you mentioned AZ Thomas, because that's one of the training camp battles that we're watching. Him, Naquan Wright. Wright banged up a little bit at the beginning of camp, and hopefully, DeAngelo Pounds and Kenyon Siddique are nearing returns. I know Aaron Glenn said recently that he thinks Pounds is getting close, and we saw them on an adjacent field today, both Pounds and Siddique running. So, that's a positive thing. >> Yeah, definitely. And then, you know, when I go from starters to the some of the guys in the underneath, Jordan Clark is another guy who I've seen the last couple days. Uh every time I look over the defensive field, I'm seeing him covering guys, I'm seeing him being in the right position. Right? It's a tough safety room. There's a lot of guys competing and battling. Right? We still have Malachi Moore in there, who's also trying to make some some noise as well. So, that defensive side is is is going to be a good battle this year. >> So, David Bailey, I don't know. Do we call it a quiet day? Because he had another sack. I mean, when when he doesn't have three or four sacks, we're saying, "Uh well, Bailey's kind of quiet." No, I'm kidding, but he's impressive. And as Tom Eades has said, this is what you expect. He looks like a number two overall selection. >> He absolutely does. Every time he's out there, you notice him, right? Even though it's quiet, he's still making subtle noise, right? Where he's right behind the quarterback, he's beating his man, right? And those are the things that frustrate, and that's why we had the fight last yesterday, right? He's a continuing to show up, and I think it's exciting for this defense because when you marry that pass rush with the coverage, it makes it so much easier for the guys in the back end. >> And Breece not only is an edge, he plays with an edge. After one of those plays, he's barking back and forth with Baker Mayfield. And other thing that really impressed me with the Jets rookie is that he's out here well after practice working on his hands with the bags. >> Yeah, definitely. He's finding a coach, and he's willing to ask the hard questions, right? The things that he needs to do to develop, and that's something you love to see from your rookies cuz some guys come in a top player, and they're like, "Oh, I already got this, you know, I'm going to rely on what I already know." text: afternoon. All right, on the injury front, Inman he didn't go, he'll be day-to-day. He has a foot, he'll be just fine. And there really good news on on Stiggers. title: Marcus Mbow & Tyler Nubin | Giants Player Profile & Projections | 187
text: Welcome to Giants Nation player profiles and projections. I'm your host Bobby Skinner here with my co-host The Football Guru, and today we are starting with Marcus Bow, the 6'5 300-lb 23-year-old swing tackle. The Giants drafted him in the fifth round last year. He had a very impressive preseason. He started three games as a rookie, but he had six games where he played the majority of them. He showed off things that we knew he was good at, struggled at things that made him slip in the draft, and he enters year two still playing only the offensive tackle position, Guru. >> Marcus Bow had a fast track to the tackle position last year filling in for James Hudson on what was a pretty brutal drive. I think in week two against the Cowboys is when he really started to insert himself there. Played left tackle for the majority of his snaps, only one game though in week nine he played right tackle, which I think might be like a little bit more he's more comfortable, not necessarily protecting the blind side. Marcus Bow is something that you and I got a close look at in Mobile actually, and there were questions then about whether he was going to move inside and where he felt most comfortable, and he was pretty adamant that he felt comfortable on the outside. The buzzing kind of around the attendees who represent all 32 NFL teams were kind of talking about whether or not he would move inside. That question stuck with him a little bit when he was drafted by the Giants, but they never moved him off of that tackle position like you said. >> Yeah, there's so many things I love about Marcus Bow, but there's also we'll talk about like length and strength where it's like, man, that's those could be those might be just prerequisites that he doesn't meet or is not meeting right now. But like like I said, I mean, he started three games last year against the 49ers, Raiders, and Cowboys, but he played almost all of that first game against the Cowboys, which was his best game by the way, too. The second half of the Chiefs games and then 65% of the Vikings game. So, he played quite a bit. Uh as a rookie though, like that first game against Dallas was really good. Gave up a quarterback hit and pressure. So, not like a perfect, you know, shut out game, but like he he played that was legitimately really good film. But after that, you know, he for the season in those six games that he played gave up three sacks, 11 quarterback hits, and and 12 pressures. Uh and that was like, you know, his final college football season, three sacks, one QB hit, 21 pressures. So, like it wasn't like he was a a shut out guy in college, either. I mean, that those numbers last year much as we may like Marcus Bow, we're 88th out of out of 90 offensive tackles in pass blocking efficiency, right? Like out of 90 guys who played, so that's every team's starters, a backup, and some change, he was, you know, bottom three in those efficiencies. And this is where we'll talk about Bow and his long-term thing. This is where that alarms me a little bit more is the fact that the defensive end he kind of got very lucky in his the matchups that he got. Like these were the defensive end uh triplets or pairings that he went up against in his time. Sam Williams, Dante Fowler, and Marsha Neely. Next game, George Karlaftis, Charles Omenihu, and Ashton Gillette. Uh the 49ers, Sam uh Oke Ronaldu, I don't know how to pronounce that, Keion White, and Mekhi Becton. The Vikings, Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel, which was his, you know, that's actually good competition, but you remember they stopped throwing the ball in that game. Uh the Raiders, Malcolm Koonce, Tyree Wilson, and Takkarist Hemingway. And then the final week, Jadeveon Clowney, Sam Williams, and James Houston. So, like that's as bad as a favorable as a defensive end match as you get. And to then put those numbers on top of like it's hard to like sell like, "Oh man, he was great as a rookie, and we can trust him." But the issue is, or not the issue, the thing is is like I do have some trust in Marcus Bow because of all the things that I like, but it's hard to also justify my trust in him with those numbers against that competition if that makes any sense, which it doesn't. >> Well, let's add just a little bit of context to this. We're we're talking about five games in which he played left tackle. This is a fifth-round draft choice in his rookie season playing left tackle. I mean, you're not really expecting someone to come in and put up, you know, shut down lock out numbers. Um this is a guy that was already being talked about in January and February as possibly moving inside down in Alabama. So, this was not somebody that you drafted that you would think rookie season would play six games at tackle and would put up shut down numbers. He had to play had to play a little bit early because Andrew Thomas was not ready for week one and James Hudson was downright awful. Um and then kind of came in and uh spelled injury. What his job would be as a backup tackle and you would hope that he wouldn't have to do this too much as a rookie either. Maybe one to three games in your rookie season. You want your your backup tackle to be in there. Um not six games. That's not really ideal for your backup tackle in his rookie season. But I I think it's more so that when Andrew Thomas goes down and couldn't play in that Dallas game, that's not the reason why the Giants didn't win in week two. In fact, they nearly won for a myriad of other problems on the defensive side of the ball. So, I think the context is knowing that Marcus Bow is supposed to be able to go in and not look disastrous and I don't think that he really looked disastrous. The numbers aren't great, but there are definitely parts to his game that absolutely need improvement. Whether it's going to be one to three game spells or a whole season at right tackle or something, there are things about Marcus Bow that he needs to improve on in order to play the tackle position or anywhere else on the offensive line. >> Yeah, and that's I guess it that's where it's a little bit of a eye test of like, yeah, those numbers are disastrous, but it's just he didn't feel disastrous. Now, when when we're talking about him eventually being like, hey, can he be a best five guy? Like, you have to can't that can't be the bar, but right now as a swing tackle, I I have some confidence in him because it's like because it's the power thing, it's not like, hey he doesn't get out of his stance. He doesn't know what he's doing, mental mistake. Like cuz he has all of that going well. The reps are very similar and it's hey it's power and guys attack that inside shoulder and win against them, but it's not a make you look stupid type of bad. Uh and that's where like I have a little bit like I we'll talk about like his position and I just am in the camp that I wish they would have tried him on the interior this year. We'll talk about that, but where I do have hope for him is the fact that I never thought he could be left tackle, you know what I mean? And not only did I think he could would be a left tackle in the NFL, he didn't play that in college at all. He played two years at right tackle, one year at right guard. He played zero snaps in college at left tackle and then like you said, 81% of his snaps as a rookie now weren't just at hey you're playing as a rookie and you got some size and strength issues, but now you're playing left tackle. And that's what gives me hope that I do think that he could become a solid right tackle eventually. It was the the Giants smartly could not go with him as the starter this year, whether it was Jermaine Eluemunor or somebody else being that guy. But I'm I would like to see him move into the inside at some point, but I'm also it's not the worst thing in the world of a fifth round pick is developing at right tackle and then maybe in year four like he gets an opportunity like you know he he shows enough to where we give him that actual opportunity. >> Yeah, and I mean that's the ideal scenario. Let's keep the optimistic view in mind. If if everything goes correctly by the year three, year four, you have a guy who's fighting for a spot at right tackle. He's 25 years old by that point. You've got yourself into a good position as an organization because he's not going to command a whole lot of money on the open market either. So, that would be the ideal scenario. Let's talk about his actual game though. In the passing game I think he's an athletic mover. He handles speed with natural ability, active feet, and he can recover, but only really with quickness. I'd still think that his footwork needs refining. There's times he gets a little crossed trying to react to what's going on in front of him rather than being settled into his step. Um the biggest problem, and we've alluded to it, is the anchor is just completely non-existent. He plays squared up and with decent pad level, but the strength in the lower half is just not there and guys can run right through him. Um he and I also think that his hand work is pretty good. He doesn't wait to punch. The punches could use some more strength, but he does get that hand out there quickly. In the run game, it's just the lack of power. Again, he squares up very very well, quick to get head-on-head, and he keeps his legs churning, and he plays with some decent power level. There's a little bit of lean in there, but again, that goes back to the lack of power in general. He looks best to me on combo blocks and walling off defenders to open holes, which kind of sounds like an interior sort of thing if you if you lack strength. >> Yeah, like like you mentioned the pass game, it's like, you know, the footwork, like you said, can be a little like wonky, but like one he's playing left tackle, and that's kind of part of his game where he changes up. So, it's like he kind of tries to keep the rusher off pace. Like he said, he uses his hands well, he understands angles, closes space, but again, it's just guys just are able to work speed to power, right? And he And the well as he uses hands, guys are able to get their hands on him first, and he's not able, like you said, to anchor. In the run game, I I actually like them quite a bit in the run game. Like you said, it's because it was so much of like, hey, he works combos and angles well, he gets off to the second level, you get him as a puller, he gets to the spot, he'll finish. Uh he keeps his feet driving upon contact. Like Like you said, with lean, but like I I you know, I'm okay with my guys leaning a little bit as long as they're not totally off balance. Where you said like Where I saw losses in the run game, like against the Cowboys in that final game, like he get like a match up with Quinnen Williams, and Quinnen Williams just bench him off him, and that's a conversation we could talk about when we talk about position-wise, but it's like I I like what he did in the run game, right? It's the you know, run game could be very mental for offensive lineman and he's got so much of that going on where he changes up his hands you know, or you know, he you know, knows how to rework his hands and stuff. So, there's so much to like about him. But again, it's just looking back at his rookie last year, I was just like man, it's just there's so many things that you like, but it's just guys able to attack his inside shoulder. It happens a lot. Um he doesn't look as comfortable at left tackle, which we talked about, but um which going to lead to sacks around the corner, but it's just it really does come down to that. It's a basic thing and it's he can get stronger and get a little bit of it more of an anchor, but it still could be something that plagues him. And again, I swing tackle this year that's this is the best I've felt about swing tackle for the Giants in a long time. Uh you know, and I'm and that's including you know, James Hudson who got paid last year where like this is bad. Like I don't care that this contract shows like you're taking it serious. I don't think this player is taking it serious. Um but there was there was two thoughts with with Bo. It was number one, let him train the entire off season be the swing tackle, right? Get a lot more work at left tackle. Um but do not let him be the starter, right? You need to you know, either uh resign Ereck Flowers or fill that right tackle spot. Or uh option two, which it was letting him spend the off season working at guard and center. Um and we could talk about like this the strength is obviously a concern there too. It doesn't go away, but I think the the length paired with momentum that edge rushers produce is where he gets in trouble and there's less space and speed on the inside. Um so like yeah, guys on the inside are strong, but they're not getting that speed. They're not always getting hands on him or have the length advantage the way that uh defensive ends do. title: Giants QB coach Brian Callahan assesses Jaxson Dart’s first training camp under John Harbaugh
text: What um how is Jackson doing with learning this offense? >> He's in a good place. I've been really pleased. A lot of new information, a lot of new things. Fun scheme to practice against. You know, a lot of different stuff that you have to handle from a quarterback perspective. So, very pleased where he's at. Does a great job with the recognition, communication, all the things that you want from a process standpoint. He's been he's been spot on. So, every day is is growth. There's new situations every I know you guys have seen that coach does a really good job of hammering home a lot of these situational points that sometimes aren't very uh skewed towards the offensive success. You know, for some long periods and things of that nature, but it's been great. We've had a lot of fun and it's a really good room, too. Those guys have been awesome. Jameson and Brandon, too. So, pleased where we're at. >> What is the next step for Jack? uh you know until we get to I haven't been in battle with him yet. You know that'll be my my first time going into it with the season coming up and hard to say you know based on we all know where he needs to improve from last season. We'll see where he's at when we play but uh I think he's made a bunch of strides from technical standpoint from from footwork to how that fits within the system and what we're asking of him from uh you know the play action game under center game and then protection scheme and all that stuff. So, I think it's been good and and we'll see. You know, I think every every week is going to be a growth process for him and I can't wait. I'm excited about it. The biggest stride that he's made since you started >> um it's hard to hard to put a a label on the biggest thing. I just I think he's continually gotten better um with everything we've asked of him and I think he's playing calmer with his feet in the pocket. I think his his eyes have gotten really good. Um, the footwork discipline and the footwork uh trying to give the word to best describe it just like the smoothness of it I think is has really improved. So that's been been good to see. You know, it's it's the hard hardest position to play in sports. I think it's so cool. Like if it's creative, is it aggressive, is it what what you've seen working with him? How would you describe what Nagy wants to do with an offense? >> Yeah, he's definitely he's definitely aggressive. Um he's definitely you know, wanting to create explosive plays and I but I think the big thing is is he wants to always stay ahead of the sticks. So, there's a lot of tape out there, but for those who don't know, how would you describe your game? >> Dependable. Um, longevity, man. I' I've played 57 games at center and I'm still rolling. And, uh, I just I try and approach every day to be a pro, you know, learn from these guys, like I said, Jurgens, Landon, Steen, >> guys before us like Kels. Um, just being dependable, man, and just attacking every day. You know, never know when your last rep is, so you just got to make the most of every opportunity. Can you talk about your technique a little bit as far as how you counter a guy that's maybe 290 295 comparatively like a Jordan Davis that's 320 330 and how you differentiate that at center regard? >> Yeah, I feel like you know with the guy who's bigger, >> right, >> you got to get your hands on him quicker and then you got to be ready for the counter on the inside bull rush stuff like that. A guy who's 290 may be able to set off the line a little bit more and kind of dictate his rush. You know, is he going to go pick the tackle? Is he going to set you up inside and get picked by the end? Stuff like that. So just being ready with your hands, adjusting on the go, and then, you know, just play ball. >> And how much has it helped you going against those guys each and every day in practice? >> Dude, I this is one of the best fronts I've ever played. Uh, you know, it's tough, but also at the same time, it's fun to go against guys like Jordan Davis, Jaylen Carter, Moro Jamal, Byron Young, Ty Robinson, Gabe Hall. Those guys are here for a reason. And, you know, being able to go against them, sorry about that, every day, it it's uh it's a blessing in disguise. It just it makes you better as a player. When you talk about going from center to guard, I think I think Willie I'm not sure how much guard Willy's played. I don't think Drew Kendall played a ton of guard before. How much does it help having other guys kind of making that same jump and learning guard? >> Yeah, we get to kind of feed off each other, you know, uh what's worked for you, uh this is what's worked for me, stuff like that. And just to kind of build that camaraderie of, hey, this is something new we're learning, but we can do this together. It's a pretty cool feeling. How have you and Drew pushed each other in year two? >> Uh just holding each other accountable every day, you know, showing up whenever, like I said, training camp, dog days, you know, what we're in day like 14, 15, I can't even remember. Uh just kind of be each other's ear like, "Hey, let's let's go attack the day. Let's make the most of this day. You know, there's no reps out there that, you know, we're going to take the playoff like this." Every rep means something. So, >> Drew, how you feeling being back and and being here on a consistent basis after, you know, everything that you went through last year? >> I feel good. Uh, I mean, I worked hard to get to this point, so just trusting what I worked on and just glad to be out here to be honest with you. So, I feel good. >> What was that process like working your way back? >> Uh, I mean, it was it was tough, but you know, I managed to get through it. Uh, I mean, just focus on what's important, which was what I was dealing with. So, I mean, it was easy and rough at the same time, but now I'm kind of glad I got through that. And now I'm just, you know, glad to be playing football again. >> I don't know if you're don't know if you're playing on Sunday or not or Saturday or whether you'll say, but uh we've had guys talk about coming back from injury and what it's like going back. Have you thought about what that might be like? And is it sort of like a will that be the final moment you kind of put everything behind you and move forward or? >> Uh, no. I've already put everything behind me uh to be honest with you. I feel like, you know, out here I feel comfortable out here. uh despite what I have going on. I feel comfortable and I've already put everything behind me. Just focus on what's what's next and what's in front of me. >> Playing center. >> Uh I mean I don't I'm going leave it up to the coaches. Uh you know my job is to play football. So I'm here to play whenever they call home. >> What have you seen from Michael Carter? >> Mer has grown a lot from from the time he started to now. Uh flying around making plays. Uh you know he got a nickel background so guy I can cover. Uh so man he's been doing good. Uh caught on pretty fast. So I'm glad glad got to see that from Mike. What was your angle of uh if it was a fight at the end of practice? What do you think about things getting physical there at the end? >> I ain't to I ain't even I ain't even see the fight. Uh but I mean this it's practice. Uh we physical going to get heated sometimes, but standard day we a team. So I mean I didn't get to see the fight, but >> to put that into perspective for normal people who don't play football, how common is that? >> Uh I mean very common. Uh I mean we're grown men at the end of the day. you know, your tensions might arise or, you know, but at the end of the day, you know, we going to take care of each other. We're teammates, but it's going it's going to happen here and there. I'm pretty sure y'all seen it a lot of times, a lot of places. So, it's going to happen. >> What are the second steps in year two that you've tried to address with or Vic has tried to address with you in this system? >> Uh, just getting comfortable uh and just just growing uh just, you know, trying to see how much I've grown from last year. Trying to remove the mental errors or the little things that I was struggling with last year. And I feel like seeing that just me progressing. Uh so I've seen that a lot. A lot of things I struggled with last year. Feel like this year I've overcame and I'm playing more confident, more faster. >> What have you seen from Darius Cooper? How has he grown one year one year two? >> Uh I mean he's grown a lot. Uh obviously, you know, going from year one year two, but you know, same mindset for him, same guy in the building, uh coming in ready to work, uh ready whenever his name called upon him. Uh obviously a hard worker. So I mean, he's grown a lot, but you know, same same mindset for him. He hasn't changed not one bit. attacks every day like you know >> is going in the 10th >> after missing like this season. Are you even more excited to get back out there and play this game >> Yeah, definitely. I'm more excited. Definitely excited. Uh I mean obviously I missed a lot of it and you know I've been itching to get back. So now now it's time and our football is back around. So definitely excited to get back on the field. >> So it seems like when you were talking about steps to year two it's a little bit more recognition of what's happening on the field. How in the offseason was a lot of film prep? Like what kind of steps were you kind of taking? >> Uh I mean in the offseason obviously with I had my injury and everything I couldn't really physically do that on the field. Uh but you know I definitely kept my head in my mind in that playbook. I watch a lot of watch tons of film. Uh obviously it's all I could do. So did that a lot and I see it paying off. >> Some players have talked about access to like VR kind of things. Is that something that you had access to? >> Uh yeah we had a little bit of that. Uh, it helped a lot, but you know, just watch I feel like watching tape is really where it's at. I feel like you get to see a lot and watching tape and, you know, seeing what's going on from yourself and obviously the opponent, too, but you can learn a lot from watching tape by yourself. >> So, all that time you spent watching tape, you said like you see the payoff when you're back out here at practice. How do you see like how does how does it feel different? >> Just just play recognition. Uh, just letting the formation talk to you. Uh just seeing the little tiny cues where that the running back is giving you the online run passes just little things that you know feel like rookies might struggle with uh just coming in and just having a lot thrown at you and trying to manage playing and doing good. So feel like I will overcome that. So just trying to you know just focus on the small things. I feel like you know once I stack those and eventually you know the big result going to come. So just feeling to like know that all that time wasn't wasted that it actually like it's helping you now. No, definitely definitely knowing that time was I mean time is important. So knowing that that wasn't wasted and now I've invested that much time into that you know feel good to see it paying off a little bit. >> At what point did you regain full confidence and in in your injury? >> Uh I mean I can't I can't really give you a particular time. >> It just you know just naturally happened just working on it just naturally just happen. How much of a role have your teammates played in, you know, really kind of making you feel comfortable and confident back and forth after an injury? >> Uh, I mean, they played a huge role. Uh, I feel like especially at the safety position, you know, we got to have a good communication. Uh, we got to have a good relationship, good bond, I feel like they translate to the field. So, if I can trust the person, you know, next to me, in front of me, inside me, then I can just focus on my job and not have do nobody else's job. So, played a big role. Dick talked about some of the safeties have calls the board uh in plays like kind of like linebackers do. Is that the role you have? >> Uh like defensive calls, checks or communication like you're kind of just >> n they get the calls and linebackers. I don't I don't I don't I don't wear earpiece. So like the linebacker linebackers get the calls. You >> mentioned going into year three, what's different about your game? Um, you know, uh, finally just getting the jitters out. Um, you know, learning more special teams. Like high school and college, I didn't really play special teams as much. Uh, so feeling more, uh, you know, prepared for that going into the season and more prepared of, you know, learning a, you know, a new playbook, stuff like that, and getting the reps down. >> How do you get rid of those jitters just simply by reps and things? >> You know, being in those situations, I feel like I'd never been in those situations before. Like I was saying earlier, the special teams, the fullback stuff, the running back stuff. So now I'm kind of, you know, know what to expect and uh go from there. >> You were dealing with something in the spring that that had you out. What were you dealing with and how how hard? >> Yeah. Um I had a little hamstring soreness. Um you know, it kind of set me back a little bit, but I knew that um you know, I'd have a little off time in the summer, kind of prepare my body and uh get back. So I feel great now and uh you know kind of excited to show myself >> in terms of pass you have a pretty good reputation doing that. >> Yeah. What's the kind of the key success? Um, you know, early in my career, that's another thing I kind of struggled with. And, uh, you know, learning from guys, um, from the Chiefs now to the Eagles and, uh, kind of watching reps over and over and over, um, has really helped me to, you know, kind of focus on not over jumping, uh, you know, when they're doing making moves, you know, knocking hands down, stuff like that. So, I feel like that's really helped me kind of excel from there. >> You mentioned some of the fullback stuff. Are you completely in the running back room or do you have to like bounce around a little bit? Um, so usually here they've kind of had the fullback stay in the running back room, but uh, you know, honestly, wherever they need me is where I'm going to be. Uh, kind of I always tell myself, you know, my career kind of being like a Swiss Army knife. Uh, just basically doing anything, special teams, fullback, running back, anything where they need me. >> You've been in preseason games before. What's your approach in those? >> Um, just like I was saying earlier, treat it like any other game. Um, you know, this is kind of where I can show my talents. Um, you know, we haven't really, you know, had tackling or, you know, kind of had thud practices, but this is kind of where you showcase yourself and go from there. >> For a player like you, is that even more important? >> Oh, yeah, 100%. You know, especially being an undrafted guy, coming into a new team, you know, you really have to, uh, you know, showcase your talents and express yourself, you know, going into these preseason games. >> How do you feel about the fact that that your physicality shows up with when the pads and lock? >> 100%. And, uh, you know, I'm big weight room guy. um love that type of stuff. So, you know, I feel like that's really kind of when I can show myself is when the, you know, the pads come on and we actually get, you know, physical contact. >> How do you go about staying patient when you aren't getting so many reps? >> Um, you know, that's where the mental side of the game kind of comes in for me. And [music] like I said before, you know, playing all through high school, all through college, I didn't do that. Um, so it's really kind of helped me to stay in the iPad and, you know, walk through the, you know, just the little stuff, you know, even when you're not getting as many reps has helped me. What's it like working in the room with Parkdale, >> man? Uh, you know, I used to I don't want to make him sound old, but I've been watching that dude for a long time now. Um, you know, it's just it's amazing to kind of see it every day. Uh, you know, sometimes people take it for granted, but, uh, just watching him and all the success he's had and now being, you know, him as your mentor, uh, being in a room, learning from him, and, you know, it's really helped me. >> What's he like as a teammate? >> Um, you know, that's the one thing I wish people could see. Um, you know, not even as a football player, he's just a great dude. um just you know outside of football talking about life, talking about um you know how things are going, stuff like that. So he's a really great dude. >> Carson, how would you describe the dynamic, the overall dynamic of the running back room? >> Um you know, I'm very excited about it. Uh this is one of the, you know, best running back rooms I've ever been in. You know, I've only been in a few of them, but just telling from, you know, not even Saquon from, you know, Tank, Will, um you know, JJ, another guy we've had come in. Damen I've played with before at the Chiefs. Um very excited. all great running backs and uh you know definitely something I could learn from each one of them. >> What do you like what do you like about Jamal as your position coach? >> Um you know he's he's a great dude and he he understands running backs like he you know he sees when a hole is not there when you have to bounce cuts. Um like we were saying earlier the pass pro, you know, how he kind of teaches us getting our hands inside. So just little key details that he's really helped me and my game and all the other running backs.

title: Nick Sirianni on Week 3 of Training Camp
text: Nick, back in you were outlining the receiver position and you had mentioned that Darius Cooper uh kind of grouped him in a bucket with Johnny Wilson as a dirty work role kind of guy. Do you think he's graduated and deserves more playing time on offense for the kind of training camp? >> Oh, there's still a lot of time left. Uh he's having a good camp. There's still a lot of time left. Uh it's about being consistent on a daily basis. He's done a good job being consistent on a daily basis and uh you know he's he's makes some really good catches, really elite hands. Um and we know he's tough and things that he can do and but I've I've been pleased with where he is. >> Saturday, >> sorry, >> who's starting at quarterback on Saturday? >> Yeah, we're still we're still thinking through that. >> Nick, on Saturday, speaking of the quarterbacks, when you're not game planning for a preseason game, obviously, what do you look for from the quarterbacks to say this was a good outing? you know, a good showing. >> Yeah, you want every it's not just a quarterback thing, Elliot. This is a this is something you're looking for for each and every position. You want the operation to be really smooth. Um, you know, and it's it's first run for our coaches, too. You know, we've we've do things at practice, obviously, but this is the first time in a game setting we're able to do that. So, you want the operation to be really smooth. You want everyone to be really clean on their assignments, and you're looking for good fundamental football. I think that's not any different than how we treat practice on a daily basis. I think it would be crazy to say, "Hey, now that we're in a preeason game or now that we're in a game, this is what's important." Now, it's our daily habits. And so, it's going to be a lot of the same stuff we look for in practice. Operation obviously becomes a little bit different there. Um, but again, we want all our guys, we we talk about detail. We want all our guys playing with outstanding detail, knowing what to do, handling situational football, playing with great fundamentals. We want all our guy >> We want all our guys to play with extreme effort. Uh, you know, and this is some of their guys are going to have a lot of plays here that, you know, that they're not used to having that many that many plays. So, you know, again, with with great effort, um great physicality, and great mental toughness to be able to uh put behind a bad play and and go on and play the next play. And so, you know, anytime you step on the field, like I'm looking to emphasize that in team meetings, um and in offense and defensive meetings where we can emphasize that so we can continue to show, hey, this is what our standard is. And so, this will just be another opportunity for that. And the difference is that it's live to the ground and in a game setting in front of fans. And that should and that's exciting. >> Andy talked about how um not knowing when they were going in between him and Tanner in certain parts of practices was kind of like the real thing in a game. >> Say that one more time. >> Uh Andy Dalton was talking about how it's kind of like a real game where him and Tanner didn't know when he was going in on a given rep and certain you have to decide who's going to start on the preseason game. Are there ways that you can kind of continue what you've been doing there in training camp? >> You're saying in a in a game >> in in these preseason? >> Yeah. Um Yeah. And I don't know if that's just for the quarterbacks. There's going to be, you know, DBs that are backing up uh or have to be ready to play couple different spots, you know, field corner, boundary corner, you know, nickel, safeties. There's we got some guys like that, too. Um, and offensive linemen in particular have to know, you know, hey, I'm an interior offensive lineman. I got to be ready to snap if called upon. I got to be ready to play guard or same thing with tackle. Hey, I'm on the left side, I'm on the right side. So, all those things, you know, are can happen in a game and, you know, we we do those things in practice and those will al also come uh viable in this game on uh Saturday. >> What's today? Thursday. >> Thursday. Is that something you want to do with quarterbacks in these games, preseason games? >> Um, again, we'll see how that all plays out of where we are with with all that, but we're we're constantly talking through, you know, who's playing, how many reps everyone's had, who needs this or who needs that. And that's just a that's kind of a fluid conversation that started the this early this week on Sunday. And, you know, there's been, again, I don't get into it too much because there's constant change through it. Like if I would have told you guys on Monday, I think I had a press conference Monday. Hey, here's who's playing. Like it's just so fluid in that. And um and there's constant little changes going on behind the scenes. And with that, >> you guys, >> this offense historically working in the middle of the field more uh and certainly when you work throw into that area, you're more prone to throw interceptions. Do you have to alter your kind of expectations for how many turnovers you want out of the position versus the, you know, the reward of of working that that part of the field? >> Sure. You you still I we've talked about an awful lot. You want to be explosive and you want to take care of the football. Um my job is to win as many games as we possibly can, not to uh say lead the league in total offense. If we lead the league in total offense, great. We're probably playing really good. But my job is to win as many games as we can and that will always be the goal and we know that part of that is taking care of the football. Um, and our guys know how to do that and have done a good job of that and our and our defense done a good job of getting their hands on some of the ball uh the balls that are out there. So, no, the focus will always be how do we take care of the football and how do we play with great fundamentals while still being explosive. And so, um, no, you're going through progressions of different things and saying, "Hey, uh, yeah, that looked good. He made the right decision on that one and it should have went there and then, you know, and then play it as that." But the the standard is hey take the right footwork as the quarterback if you know go through your progression go the right place with the football and that's going to be that's going to be the standard for quarterbacks throughout time right is is did they make the right decision did they go the right place with the football did they make an accurate throw and that will continue to be the emphasis >> a lot of the offensive linemen the young offensive linemen I mean how big is it for them to get like preseason game experience Saturday. >> Yeah. I think again we're live up front like they're going like at practice, you know. Now the only thing they don't have is when somebody gets they they could get rolled up on still if somebody goes to the ground, but the thing they don't have is like the tackle gets rolled up on. So, we're getting a great We've been in pads, uh, you know, however many days we've been in pads as as much as we we possibly can cuz we're live up front. And so, what better reps to get when you know, and we you've seen that we've done some ones versus twos, twos versus ones. And what better reps to get than against if you're a young offensive lineman against Jaylen Carter and uh Jordan Davis and Moro Jomo and um you know our ends are doing a really nice job and Nolan and Jix and and AK and AJ you know and so um we're getting so much of that good work in practice. Again, this is just I think what what happens in preseason games, the way we kind of look at it is just like, hey, now more eyes are on it, right? You guys get to see everything in practice. We get to see everything to an ex to like and then some by rewatching the tape over and over again, but now more people get to see it. And so, um, yeah, excited for that opportunity >> in these preseason games. >> On that, the live part, your live up front, um, how important is adding in the tackling aspect to evaluate the running game? Yeah. Again, you you see when we go through practice how many tackling drills we do, but the tackling drills aren't to the ground. Um, you know, it's getting your body in position, and that's half the battle, right, of getting taking the right angles, defeating the blocks, putting yourself in position. Um, but now it's going to have to be, hey, now you got to come away with a body part and you got to come and you got to come down with the tackle. And so, yeah, that's that that for those guys, that's different, you know, that's different. Obviously, quarterbacks can get hit now. Um, that's different. Um, and so I would really say, you know, O line, Dline, they're going full goal now. The D line's going to have to take the guys to the ground. But that's a great opportunity for us uh to evaluate how a guy tackles is in this is in this game because now it's live and now you can not only see his approach angle, the way he broke down going into it. Um but now you can see if it's a load tackle, how he he approached that um and how he did he come away and with getting the guy down um which at the end of the day is so important. And then you see, right, the relentless effort of everybody else because if we do miss a tackle, you know, our our philosophy is, hey, we miss a tackle, we got to have eight guys there ready to hit that guy and make him pay for for for breaking that tackle. And so that's going to show up, too. But again, I we've seen the guys relentless effort to the football. We preach that. We talk about it. We we we condition and we show it in team meetings on a daily basis. And so that will be fun uh to see. But yeah, good point. Great evaluation tool for how guys tackle in a live setting. >> Nick, that you're looking forward to seeing in a preseason setting. >> You know what, Tim? I think I'm just looking forward to all of those things that just getting back out there in a in a game day setting. Uh, you know, the process that we go through as coaches, the process that they go through as players. I to say I'm I want to single this position out. I'm I'm just looking forward to watching all these guys play um in a in a game where where it is live, even though I feel like we get so many good evaluation process here with the caliber of our team and our players. Um and so I know I'm dancing around your question a little bit, but I I really to say hey this position over this position, I'm just so excited to see all the guys compete. I mean, at the end of the day, this business is for people that are ultra competitive because it's how competitive it is, and I look forward to seeing that. It's always good to go against somebody else. And so, um, you know, sometimes in this point of camp, you're like, man, I just we just want to hit somebody else and go against somebody else. And so, looking forward to see our guys every every position go against another team and uh and all the things that come with that. >> Preseason games. How do you go about wanting Shawn to get in a rhythm as a play caller, but also not showing your cards too early? >> Yeah, good question. Um, you know, I think I look at it in the sense of anything you don't want to we got to go through our process because that's so critical that we're doing that. And again, we we'll have four or five practices throughout camp and joint practices where we get to practice that and also training camp or pardon me, preseason games where we get to handle that. I think though at the end of the day, anything you don't want to put on, anything you don't want people to see, you can't put on tape because everyone's watching, right? I think back to the 2021 season, we put a couple things on tape and we're like, man, we wish we wouldn't have shown that and it kind of showed up in a in a game uh early on and you know, that's on my notes constantly to talk about that to the guys uh the coaches in particular throughout the first couple preseason games to highlight back to that. I won't get into specifics of what it was, but to get back into that 2021 season of something that that happened there that we're like, man, we wish we wouldn't have put that on tape because, you know, this the couple of the opponents saw that. So, um, but you got to go practice the things that you want to that you've been working on, um, and what your staples of your offense are, um, or defense. And so the guys can go out there and operate and go out there and again play with you don't you're not masking it so much where you're like, um, I'm not running the plays that are our base staples, but you know, go because we want these guys to go out there and execute with high fundamentals, knowing what to do so we can again know what to do. so we can see how you do it and see how their talent shines. So, um I think and I think Dave, you can do that. Like the process of it and the communication of it is so critical too. You can do all that while not showing all your cards. Um if that makes sense. And so that will be our that will be our process through this game. >> Said that they said that Jaylen looks faster running faster. Uh do the um metrics back that up? I guess I know you guys have ways to track that. >> Yeah, you know, I think I think he looks great um in every aspect. I think he's he's when he has to run the ball, he's running it running it well and looks fast and explosive when he's passing it. I think he's been so consistent through camp of, you know, I just think he's getting better and better and more comfortable as each day goes by. Um and I love his consistency right now and I love the way he's playing right now. I'm really excited for him uh in this season and the the things I know that he can do and I'm just just so pleased with how he's attacked everything and man I'm really excited for him and pumped for his you know for this year >> his development can you all play in a game and if so you have conversation with him just because >> who did you say >> you are >> okay >> like can he play in a game and if so do you have a conversation with him just about stadium fans and that aspect of it because it's so different. >> Yeah. Um yeah, he's he's doing a nice job, you know, everything's new to him, right? Everything's new to him and uh but you know, he's he's continuing like like when everything's new, that's a that's a great feeling to have. He's like, man, he can only get better from some of these things. and uh you know and so obviously when everything is new to you I mean everything's new to you you know the the game day process will be new to you as well and so what we want for every whether our guy whether somebody is playing in the game or not playing in the game um we want all our guys to go through the pregame process to so their first time going through it's not game one and so that won't be any different And if that's Squan or uh Zach Bon or you are so you know they're all going to be going through that process. You know your job to in the process is to go through the same routine every time so you're not thinking about the magnitude of the game. Kind of like kind of like the your dribbles on a free throw. You're focusing on that instead of the crowd going wild and all those things when you have to have hyperfocus. And that will be his emphasis and that will be everybody's emphasis on the team. In Tuesday's practice, you finished with Flint sprites. That's not something you usually do. What was behind that? >> You know, we want we we feel like um just being in great You can't play with relentless effort and you can't play with great detail unless you're in phenomenal shape. And so it's just the emphasis, you know, we did some two-minute drives uh that day and um you know, the emphasis there was, hey, we we were going to as we talked in the staff meeting, you know, we said, let's see where we are at that point. Wanted to get a little bit extra work and you can see how our guys attack that. Like our guys know how critical it is to be in great shape and know how hard you have to push yourself there. We got great guys that lead that. And you know, I think sometimes you could be like, you know, I know I saw it at my son's football practice last night. They went sprints at the end and he's like, everyone's like, but our guys attacked it like crazy because they know how important that is and and and that just speaks to the character of our football team of like that just speaks to our character of our football team that it's just like we know how to work, our guys know how to work extremely hard in the time that we're out here. Um, and you know, I I think that was just another good example of it.
