title: Jalon Daniels & Graham Barton on Executing the Offense | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Hey, man. How are you? >> Good. >> How do you evaluate how your offense is doing against this kind of thing? practice >> Yeah, I mean, it's uh it's great work cuz you're getting live, you know, uh live looks. You know, you're getting different personnel. You know, throughout camp, like you kind of get used to who you're going against, you know, you know their strengths and their weaknesses and they know your strengths and weaknesses, so it's hard to always truly evaluate uh yourselves off of uh one on like practice against yourself, but uh coming out against a totally different opponent with, you know, different defense, different looks, different flavors. Um you kind of get to test your test your metal, you know, you get to test one, obviously, your physicality, but, you know, your communication ability. Um you know, mentality-wise, how you come together, chemistry, how you hit combinations. And I think we got made a lot of progress this week. Um these two good days of joint practice. Uh I was really impressed uh with, you know, our unit as a whole. Um I thought we communicated well, you know, having a new offense with uh Zach Robinson and this was kind of the first time we've uh gone, you know, live like this against another team and and and we didn't there weren't a whole lot of issues, you know, schematically and targeting-wise and communication-wise, so I was super pumped about that. >> Have they given you any indication at all about how many how much you'll play on Friday night at all? >> Uh no, I'm not sure yet. Um Yeah, yeah, I mean, you always prepare like you're going to and and we'll be ready, but uh we'll see. >> Two-minute drill at the end of practice, offense scores a touchdown. >> Yeah. >> Defense gets the stop, no points. Can't write it up better than that, huh? >> No, you can't. Um yeah, that was awesome. We were uh you know, we kind of marched down the field, receivers made some good plays. We were, you know, from what I could tell, these protected well up front and um yeah, that's that's what you want for your first uh live look at a two-minute drill, so. >> How difficult is that to kind of like scramble at the end? to look like there was the run play, got stopped, you had to snap it before you know Kate gets to you? >> Yeah, yeah, we didn't have uh I don't know. The the run look was tough, you know, it made it hard on uh you know, our our backside combinations and um so to be able to to you know, get stuffed, get back up to the line, and be able to call a play, get the blocking scheme right, get the snap off, and uh find an open receiver that quickly is not easy. And uh so this early in August to be able to execute like that is pretty cool. So uh definitely a a good building block for us. >> It seems like this rookie class so far is getting along well. Just how impressed have you been with them as a whole with Reuben and Josiah and guys like >> Yeah, yeah, super impressed. Obviously, you guys all have, you know, seen uh Reuben and and what he can do and his just uh mentality and stuff. Uh Trotter's another one of those guys who's super physical. Definitely makes us better as an O-line going against guys like that. Um yeah, and they've been, you know, it's been super impressive to see all of them really and just uh the you know, the edge them and even the free agents, you know, that have come in. Guys like A'Shawn and Anzalone and Nacho. Um just like that defense is just playing really physical and I think you saw it out here in joint practice, you know, I didn't get to watch a whole lot, but just the the 2-minute drill, you know, there wasn't a lot of time for Geno to get that ball out, which is you always like to see that. So it's good. >> you think about going against Onyemata again? I assume you went against him a lot in the division. Yeah. Uh yeah, yeah, Onyemata is a great player. Um you know, we played him in Atlanta a bunch of times. Him and uh um I'm blanking on his name. 56. Uh Saints linebacker. Yeah, Demario Davis, sorry. Uh great player. Sorry, I forgot his name. Uh we've gone against him a lot in the division and then um Onyemata a lot in the division, too. So, you know, good to see both of them out here. I think they were two big pieces of both those defenses and they'll be a big part of this Jets defense this year and uh they're good players, good challenges, and and great to get a good test against them. Uh go play hard. Like, you know, if you're you're going to probably make a mistake, but just do it full speed, play physical, you know, run to the ball, pick your teammates up. Like, show that you you know show that you want it, you know, and and you know, obviously you don't want to make a bunch of mistakes, but but if you do, just make it be going 1,000 miles an hour and you know, that's I think that's kind of show you belong with the physicality-wise and the effort and execution-wise. That's what I would say. >> What was your perspective on all the fights or tussles, whatever you want to call them the last couple days? >> Um you know, it happens. You know, a lot of joint practices, you see fights all over the league. You know, you know, obviously we're not out here to start a bunch of fights, but we're going to protect our guys, so you know, when guys get cheap shot at our guys go down in a way that's, you know, not what we set as the, you know, the etiquette, practice etiquette and you know, it's going to be handled and you can't just let guys do that, you know, you got to So, I think that caused a lot of it yesterday. I don't think there were any fights today that I recall was a little chippy, but you know, you just you obviously you don't want you want to get better, you know, and you want to practice hard and and you don't want to waste a bunch of time fighting, but at the end of the day you're going to protect your teammates. >> Understandably, it's early, but has anything stood out to you so far with the team, whether it's the play making or team chemistry, anything? >> I just think mentality-wise like guys really want it, you know, obviously we talked about the rookie class and the free agents coming in, but then, you know, what's not I feel like has been as talked about as much is a lot of us were here last year and a lot of us did not enjoy last year. So, I think there was a bad taste in everyone's mouth and the urgency to get better is there and the urgency to win is there and I think you feel feel from the top down. I think you know, that's just you know, not okay no one was okay with with how last year ended and you know, we want to obviously win the division get in the playoffs and make a run at this thing. So, I think the urgency to do that is there. Yeah, it's very valuable cuz you get away, you're in a hotel, there's no distractions, you know, you're hanging out, you're killing time, you know, you're doing whatever you're hanging out with the guys. It's good time. It's fun, you know, you obviously get great work but then you get the you get a bunch of down time hanging out with your teammates whether it's on the plane or in the hotel or at meals and stuff. So, it's a good time, you know, it's a you know, hopefully 10 years from now you're looking back and and you remember the fun stuff about these trips. So, yeah, yeah, you just there's a lot of bonding that goes on a lot of that team chemistry is formed this time of year. No problem. No problem. It's good y'all. Good. Good. >> How would you evaluate yourself just in these past two days of flying with seeing a new opponent? >> Yeah, I mean being able to to adapt to the game, being able to see another team, see another defense, be able to see what they're doing on the other side of the ball, being able to go back home, go back to the telly and watch film on it. I mean that's always great for me cuz I feel like I'm probably my worst critic and even when things are going good outside I feel like for myself I like to see how to be able to find those little things to keep getting better. >> How excited are you you get to play your first NFL >> I wouldn't even say excited is the word for it. I mean it's a dream come true to be able to play at this level playing professional football. I mean I've been dreaming of this moment since since I was a kid. So, being able to go out here and be able to play some some NFL football Friday means the world. >> What did this work with another NFL team across the group for you this this last couple days? >> Um helps you be able to to be able to see like I said see a different defense, be able to see a different structure, be able to see the tempo of other other players obviously. This is my first time going against another NFL team. So, uh just being able to see what they do, be able to see little things that I'm able to key on on film, and just keep on getting better from there. >> How much is Baker just been a help to you? >> Yeah, I mean, a lot. Um there's a lot of different things that we didn't go over in college that you have to be able to know here at this level, and um to have him right there next next right beside of me, be able to ask him whatever question that I want, I mean, it's been able it's been very tremendous in my development. >> Does it help that you have similar games, that both can move well? Does it help in that regard, too, that he's not necessarily a pocket statue quarterback, if that makes sense? >> I mean, just being able to to talk to him about when to be able to get out of the pocket, how to be able to stay within the pocket when the pocket breaks down, what are you going to do, what's going to be your next move, and I think something that we harp on a lot in the in the quarterback room is ball security. So, like, in college, there was a lot of times where you have the ball one hand, and out here, like, these defensive players are out there trying to be able to get the ball. They got to make money, too. So, um just being able to talk to him about those little situations, nuances, and be able to develop from there. >> What did you learn from him on that 2-minute drill? >> Uh I learned that he has a fire he has a he has a fire. He has a fire underneath him, and um he's somebody who goes out there when he has that fire, you're able to see him go out be able to go out there and operate, be able to make every single play. Um and that's I mean, we able to see we able to see that. >> What would be success for you tomorrow? >> Yeah, I mean, going out there and being able to play every single down, uh being able to to make sure I'm focused on the next play. Um I think that's very huge for something that we talked about a lot at Kansas is be able to focus on the next play. Your best play should always be your next play, and even if it's a good or a a play that you don't really want to remember, go ahead and get to that next play, because your next throw needs to be your best throw. >> Is there a part of your game that you maybe haven't been able to showcase just yet that you're hoping to show either in the preseason or the rest of training camp? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously, quarterbacks aren't getting touched out here. So, um a lot of it is just being able to work within the pocket, be able to uh show what you're able to do, obviously, through the air. I mean, we play quarterback, so you want to be able to practice on that a lot. But, I mean, I feel like when the pocket breaks down and the defense does their job of being able to cover everything, I have the unique ability to be able to get out, be able to still try to have my eyes down field, be able to make a throw on the run, and at the end of the day try to move the sticks. >> So, rookie class had a lot of buzz surrounding them. Y'all do a lot of bonding outside the field, I mean, as a class together, things like that? >> I mean, especially when we first got here, a lot of that was I mean, obviously we're in training camp now, so we basically have a schedule as soon as we wake up to when we go to sleep. But, when we first got here, it was a lot of team bonding, especially with the rookies. I mean, this we have a lot of talented rookies out here, whether you're a draft pick or a UDFA, you're able to see a lot of people who are UDFAs going out there making plays as well. So, I think we're we're a pretty close-knit group, and I think that helps us go out there and be able to go out that mindset to be able to help the older guys as well to go out make plays. >> How nice is it to have a big target to throw to, like Tanner Hudson? He balled on that last drive, too. it's great. You're able to have, especially when you have one-on-one coverage with no safety help over the top, you're able to be able to to take that that advantage. Be able to go out there, allow him to be able to make a play, and he's somebody who has the ability to be able to make catches no matter where it's at. >> What did you think about going against David Bailey again? I believe you faced him in college. >> Yes, I did. I don't know if I went against David Bailey today at all. But, I mean, to be able to see him go from from college to NFL, I mean, you're able to see him go out there and make plays, and that's what you want to see. >> What do you think of him as a player? >> Uh fast, twitchy twitchy guy, someone who's able to make plays. I mean, especially when we were in college, he was able to do a lot of different moves when he gets to contact with the tackles, and I think that's what allowed him to be able to make a lot of plays in college. >> All right, thanks, guys. >> Appreciate y'all.

Yeah, let's go to the the cornerback room. Benjamin Morrison suited up for the >> He's in pads. Now, you know, that could be like what Jaylen McMillan did yesterday and they just as Indies they tend to bring them along gradually then like that but I'm not sure why he would have the pad he didn't have the pads on yesterday during warm-ups but he does today which would make me believe he's going to do something in the DBs are right here. Yeah, so good to see him back on >> tuned for that for developments. >> Yeah, absolutely. That'll be something we keep an eye on and you were talking yesterday about the position groups to watch. You wanted to see how the cornerbacks did against some of the Jets wide receivers including their their great star wide receiver Garrett Wilson. I thought the pass defense really showed up yesterday. Um, you know, as as we said, Zion McCollum was out, Benjamin Morrison was out, and so you need somebody to run with the ones opposite Jacob Parish, and Damarion Williams got the call, and he really showed up. And he had the pick six, first big play of the practice, kind of a tone setting play. Uh, and you know, when you look at this group beyond the starters, and also considering, you know, the kind of the question mark about Benjamin, I think Damarion, who has previous regular season experience with the Ravens, I think he could see a legitimate path to making this team, and it can't hurt when you come out here and make splash plays like that. But I thought the defense had a pretty good day overall. >> Yeah. We also talked about Jaylen McMillan yesterday. He did suit up in pads. He did participate in individual stuff, no 11-on-11, but he he is making his way back. >> Yeah, it's just a work in progress, and maybe we'll get a little bit more out of him today. He banged a knee, which hurt, and has him out for a while, but it's not like he has a like a hamstring strain or anything like that. >> You wanted to see the edges against those tackles for the Jets. What did you see yesterday? >> a lot of good stuff. Um, David Walker has to be the story of this camp. He just every single day he's showing up, and uh, I mean, he did it again yesterday. He had several good good reps where he was just getting in the backfield quickly. He He has a good combination of power and speed. He's got a lot of lower body power, and he translate that, you know, that that power, speed to power really well. Um, Reuben Bain had some nice moments in the uh, one-on-one drills. I didn't I'm not going to claim I saw every rep of every defense, cuz there's two, you know, every time there's offense, defense, offense, defense, so you can't see all of it, but I did see some Yeah, I did see some nice reps from Reuben Maye, which is at this point is come to be expected. I think the best 101 rep I saw for any of our guys was Alkha Ke Diabate with a with a really crazy fast spin move on one of their tackles. So, those guys are showing up and that's a big deal for us. >> Yeah, well, we're really looking forward to Friday night, the opportunity to get that first preseason game in and let's preview it a little bit. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn like we said when asked about his lineups, he said, "Oh, everybody's playing including Geno Smith." So, so we do expect to see that from the Jets, but he also complimented the Bucs defense after practice saying that they had quote a scheme that's difficult to deal with. So, that's a a bit of a sign of what they saw in in practice number one. >> what you deal with when you deal with Todd Bowles. Todd Bowles has always been one of the more crafty designers of defenses of blitzes of what you would call I can't think of a word right now, but fake blitzes where it looks like a blitz, it's not really any more than four rushers, but they're not coming where you think they're coming from. And so, that's what both sides wanted from this joint practice was to see looks that they're not used to cuz in our joint practice we're trying to get our defense running our defense. And after a while you see what they're doing. Here you don't you don't know what's coming and apparently that was an issue for the Jets, which is good to hear, but totally expected when you talk about like guy like Todd Bowles' defense that he's got a well-deserved reputation for being a mastermind at designing a play. >> Well, another thing to keep an eye on Friday night of course a big talk in this camp for Tampa Bay has been you got Zach Robinson coming in as the new offensive coordinator, the formations look different, the personnel looks different, but the Jets showcasing a veteran OC as well. >> Yeah, Frank Reich's been around, right? Um I think the thing to keep in mind though there is that this is not only a preseason game, but the first preseason game with at least on our side a lot of you know, bottom of the depth chart players and I don't think you're going to see Zach break out any of his real schemes. Pre as you know, preseason depth offensive schemes tend to be very vanilla. Some pretty basic runs, some pretty basic routes. Yeah, you just don't want to put on tape the thing that the things that you're actually going to be leaning on. So, I don't know if we'll learn a whole lot from it, but from an individual standpoint we can see which players can stand out within the system that we do run. >> Well, the Jets going 3 and 14 last year, they had so many close losses early in the year in that 0 and 7 start. So, it'll be really good battle match up match up. >> It's interesting they like you said they had four of the top 50 picks because they they definitely did a rebuild last year trading away Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. So, the fact that they had all those high draft picks came at the cost of some of their best players and so they are starting over and it is an interesting combination of approaches because yeah, they have all these rookies who should be instant impact guys and hopefully be for them at least become core players, but the free agency moves they made were actually a lot of 30-year-olds. You know, DeMario Davis, David Onyemata. I'm sure there's others that I can't think of right now, but they they did a lot of uh, filling in the gaps with very advanced in their career players that are now mixed in with all these rookies and it's like it's an interesting meld of strategies to see if you can, you know, get back into playoff contention. >> Yeah, so preseason game number one is coming up on Friday. We can't wait to bring it to you live on the radio network. You're going to have local pregame coverage starting at 4:30, statewide network coverage starting at 6:00. title: AJ Barner: "It's Going To Be A Big Year For Elijah Arroyo & The Rest Of The TEs" | Seattle Seahawks
text: I got better vibes today for you guys. Ask me about my teammates though, too. I I said I got better vibes for you guys. >> Starting off, you want to talk about your teammates? The camper is having >> he's balling. >> What do you see out of >> um just doing what he does? Um I think that's what we've come to expect from Elijah and uh it's going to be a big year for him and the rest of the tight ends. So, we're super excited for him and um hopefully on Saturday he gets a chance to show it on a live game. You cut it. >> Speaking of your teammates, just what makes this room so versatile? You guys kind of all specialize in something a little bit different. >> Yeah, I think you said it best. Uh, we have a bunch of different guys that can do a bunch of jobs. Um, and I think that's the tight end position in a nutshell, right? You kind of feed off one another. Um, you pick each other up where you need to. Um, and we have a collection of guys that can do a bunch of different things. So, it's it's exciting to be a part of. >> You got a pretty long pass from Jaylen Noro in that one that one series today. What did you kind of see from him? >> Um, he's looked really good. I mean, he's throwing the ball very confident. Um, I think that's the biggest thing as any player out here. You want to make confident decisions and then go let it rip. And I think Jay Mill is really taking a stride this uh camp. And uh again, another guy on Saturday that I'm stoked for him to just go out there and and show show what he's got. >> How big is the jump from your one year too? You saw that last year, but like having like draft prep off season everything off season coming back after a year in the NFL. How big can that be to kind of recycle kind of makes his rides? >> Yeah, I think it can be huge. Um, I think you just find little things. The game slows down for you a little bit. Um, you know, a bit of a new scheme this year, you know, so you still kind of have to take a step back and and learn everything, but you kind of learn the flow of the game a little bit. You learn how long the season is. Um, and that there, you know, there's not time to necessarily waste and and not get better, but there is time to take strides in your improvement and take a step back and say, you know, here's where I can do different things to improve. >> How close to fully back are you, AJ? >> Yeah, today was a good day. I I'm starting to feel much better. Um, it's been a grind, though. Like, I've really been putting my head down and working hard to get back. Um, but I I would say I'm getting close to feeling better than I've ever felt, which is really exciting. >> Better than before even had the injury. >> Better than before I I got here. I felt like since I got here, I had an ankle injury in the Senior Bowl and that was something that I took care of this off season. So, that's been with me for two years. >> So, that was the kind of the significant thing you had this >> one of them. Yeah. So, I mean, you play so long with an injury that's kind of everything up the chain. It's like the hamstring and so got had to get all of that right and uh really starting to feel my best right now. >> Um I mean it's part of the game. I think some of that stuff is just they have to report it and some of that just nature of the business and the position that I play. Um but yeah, I definitely did have to deal with some things. Um and it was really challenging. Um, so hopefully I don't have to deal with those this year. I guess that's all I can say. But I mean, that's kind of the the the game that I play and um, regardless like I'm going to put a product out there on Sunday that the twelves are going to be proud of and that I'm going to be be proud of. >> AJ, the last time we talked to you, you only had a few practices under your belt and mentioning the good vibes. Do you now feel like you could you could feel that you have a tight end coach calling plays for you guys at this point? >> Absolutely. I just think I I'm kind of out here and just having more fun with it. you kind of get back out here for the first time and um you're trying to learn the playbook and trying to get back on your feet. And there's a big difference between coming out here and just like taking it very serious, but at the same time like not taking it too serious at all and just enjoying your time out here and trusting your instincts and and letting it rip. So that's really what I've been focused on and need to continue to do. >> Even with a new coordinator, there's a lot more carryover in terms of personnel and scheme than when you came to camp last year. Can you sense offense being ahead relative to last year because of that? >> Yeah, I would say so. I would hope so. Um, we better be ahead. Um, you know, like you said, we got a bunch of guys coming back and the urgency is there. The standard that we have is there and um definitely should should start on a high note. >> What has Brian brought in? Not technically, but just the way that he relates to players, ability to communicate. What have you seen from him? >> Um, he's about ball. He's about his business. And I think as a player, you can respect that. He's going to shoot you straight. he's going to um call plays that work. And I think he's came into our building and he's been himself because at the end of the day, that's what we want from from all of our people here. If you come in here and you and you be yourself and you fit into our culture, then uh you should have success. >> AJ, where do you think like personally you can take your game this year? >> Um I think I just need to continue to to to do what I do at a consistent level um and do it game in and game out. And um I will I will do that this year and I'm excited to make that happen. and um I made the strides to do that. >> And back to Milro, like we we know about his legs, but what stands out about it just for him as a thrower. >> Um I think he is a quick release like he gets set to throw the ball and and it comes out really quick. Um and he puts on the right spot, but it's he's got quick draw. He's got the quick draw attribute in his package. you saw the way you bringing from that kind of diverse things. >> Yeah, it's exciting. I think with the multiple personnel groupings and you touched on the different the different guys that we have to use and different skill sets, maybe some routes that are further down the field, different protections, um different motions with them and uh tying in the run game to the pass game out of those big personnels. So, um don't really want to get into too many specifics with that, but I think um it'll definitely be a strength of ours come the season. >> You mentioned Jaylen being maybe more confident this time around. Does that show up like in the huddle and things like that as well? Um, yeah. I would I think so. I think Jay Mill is a guy that's, you know, has that confidence to him. I mean, we all know the the player that he's been. Um, but I can just feel him get more comfortable in the pocket. He's standing in there. He's making decisions. And, yeah, when he wants to use his athleticism, he's going to go ahead and do that. >> Thanks, man. Thanks, AJ.

title: Drake Thomas: "This Organization Means A Lot To Me" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How's it going? >> How's camp? >> Uh camp's great. This is honestly like the best time of the year. You're just, you know, all the way, it's all football all the time. You're with the guys, you're competing, you're getting better. Um in the football world, I feel like there's no better time. >> Got a game on Saturday, that's got to be something to look forward to for the players ready to go hit somebody else. >> 100%. It's an an amazing opportunity to go out and showcase what every we've all been working towards uh for the first time. So, you just put that on display for everyone to see and um just uh it's a huge opportunity. >> You've been the young undrafted guy fighting for a job and it ended up getting you a job here instead of with the Raiders. Like, how valuable is that exposure of the preseason for guys in that position? >> Uh it's huge. I mean, you just kind of said it. Like, that's the only reason I'm standing right here in front of you guys. The only reason I've I I've gotten the opportunities that I've gotten because those preseason games. So, uh when I say it's a huge opportunity, like that's not something small that I'm kind of just brushing over. Like, it's these next 3 weeks, these next 3 games can be life-changing for kids for for young guys in this league. >> Do you think it's still different for you this year just, you know, you feel more maybe a little more established in the lineup and things like that? >> Uh yeah, I'd say more confident just based off experience. But, um like as far as like approach and mentality, I feel like I'm still taking the same thing, the same consistent approach and mentality and mindset that I've taken honestly for my whole career. So, >> You're one of the few guys on this team who has developed and who started starting as a practice squad guy. What do you think of the biggest thing that this organization has helped put develop with players? >> Uh I think they they they play to guys' strengths really well. They they see what um guys are good at and they use those traits. Uh We had a presentation in the team meeting the other day and then they were talking about like what you got to do to stand out in this building. It's like it's really just be really good at who you are and like own that role and do it to the best of your ability. And I think that's so true. Everybody has their own unique ways that that makes them them and I think our staff really utilizes each guy um in correct ways. >> Drake, you had a pretty big year last year. Why change the number? >> Um my dad wore 32. Um since I was little, I always wore 32. I wore it like Pop Warner, um middle school, high school, college. Uh I just I feel like more like myself when I'm wearing 32. >> What did last year I mean like you said, you've always been confident in it. What does a year like that do for you where everyone kind of deep believes they can be that kind of player but to get to show it, become a starter. Like what does that do for you? >> Um I think it just makes you super grateful cuz you see a lot of guys not get that opportunity. Like it's it's rare. You know, there's a lot of guys that come and go through this league who never get that shot. Um that are put in tough situations that you know, they went undrafted but they're super talented but they never necessarily get the the opportunity to showcase or get comfortable in a system or whatever it may be. Uh so it just makes me really really grateful to to realize that's what I where I came from and um I'm just super blessed and I I make sure that I live in a way that I make sure I acknowledge that. >> The five-year contract that you got, I mean did the depth something to >> Say it again. >> The contract that you got, did that kind of ease something to >> Yeah, for sure. I mean I This organization means a lot to me. Just from them claiming me. They they believed in me and then through my injury, they stood by that and they they gave me time to get healthy. They gave me grace during the process of me getting comfortable like getting back to myself as a player. Um so to to be able to stay here and have that in writing for another 2 years, it means the world to me. >> Drake, you talked about kind of you know, young players being themselves in this building. Was there a moment when you got here or throughout the last couple of years where you kind of realized that? Has that kind of come out just being yourself? just over time. Banked reps. I think being yourself like as far as like personality wise like in the locker room, I think the people that we have in there make it easy. Everyone's super welcoming. Everyone, you know, you when your best players are your best people, then that that's what creates a a great culture like that and allows people to come in and be themselves and feel comfortable. There's great relationships in there, you know, the great friendships. So, um as far as being able to come in and be yourself, I think it's really easy with the group that we have in the locker room. >> With wearing number 32, how influential was your dad on you in terms of getting involved in football and the relationship you have with >> Yeah, when I was little, I feel like uh I mean, he played college football at Marshall. Um and when ever since I was little, I loved the game. I loved the sport. All I wanted to do was be like him. He was huge, you know, that that that prototype like male father figure that you would want in your life. Every everything that that he did for me like just sacrificing time, whatever it is, money, um whatever it is, the taking us to trips for for different sports and making sure that we never miss an opportunity to get the most out of something like you know, everything that he displayed to me and showed to me like I just hope to one day do that too for for my future kids. >> Did he wear 32 for a reason or was it just a number he got in high school? >> Uh my family was Steelers fans, so it was kind of Franco Harris a little bit. >> Walmart again. Almost like cliche for linebackers, just talk about the defensive front, but for you and E.J. to play behind the guys you do, like what does that do for your job when you've got >> It makes it a lot easier. Uh Uh me EJ have talked a little bit this training camp and like when those guys are rolling, it makes practice a little bit boring. It's like a weird feeling cuz like you kind of just sitting behind the line of scrimmage and waiting for something to pop out and nothing does cuz everything like the the double teams are being taken like they're come they're getting through they're making plays and it just makes it a little bit boring. So, uh you know, I don't take that for granted, you know, thank them when I can, whatever it is, but uh those those are really good players that we're both playing behind. Thanks. Appreciate you guys.

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: "We Have An Awesome Culture" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Jess how's the I know we talked to you week or two ago but how how do you feel like this camp is progressing for you and the offense? >> It's been going great. Battling with the defense it's always a challenge and you know when you're faced with challenge you know you grow. A lot of good things a lot of bad things but we're just taking the opportunities that we have here day I think tomorrow's like 16 of practice and we're looking forward to getting better and that's what we've been doing. >> Did you see Hard Knocks last night at all? >> I did. >> Yeah what did you think cuz that kind of the scene with you and Cris Carter and >> Uh it was good um kind of relationship that we have you know I appreciate uh those words and um you know we just want to get better. Everybody you know in the receiver room on the offense and me included want to get better each and every day and anytime we have the opportunity to do so you know take full full of the moment. >> What kind of coach is he? Say it again? >> Um I mean he just has a lot of great knowledge of course um very hands-on. He knows his stuff too you know I can trust you know I can trust his opinion and and how he sees things. Um and he's meant a lot to you know my development over these last two years. >> You alluded to it in that scene but how much has the route tree changed the things daily? Basics of the route tree changed? >> Say one more time. >> You alluded to it in the scene last night of the route tree changed? In some what's different or how much of a difference is it? >> Um we're going to continue to grow in in the space of you know putting in plays down and and routes I think right now it's been kind of basic just want to get the fundamentals and basics of our offense down and that's what we've seen a lot and you know as we progress through camp you see a little bit more um and I'm excited about. I'm excited to you know run new routes be creative and and brainstorm with you know, the great offensive minds that we have. >> Is that simply a counter to the counter? You know, teams are going to study you and then >> Yeah, 1,000% you know, just having answers is key to being successful in this league. So, just making sure we have answers for any look we might we might get. >> Was last year the most you had run routes out of the backfield? >> Last year, yeah, it was. It was. >> And what what kind of adjustments what what did you learn from from that in terms of getting used to doing it? >> Yeah, I mean, uh I think me being in a slot a lot of the years and it's it's kind of just the same kind of the same mindset, you know, find the zone, understand who's really guarding you in that zone and um you know, you can take advantage of the defense having linebacker safeties, nickels, um you know, guarding you. So, just taking advantage of that and um you kind of get to see the play progress and see the play develop and then, you know, it's certainly a timing thing with the quarterback. So, um I enjoy it. I did a little bit in college, but last year it was the most I did, yep. >> You've been around Mike McDaniel a couple years now. Obviously, Hard Knocks he's getting a little more spotlight on him and more of the the country's getting to see him. Are you guys excited for people to kind of get to know Mike a little bit better the way you guys did? >> 1,000% yeah, I'm happy he, you know, he can take that off our shoulders, you know, and be the star that he is, you know, um you know, he's very important to us in the building and a representative of the city. So, you know, people want to hear what he has to say and you know, how we, you know, basically the leader, you know, of our team um in this facility get to where we're we're getting to, which is a awesome culture that everybody loves to be a part of. So, I think spreading that and spreading who we are is amazing. He's done a great job with it. >> Has anyone tried to do the sledgehammer uh contest after those guys were gone? >> No, no, I think no. I don't know if well that'll come back at all. I don't >> How do you think you would have done? >> Uh I'm not a fan of it. I'm not a fan of it, you know, a long day of practice, you know, I just want to kind of watch film and chill. >> How has daily life off the field changed for you in the last year? Uh not too not too much, honestly. Just keeping it simple, you know, um like I said last year, I don't I don't need too much, you know, a lot of a lot of this a lot of being here, you know, take up a lot of my time and um just really focused and when I get home, get to chill with family and then come here and get to work. So, really really not that much. >> One more on Mike. Have you with him going into his third year have as a head coach, do you sense anything different about him? Do you just think he's kind of more comfortable in the role or is he the same guy he's always been? >> Mm. You know, I definitely think he's growing and I think our our relationship, you know, and the relationship with people that he has in the building is growing and just understanding each other. So, I think he can dive further in-depth with the conversations that we're having. So, um it's awesome. It's awesome, you know, we preach relationships are everything. So, just in that aspect, it's been awesome, like I said, to grow and um to bring on new challenges together. >> People talk about quarterbacks getting used to different receivers and how they run routes. As a receiver, do you have to get used to different guys when you run route combinations with different speeds, different tight ends, and versus receivers? >> Um in terms of receiver and quarterback play? >> yeah, no, in terms of your the way you run routes, does it matter who you're next to when you're running those routes? Do you have to make any adjustments based on how they run their routes? >> Oh, um I would say, you know, I would say not really, but you got to be able to adjust on the fly, you know, when you you got Sheed next to you, you know, he's a he can fly. So, you know, the windows might open up pretty a little bit more faster with him and, you know, Toy Horton and then when I'm next to Coop, you know, we're playing kind of like a pick and roll kind of thing. Um so, just understanding that, being more patient and understanding, you know, what the defense is trying to do and taking advantage of that. You know, usually when I line up next to to Coop. So, it is different. It is a different mindset lining up next to those guys and I think us being versatile and being able to do a lot of things in our receiver room, you know, just you know, opens a lot of doors for this offense. >> But, Mike has talked about having a little bit different messaging this year as well. Kind of you know, not about to get back but running it forward. And Hard Knocks kind of sort of seen last night where he was talking about how you can't totally change it cuz there's just some new guys who still need to hear the old message and everything. How but how do you feel like he's kind of balancing that? That's right. >> Oh, I think it's been great. Um, you know, like I said, pretty much we have a lot of guys that were here from last year that seen the start of the culture but we have new guys like you said and they have to understand how we got to meet our goal, our ultimate, you know, team goal. And so, they have to understand that but like I said, this is a new year and and relationships are everything like I said. So, we get to expand and grow that message and you know, who we're about. So, that's the that's the fun part about this thing. >> There's been a number of plays this game where you've had like a deep throw coming your way and it looks like as the ball's on the way down you gear down slightly and then you speed back up to create separation. What what was like the origin of that maneuver? >> Yeah, really just um just control. Just just having enough control and um calmness just to, you know, put the DB where you want, you know, um when the ball's flowing in the air sometimes. You know, you have to make something happen to create space for yourself um to make a clean catch and then run with it. So, really just that and I give that testament to, you know, the drill work that we do, you know, every single day with, you know, Frizz and um Ricky White actually just being comfortable in in uncomfortable situations down the field. So, um that's something that we work on. >> Ricky White particularly good at that? >> He is. He is. He definitely is. Has a great calmness, great knack for the ball, has great hands, and and that's something, you know, we both want to grow at, and and I want to pick his brain on things. Excellent player. Um that pushes pushes me, and I would say all the receivers, you know, to be on their their game, cuz he definitely is on it. So, yeah, just working with him and and getting better. >> So, you're learning from him? >> Oh, 1,000%. I want to We have Our room is Our room is top in the league. We're looking to be the best in the league, and the people that we have in our room, you know, I I greatly respect. You know, when it Y'all see Montario out there every single day. Cody White always making plays. Jake Bobo does his thing all the time. So, there's room for improvement from for all of us, and to learn from those guys. It's It's a pleasure. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, man.

title: Leonard Williams: "We Have To Climb The Mountain All Over Again" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's up? What's up? >> Good. How are you? >> It's pretty good. My wife takes care of it for the most part. I kind of just uh enjoy the fruits of it. >> Literally. >> Is there any fruit there that you're growing? >> Uh tomatoes. Yeah. >> It is. >> Did you Did you watch our >> What's that? >> Did you watch our >> uh I haven't been able to see it yet. We're we're pretty much showing that we are attacking a problem and not a person. And um it kind of get freedom throughout the whole building uh to go player to player, player to coach, coach to player um and just help each other get better and and figure out that you know winning was the ultimate goal and and put all the egos and pride aside. >> With that, how have you seen him kind of grow or evolve in the two and a half years he's been here? >> To me, he's just becoming more and more of himself. Um, you know, you see him come in, uh, his first year and you could tell he he wanted to like get everyone's respect and kind of, um, earn guys respect and trust and then, you know, now he's just seems more confident and just leaning more and more into who he is and and his principles. >> You like him get a little spotlight with Hard Knocks and more people discovering him. >> Yeah, to me, I like it. Um, you know, he's a great coach. He has a great personality. Um, I think he deserves to be uh, recognized and um, I think this is, you know, put him in a spotlight and uh and nothing has to change, you know, he's just being himself, which is what everyone else in the building is doing. >> In the episode last night, they showed him like really getting on Derrick Hall, getting too [clears throat] close to the quarterbacks. He's pretty stern, but then afterwards, he's got his arm around him. Tell him that he loves it. Like, what do you appreciate about that sort of >> I mean, what I appreciate about that is that is the type of energy that spreads throughout the team. Um, and you've seen it from the top down. I mean, he's the head coach who's, you know, getting on someone and there's a heated um altercation in that moment, but at the same time it's like all love. Is it that easy though to not think about, yeah, we're the defending Super Bowl champions and we gota, you know, >> it's surprisingly been easier than I imagined. And, you know, without that, obviously, we wouldn't have got the opportunity for that two-minute. >> I'm sorry. To that to that point, when you look at the performance of three quarterbacks and the numbers, how reflective that is of Mike McCarthy as a play call. >> Yeah, I think it's it's very reflective of of coach McCarthy and his play calling and his system. um and how it's tailored to, you know, be friendly for the quarterback. And I think it also speaks to coach Tom Marth and coach an and um you know, everybody in that room and Aaron um [snorts] you know, helping us out. You know, he's giving us little tips here and there. Um but yeah, I think it really it really shows how um QB friendly this system can be and and when we execute the way that we want to like like all of us, I feel like did tonight. Um yeah, we can we can be a really really fun offense. up to uh on your throat to Tanya that took you guys down to like the one yardd line. When you're feeling the pressure on that play and you step up, what are some of the points of emphasis? What's going through your mind to make that play possible? >> You know, to be honest with you, I feel like pocket movement is more of a feel thing than anything. It's it's more of like like I came back and watched the film and I didn't really even realize that I kind of stepped up around that. like it's just it's just something that naturally kind of happens and you drill um you know all the time with you know little things that we do at camp with Tom and Avant running at us with pads and um you know we we drill that all the time but I feel like the more that you're in the game the more that you feel that it kind of just becomes second nature and being able to throw you know off of a quick movement is is something we drill all the time. So again I got to got to shout shout Tom out on that one. you know, he's uh he's done a great job with the drill work in Indie all offseason and then in training camp and um yeah, that was a big time play. The middle just opened up and you know, one of our one of our favorite plays there and uh yeah, it was it was a big time play. Obviously, you know, I I wish I would have maybe put it on him a little better and uh and got it in there, but you know, it happens and then Lou goes and gives a six. >> You mentioned the uh you mentioned Aaron's input on the fourth and one play. What other kind of input was he giving you on the sideline? He said at one point that his role would be to, you know, give some comic reliefs, tell some dad jokes on the headset. Just what was he doing on the sideline tonight? [snorts] >> Yeah. No, he was uh very involved and and not even just in the game, but before the game, you know, he really kind of talked to, you know, all three of us, but more me and Drew. Um just about some little things that helped him when he was young in the preseason. Hey, you know, find your guy. You know, today it was Bobby. For me it was Kaden for Drew and you know Jeremy for me like sometimes that's that's what you do or you know when the headset goes out have a play that you're ready to get to and you know he was helping looking at the defensive signals and um the sort of pressures that they were running and and giving us feedback on that. So he was very helpful you know leading up to this game and then throughout the game he was very helpful as well. >> Been a very long time since you had a live pass rush and like I think it was maybe the second pass and you had a free rusher chasing you already. How do you feel like you uh handled that and uh was just kind of good to get those reps after it had been so long? >> Yeah, I mean obviously anytime you have a free rusher running at you, it's not ideal. Um you know, got to make sure I get myself into a better protection there and um you know, be able to pick it up. They brought a pretty pretty tough blitz with the will coming in a double A and the nickel coming off the edge. Um they kind of got us. So I mean it gets real and you know those the guys in the NFL are all very fast. So, had to get up on my horse a little bit, but you know, getting getting tackled on the sideline, it felt good to, you know, get tackled again and like being a be in a football setting again, it it just felt more real and and you know, that kind of I feel like really got me into the game. I always have said like the first hit, you know, it really, you know, then you settle down and uh it was good. It was good. Well, did you have a last moment >> where like the nerves you must have been feeling where you just felt locked in like something happened with a play at completion or just felt like okay the nerves are kind of gone and I can just settle in? >> Yeah, I mean kind of like I said the you know getting hit for the first time that kind of that kind of happens but you know I think that second play that we ran the little naked over ball that I threw to Brandon Smith. Um you know I've always said the the first hit you take and then the first completion you make is kind of what gets you in that rhythm. And you know, obviously we weren't able to continue that drive, but kind of that first completion was big. And then the first time I got hit, you know, that kind of just gets you gets you going into the game. And obviously the preseason's a little different, you know, with when you're playing and when you go in, you know, you got to kind of find your rhythm that way, but I think, you know, getting that first completion was big. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thanks, guys. >> How would you assess that first throw? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, it felt good. I think Kaden on the first throw in particular, Kaden did a great job of separating versus man coverage. Um, and and that's what, you know, you need from those guys. He did a great job of, you know, obviously we got it back later of getting him in the end zone, but he did a great job of, you know, making a a play after the catch as well. Um, and the O line did a great job of, you know, holding up in pass protection on third and seven. Uh, so yeah, I mean, it felt good to be out there. scoring drives and then a victory formation. Do you think everything went as well for you tonight as you wanted it to? >> I mean, I I think my job as a quarterback is to go out and put up points uh no matter what the the situation is. So, I feel like we did a good job of that. And it wasn't just me out there. I had 10 other guys and and then including the coaching staff and obviously with coach McCarthy calling the plays, but the the whole offensive staff doing a great job of, you know, getting us into successful plays and allowing us to go out there and be successful. So, it's a it's a total team effort. Um, and no matter what. Um, and then obviously defense and special teams, you know, did a really good job tonight, too. So, it wasn't just one phase or one player that that won the game tonight. >> It took you to kind of settle in tonight. >> Uh, I mean, honestly, like pretty fast. I think for me, football is football no matter what. And honestly, I feel like the adjustment for me at the NFL level came during rookie OTAAS and and OTAAS in general. And uh more specifically like with this training camp cycle um and going against a great defense every day with a a challenging scheme that really challenges us as offense. I feel like that really you know mentally prepared me to to go out there and just handle everything. And then you know I feel like um the first rushing touchdown I had was like the first hit I've had in I mean uh I don't know how long but since mid October. So I feel like that that kind of got the physical part out of the way. I feel like, you know, going against our defense every day in practice, um, really helped me mentally prepare for the game. >> Quarterback school and all the footwork and all the different things you've been working on. Were you able to go out and play without having to think about any of those fundamentals? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, I'll probably get a minus grade on one of my footworks. Uh, it was kind of a a crazy, you know, reverse out on a on an under center exchange, but other than that, I felt pretty good. And I feel like coach Arth and really the whole room between coach an uh coach McCarthy and then obviously having Aaron and Mace and Will for me, they did a great job of helping me and answering any questions I had, you know, throughout the last two and a half days of prep for for Green Bay with our offensive game plan. and they did a a great job of simplifying it and really just allowing us, especially like the younger guys that I was I was in with just go out and play fast and play free and and really call the stuff that they know we've repped a lot and can go out and execute at high level. And again, we did a great job of that and it starts up front. Like I don't think I was really pressured at all. The only time I really was is when they they kind of went zero and they brought more than we could block. So that O line did a phenomenal job for me tonight. Jordan on the Norwegian play. Um, what are you thinking when that call comes in about where you've got to place the ball? What are you processing there? And and how'd you feel about the throw itself? >> You said the the first one, >> the long one. Yeah. >> Yeah. Uh, I mean, for me, I I knew I kind of recognized man coverage right away. And, you know, with the whole player, I really thought I was going to have the tight end on on a crosser, but um, the whole player sat sat inside and kind of took that away because our tight end beat his guy on the route, but the the linebacker took that away. And you know, I I knew I had really good leverage on that basic route with Kaden. He did a great job at the top of really giving a two-way go to that DB and not allowing him to, you know, guess and and anticipate where Kaden was going to break it. And then on that, you know, you just want to give him a catchable ball and one that's out in front or on his body that he can turn up field and really, you know, do what he did. Um, and go, you know, make a a 12 yard gain, a whatever it was, like a 70 yard gain. Drew in when you checked into the game, there was a pretty loud pop from the crowd. They all yelled Drew. Did you hear that or did you think they were booing? It kind of does sound a little similar. >> Uh, no. Honestly, I I was more focused on saying the annunciating the play call more than anything. So, I I I didn't really hear it at all. Yeah. >> This is obviously your first true taste of NFL action. What's it like for you from a confidence perspective when things are clicking as well as they were for you in those three drives? Yeah, I mean I think it's a huge confidence boost, but um I think you know I I came into the game confident just because of the preparation and everything that has gone on the last two weeks uh down in Latroe and then again coach McCarthy and the whole offensive staff putting together a really um concise game plan. Uh and again just calling stuff that they know I'm comfortable with um and just allowing us to go out and play fast. So I feel like they did a great job of putting me in a position to go out and and be successful. the uh the touchdown run. Was that a read option there? >> Uh yeah. Uh more or less. Like I kind of had a throw option, but then I saw the the safety kind of come down and and press the the throw option. So I knew at that point it turned into like a a true zone read off the defensive end. >> That was a red zone rep where it seemed like kind like you ended up throwing it away like over over Kaden, but it seemed like initially like you got a little happy because you you were able to settle down in the pocket, reestablish yourself and and just see the field. How much of that is coming from the work that you guys put in to kind of not try to overdo what you're supposed to do and stick to what you're working on? >> Yeah, I mean I think like you said, I kind of got a little bit of happy feet. I got to go back and watch the film to kind of understand why I did that. But, um, you know, when that happens, you just kind of almost have to take a deep breath and, you know, I I didn't have any pressure on that play. So, I just got to kind of buy some time at that point because I'm playing off rhythm. Um, and kind of just try to work a scramble drill. So like that throwaway, it was really just like a a him and nobody buddy throw uh where we're either going to, you know, have a touchdown, maybe a PI, or it's going to be incomplete. So sometimes, you know, I I kind of screwed up in the first part of the the read, but you don't make a bad play worse is is something that we kind of always talk about. And you know, each play lived a life of its own and and on that play, you know, got to clean up the footwork on the first half, but you know, I think the receivers did a great job of kind of getting in the scramble rules, especially tight down in the red zone and the O line did a great job of, you know, sustaining blocks. >> Do you see that? Do you see that as a sign of progress for yourself to be able to react in a live moment and and think through all of that to stay stay in play? >> Uh, yes and no. Well, I mean, we we definitely rep it a lot, but I feel like, you know, kind of going back to high school, I had a lot of that. Uh, just because of the high school system I was in. I mean, it was it was five wide and I was eight yards in the gun and it was just throw the ball every play. So, I feel like that happened a lot throughout my high school career where I could kind of develop that and kind of learn the dos and don'ts of that. Um and then coach Arth and um you know coach McCarthy do a great job in our seven periods emphasizing if you know the defense does a great job of taking away all your progressions uh scramble because you know that that works very valuable for for everybody. It's very valuable for receivers and quarterbacks obviously getting on the same page with the scramble rules but also our defense staying attached to them uh to our receivers. So you know I think it's something that we emphasize a lot of and then you can see that show up in the games. that Dragon that slant flat combo a lot on that second touchdown drive. Why why that and why is that such a comfortable uh concept for you? >> Uh well, why that is because I that's why I got over the headset from Coach McCarthy. But um yeah, I think it kind of going back to to base calls. Um that's like a day one install for us. Um and with me and everybody that's in there, we know we can go out and execute that. We can, you know, check um into different concepts if we need to. based off coverage. Um, and it's something I feel comfortable with. You know, I I have um a decent amount of experience with it kind of going back from high school and college, but also, you know, it's probably been one of the top seven concepts I've probably repped since I've since I've been here. Um, going back to rookie mini camp. So, I feel like coach McCarthy does a great job of just, you know, getting a quick play call in and allowing us to kind of assess it and change it if we need to, whether it's protections or route concepts, but then at the end of the day, just go out and and run slant flat. >> Thank you guys. Miss closed.

text: Especially with the two youngs. >> Uh really like to quarterback play tonight. You [sighs] know, uh not to be a broken record. I've been talking about it. It may be you know, maybe I talk about it too much, but you know, the communication from the bonds are getting the play entry in there getting you know, tempo on the huddle. We're we're going to be better coming out of the huddle. I I didn't think we were super clean. I didn't like the snap, you know, of of how we were how we're going to play. So you know, so it's good to get that on tape. But for the most part I thought we This is a good start for us. You can you can hit me with the specifics, you know, to the fundamentals and all that after we you know, we watch the tape and just and being clearly honest with you, I'm watching the substitution. I'm watching the interaction of special teams. I'm watching the defensive communication. You know, it's our first time, but guys that have been in the box haven't been in the box. I I don't look at it that way. You know, I'm you know, I think it's just the way I believe this game is played. We we spend a lot of time and our coaches and players are I think they're doing an outstanding job of having an understanding of what the other guy does, you know, in the offense understanding defense vice versa and I'm and I'm quick to say especially when it gets ready to play the game, I really don't give a hoot what they do, you know, it's about how we're going to play. Um you know, from an offensive standpoint, if you do it the right way, that beats good defense. You know, same on defense. If you're doing it the right way in the area of, you know, winning the pre-snap, playing with right fundamentals, finishing, you know, as a unit, you know, you'll be successful. So, um today was our starting point. We have I'm just we have a lot of work to do. I think we all recognize that. Um but this is this was a good start for us. >> Coach, you mentioned you mentioned this is your first, you know, first time, first game here. title: Drew Allar, Will Howard SHINE, rookie WRs dazzle, OL struggles, STs woes | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all the Pittsburgh Steelers win 20 to 9 in their first preseason game here. And the story, let's be real here guys, it's the quarterbacks, especially the young quarterbacks. Now, that's not to say Mason Rudolph didn't have some moments today. He did. He had a really nice sack escape. Some of the stuff that happened to him were out of his control. The O line had some struggles. There were some miscommunications. There was one play early on where there was two guys that ran the same route. Clearly should not have been. He extends the play and at least finds Rowan Wilson in the flat. He made a positive out of nothing. Um but you know, I do think the story is Will Howard and uh Andrew out here. Mason Rudolph was fine. But Will Howard with that two-minute drill before the half, man, really impressive stuff. The poise he showed. You know, that that throw going off kind of kilter, out of structure to find Tonyan to really jump-start this thing was an impressive throw. And then I thought the seam ball. I mean, that seam ball was perfect. Placed it high. No one else could have gotten it but Robert Tonyan. And that's the type of throw you look for from a quarterback. That's precise placement. You're not trying to find, you know, a guy that's trying just to lead a guy straight into the defender. He's protecting his guy there. And I thought he looked good outside of structure making some plays on the run on some rollouts. Will Howard looked solid tonight. And that two-minute drill was really impressive. Um and then Lu Nichols pounds that in. Um and then I thought Drew Allar, I mean, Drew Allar three touchdowns in three drives. Lot to like there. The best thing, you know, there wasn't even like a wild throw. And there didn't need to be. He hit every layup. You know, they ran like slant flat like eight straight times. And you know, slant flat's like a base core thing everyone runs in in high school. And it's the preseason, so you're not trying to show much, but he was just hitting these slants and these flats and just going bang bang bang. Making layups look like layups. That's been a huge thing for Drew Allar is can he just make easy stuff look easy? He made it look really breezy today. Listen, there were some moments sometimes where you were like, "Okay, there's the There's, you know, some questionable maybe breezy moments where he's letting it go a little bit." But, for the most part, I mean, what He was like 10 of 13, 155 passer rating. Like, you can't really complain much about what Trubisky did tonight. He looked really in sync and looked really sharp. So, just a really impressive night for him. I thought Lou Nichols played really well at running back. I think he runs hard, runs behind his pads, he's good in pass pro. I really like him. But, the the noise out of this running back room right now is Caleb Johnson. Caleb Johnson, what is going on, dude? Didn't play until the second half. Not good news for Caleb Johnson's roster hopes. I'm just saying. So, we'll see if Caleb Johnson is making this roster, but wouldn't feel good about it right now. And wide receiver, Jeremy Bernard is just so compact. He's so sudden. He's so good after the catch. And you saw Weegens, too. Weegens had like five tackles on these returns tonight despite like 10 penalties. I just thought Cade Weegens looked really solid today with the ball in his hands. And that's been the guy he was all the time. But, so did Bernard. And those two stood out in a big way. I thought the two young rookie wide outs looked really, really promising. And that's really good. No Roman Wilson tonight, though, really, in terms of anything. You know, Pittman and Metcalf are banged up and not playing. You hoped he would step up. He had trouble getting off press on the outside. Didn't make as much noise. Let's see if he can do it in the rest of the preseason. I thought Tonyan stood out. I thought Riley Nowakowski, you know, after a drop, made a really nice one-handed grab to redeem himself late in the game. That was nice to see. This O-line This is a different offense. I I want to say it There's more real pass sets. You know, the Fontenot play where Rudolph gets sacked by Van Ness, you know, he's expecting a bit of a chip from Washington. Washington just gets out of there really quick. He he then has to kind of rush outside. He's called for a holding on a later one where Lou Nichols bounces it outside and it's hard for a a tackle to adjust that cuz you don't expect the bounce outside. It was a good read by Nichols, but um you just don't expect that. And so, it wasn't Troy Fautanu's best day. He had a false start as well. Um but I also remember back in his rookie year when he was at right tackle and looked awful in the first game against the Texans and then he was going against Nick Bosa in week two and looked pretty darn good. Um so, I I I don't I'm really concerned about the left side of this line. It's the preseason. We'll see as they progress. Um Dylan Cole and Spencer Anderson had some moments, too. This O-line did struggle, I think, tonight. I did think that was one thing. That and the special teams penalties. Six special teams penalties too many. Um and the special teams have looked sloppy in in some of these drills and I've heard Danny Crossman be very vocal about those um in his kind of little periods during training camp. So, those are the two big things I think that I came away with was, man, I really uh the O-line didn't play all that well, the first-team O-line, and I didn't think that the special teams really was was fluid at all. It's like a lot of penalties today. And coming off Mike McCarthy's comments on Tuesday, not something you necessarily want to see. I did think on defense you saw some really intriguing stuff. I mean, Gabriel Reuben Yaya Black looked decent in run defense. I thought Kyler Baugh, who is Kyler Baugh? Most of you probably don't know him. Two sacks. He looked tight. Um really really eccentric guy. He's an energetic kind of energizer bunny type of player. He's just really explosive there from the middle. I I I really like what we saw from him. I like what we saw from Zayzio Timewo. A lot of good options on the depth of that. Um I thought we also saw some good play out of some of these depth DBs. The Nico Slaughter, I thought had some really good plays in the screen game coming downhill. He is really physical. He's willing to put his face in the fan. Not going to shy away from it. We saw Israel Mukuamu Jr. get a really nice PBU on a slot fade against the first-team Packers offense. Thought that was really good. I thought Devin Boykin, you know, the kind of safety slot hybrid, thought he played really well. I thought I'll front Jaylen Jimen Davis one and a half sacks today. He's tight hip but he's also explosive. He's got this hot motor. This team runs hot with their motors. I love that about them. And I thought Patrick Graham's defense looked good today. They didn't do a ton of crazy looks but they did some really good blitzes. They showed some different looks. I thought it was really solid despite a lot of those players not playing. Um and so overall you got to feel pretty good coming out of this. The two young quarterbacks playing really well. Really really good and then Mason Rudolph also looking pretty solid. I mean all three quarterbacks I thought had a good performance today. Thought you saw some really promising thing as out of your young skill guys. Um I think you feel good about a lot of this team. I do think the O line's one thing that we'll see how that progresses. I'm not too concerned about it just yet. It is the preseason and Troy Fautanu is a proven good football player. But let's see where that goes, you know. Right tackle to left tackle is not easy even if you have played left tackle in college. Switching there two years not not just easy. It's not like it's not like switching from guards I think. You know, guard's a little easier and tackle is a little bit more depth because you have to hit set points and different things. But we'll see where that goes. Make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn notification bell for more and thanks for watching everybody.

title: Steelers-Packers PREVIEW, predictions, players, things to watch, Drew Allar, Will Howard
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to another episode of the Steelers Breakdown podcast. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. I'm actually back home now. Isn't that nice? Not Latrobe anymore in those Fred Rogers Center recording studios and all of that. But I am joined here by the first time a guest of the program, my good friend Brendan Howe of Steelers Now. But yeah, you mentioned not being in Latrobe. It was nice this morning. I know I've been driving back and forth. Unlike you, you got to stay there. I noticed this morning I didn't have to set alarms on my phone to wake up. But before that, we have a preseason game on Thursday. The Pittsburgh Steelers will take on the Green Bay Packers tomorrow at 7:00 Eastern Standard. Not really what I would do if they do play with Aaron Rodgers, but kind of what do you think's going to end up happening? >> So this game would have a lot more hype if it was like the Sunday night game last season during the regular season, um you remember that the uniforms everybody thought was ugly that I disagreed with. I thought they looked good. Yeah, th- this is a preseason game. I agree with you in the fact like if you're going to play Aaron Rodgers, you should put him out there for a series and he should not throw the ball once. He should hand it off every time. But if I kind of had my way there, Mason Rudolph would get the first few series and then you really want to see who you have out of Will Howard and Drew Allar, which both of them haven't played football in a good while, especially Will Howard. I think I counted up the days uh when I wrote about the other day, 570 days since he last stepped on a field in game action and that was the national championship two Januaries ago. Uh so really excited to see what they could do. Honestly, like I know Mason is there and he is a very viable candidate to to be that backup quarterback, but we kind of know we're going to get out of Mason Rudolph. So I I don't need to see too much out of him on on the field. I'd rather the lion's share of reps go to Howard and Allar. >> So would I. I mean, I think that's what's going to happen. Mike McCarthy talked about three groups. There's going to be the first group that plays about a series or two at most. The second group which plays the rest of the first half and then the third group's probably going to get most of the second half, if not all of it. And so that to me clearly sets up to be Will Howard in that first half, Drew Allar in that second half. The only question is is that first team quarterback going to be Mason Rudolph or Aaron Rodgers? I think that's still a question. You know, Mike McCarthy has talked about this, kind of wanting his quarterbacks to play. Uh clearly Aaron Rodgers talking to him yesterday does not want to play in this football game. I mean, there's no doubt about it. He doesn't see much value in it. My guess is, and this is just where I'm kind of leaning towards, is we end up seeing Mason Rudolph. That's kind of where I'm going with this right now. I guess there could be a scenario where it's Rodgers playing one series and we don't see Mason Rudolph play this week. I suppose that could happen. That's kind of an out of the the way theory that could happen if Rogers plays, but I think the two young guns are going to play a lot. And let's go to those young guys. You know, I don't need to see anything from Aaron Rodgers in this game. I don't need to see anything from Mason Rudolph in this game. I know what those guys are. I have you know, 10 years of experience with with Mason Rudolph now. Aaron Rodgers has plenty of experience to draw back on, but we have not seen Will Howard or Jarret Stidham play a game in the National Football League preseason or regular season. So, let's start with Will Howard. What are you kind of looking for from Will Howard in this game? What do you what do you want to see especially after the training camp we've seen from him? >> First off, I thought that the parallels of both Howard and Rodgers talking back-to-back days. Howard gets up there, he has a big smile on his face, he's giddy, he says, "I know that people say preseason football isn't real, but it's real to me." And then Rodgers gets up there and he says exactly what Howard said, "Preseason football isn't real." And then he said he did admit like later on that when he was in Howard's shoes, he Sorry. I don't know. I thought my phone cut out there. I'm recording on my phone. So, um Rodgers gets up there and he says exactly what Howard was saying that people say. And then he admits later on that it was the Super Bowl when he was in Howard's shoes, but I want to see Will Howard get out there and flash the confidence that he had at Ohio State. Like we saw what he was able to do when he was playing for that team with a stacked receiver group. Uh he's going out there, he's going to be throwing to like you said DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman will not be out there. He's going to have a bit of a mishmash of receivers in terms of Brandon Smith and Roman Wilson and Jalen Bernard who Roman Wilson and Jalen Bernard is really interesting in itself where I want to see how both of those guys do. Uh he's not going to have quite the the receiver room he had there. And also like you want to see him kind of knock that rust off. Like I I don't know what it's like not or what it'll be like for him going out there and having not played in actual football game action. Like, I talked to him this offseason and it was weird for him last year to not play at all. He's talked about this camp where it was odd for him to to stand on the side and it's a different sort of excitement stepping out in in this game. So, all in all, you want to see him go out there and kind of you want to see what he can do after that long layover of of just practicing in in last year kind of being out of the mix for a little while. >> I really want to see him in a live pocket. That's my big thing with Will. You know, he's at Kansas State sometimes had trouble against pressure and and the accuracy under pressure. We haven't seen him in a live pocket and when he was at Ohio State obviously was playing with tons of NFL talent in the trenches. So, I want to see how he looks um in a live pocket. I I also do want to see how that accuracy looks on the field because I think he's been pretty accurate at training camp. I think that has been one thing that's really stood out. That, you know, the seam balls that he's thrown, some of these balls that he's thrown up the seam have been really really nice. Um and so, there's a few things I want to see from Will Howard, but I want to see that command of the offense. I want to see him commanding that huddle. I want to see him deal with pressure, step up and and feel pressure, not run into sacks or or be a statue and kind of collapse in the pocket and just look frazzled. Don't want to see that. Um you want to see a guy that looks like a game manager. You know, I'm not looking for a guy that looks like the future franchise quarterback here. Um and and that's one thing I think, you know, Will Howard has to prove, but let's see how he does it. So, I'm actually really looking forward to seeing Will Howard out there.
