Um you know, he's skipping balls every now and then. He's not putting them behind guys. Um and even if they're not completely off target, they're not, you know, leading guys in the direction for yak and things like that. So, the the accuracy has to have work in the underneath to the intermediate. So, I'm looking for accuracy. I'm looking for the footwork to be consistent. We've seen that in the most pressure pressurized situations. But, with those two in practice, hasn't looked pretty. So, if you can go out there in in actual game action and follow that around and make that look good and and play well under pressure like that, I think that'll be a really promising sign. >> And we we've seen that in the Hall of Fame game, Haynes King did that very well and led the Panthers down the the the the field. It's always fun when you see young quarterbacks out there because those two are so different as well in their skill sets. And I'm just interested to see how they go about it. And they have different objectives to me that I want to see from both of them. Meanwhile, you you Brandon you and I have been there all of camp. We've watched these guys. Give me a guy that maybe is under the radar that you're excited to see. Um that you really want to see play in this preseason because you think they have a chance to up their stock. >> So, Caleb Johnson, I talked about this even before training camp started. title: Grading the 49ers After their 19-13 Preseason Loss to the Titans
text: The 49ers just lost 19 to 13 to the Tennessee Titans in preseason game number one. Here are their grades. Quarterbacks C++. Curtis Ror outplayed Cam Ward until he injured his rib running between the tackles trying to score a touchdown in a preseason game. More on that decision in a minute. Ror finished the night completing 12 of 14 pass attempts for 101 yards and posted a respectable pass rating of 96.7. He saw the field well, got rid of the ball quickly, avoided a sack, scrambled for a first down, and made a beautiful deep throw to Dejon, dribbling up the right sideline. Ror looks like he has potential to develop into a quality backup or maybe even a starter. Too bad the Niners got him injured. His replacement, Adrien Martinez, was awful. Running backs D. None of these guys will make the team, nor should they. They're all mere camp bodies. The best one tonight was Sincere McCormack, who was quick and ran hard, but averaged a mere 3.8 8 yards per carry. In fairness to him and the other running backs, who aren't really worth naming, they kept getting hit in the back field, which means they never really had a chance. Wide receivers, Bminus, Dejon's dribbling was by far the Niners's best receiver, but that's not saying much considering all their veterans sat out. That made dribbling the focal point of the offense, and he responded well, catching seven of eight targets for 63 yards. He doesn't create a ton of separation, which means he might not be the best option to move the chains on short passes, but he has outstanding hands. He catches the ball far away from his frame and he's a true deep threat on a team that needs one. It'll be interesting to see if he opens up Brock Pie's downfield passing game. The second best wide receiver in the game for the Niners was Jordan Watkins who caught six passes for 58 yards. Tight ends F. It made almost no impact. It's really too bad the Niners haven't drafted a tight end since Cam Lu. Offensive lineman D. The Niners have a real problem at left guard considering they don't have a starter at that position. The favorite to start is Robert Jones, who played tonight and was awful both in the run game and the pass game, and he's their best option. The Niners need rookie Carver Willis to grow up quickly and take his job. He played most of the second half and performed better than Jones, which isn't saying much. Defensive lineman D. Rookie Grayson Halton was the star of this group. He stood up double teams in the run game and recorded a tackle for loss and a sack that was called back due to a penalty away from the play. The rest of the defensive line was horrible, though. Alfred Collins got pushed around and Romelo height made no impact as a run defender or a pass rusher. In fact, veteran camp body Abana Okaranquo was much more impressive than height, which is troubling. Once again, the Niners will be extremely reliant on Nick Bosa to be durable and dominant, two things he might not be able to provide anymore. Linebackers C plus Tatum Bthun was solid as usual. He's an excellent backup middle linebacker. Nick Martin played most of the game, which probably isn't a good sign for his chances to start at outside linebacker. Maybe the Niners wanted to showcase him to the Titans so they'll trade for him considering Robert Salah drafted him last year. Martin's biggest play was a 15-y penalty against him. He still doesn't seem to know what he's doing as opposed to rookie Jaden Duggar who didn't play like a rookie. Don't be surprised if he becomes a Niners third linebacker by the end of the season. Defensive backs B. Jack Jones left the game early with a hand injury. Rookie Ephesians Pric replaced him and promptly broke up a potential touchdown pass intended for rookie firstround pick Carnell Tate in the front right corner of the end zone. Pric engulfed him, made him look tiny. He has serious potential. None of the other defensive backs stood out with the exception of Ashton Davis who nearly intercepted Cam Ward. Special teams C. The Niners have an outstanding kicker tonight. Eddie Panero made a 52-y field goal. Easy, like breathing. Unfortunately for the Niners, they don't have a punt returner. Coaches D. I usually don't grade the coaches during the preseason because they don't game plan. They're coaching to evaluate certain players, not to win. And yet, for some strange reason, Kyle Shanahan and Klay Kubak decided to call a quarterback draw for Curtis Ror from the four-yd line. It's always risky to run a quarterback between the tackles near the goal line. And on this play, Ror injured his ribs. It's unclear how much time he'll miss. Fortunately, the Niners also have M. Jones to back up Rock Purdy. But Ror seems extremely promising for a young quarterback. He's big, he's accurate, and he's mobile. Now the Niners just have to keep him healthy. Easier said than done for them. [music]

title: BIG 49ers injury update on Nick Bosa, CMC and more...
text: Big 49ers injury update morning after their physical joint practice against the Titans which also featured some nifty plays from the secondary. That's the Jacob Robinson interception and Jack Jones celebrating with him. He's been making plays for the 49ers. Here's some of that physicality. Fred Warner and then Jaier Brown who later had a pick six there. Thuds up the tight end of the Tennessee Titans. That injury report as promised. Nick Bosa at the top of it. Knee tendinitis is the more specific diagnosis given by Kyle Shanahan yesterday. Kyle said that it is weak to week for Nick Bosa and that there isn't much to worry about at this point. >> Uh just soreness, tendonitis. It's a pretty normal thing um with ACL's. Um you know, just talking to our guys, they say it happens about 90% of the guys we've had. Um so it's normal thing and that's why we got to be smart here for you know week to week but um feel no concerns about him um being any more than that. >> So we will obviously monitor this situation. One warning that I would give is that this was Nick Bosa's third ACL tear. I know that he classifies as a superhuman to have been able to even come back from two ACL tears and to look as good as he did earlier this training camp coming off the third, but at some point you can't just keep on coming back from ACL tears. I don't know if Nick has reached that point. I'm not saying that he has, but it is something to monitor as he comes back from this third ACL tear. 49ers aren't worried. As you heard Kyle Shanahan say, 90% of ACL cases have some sort of tendinitis. So, we will see how this progresses with Nick Bosa. As long as he's ready to go by week one, then you're fine with it. If you're the 49ers, you're trying to get him ready for that week one day. Then there is Christian McCaffrey. Now, this one you really don't have to worry about right now. McAffrey is just a little bit of stiffness. It's like the Dejon Stribbling situation that kept Dejon out of practice for what, four, maybe five sessions. Dejon Stribbling is back in dominating. And Christian's already put in enough work this off season to be fully ready for week one. He I have even said it looks faster this year than he did last year because he's a year further removed from the Achilles injury. 413 touches last year. The key for Christian McAffrey is going to be keeping him fresh so he could continue showing some of the explosiveness that we have already seen so far in this 2026 training camp. And keeping him fresh that's going to be very I think reliant on the health of Jordan James and Kalon Black. James still out with the rib. Kalon Black still out with the adductor injury. So, the 49ers suited up only three running backs yesterday against the Titans in that joint practice. Patrick Taylor Jr., Khil Herbert, who actually had some nice runs, and Sincere McCormick. We will see what the 49ers do for the game on Thursday. Obviously, no starters or very few starters playing for the 49ers. So, McAffrey definitely won't be out there, but they may want to get one more running back. Maybe sign somebody off the street to have in uniform to finish this game. Kyle Uchek is currently out with a broken finger. He also won't play. So, a lot of injuries in that 49ers backfield, but they do hope to get Black and Jordan James back before the start of the season. and be a good time for Isaac Greno to be cleared from his pectoral tear because there are some opportunities for some carries right now. Christian Kirk, 49ers wide receiver coming back from the calf strain. He's been running fairly fast off on the side. So is Jacob Cowing and Cowing especially needs to be back sooner rather than later. A lot of young receivers making a case for this 49ers roster. Varian Low, the swing tackle, was hurt on day one of camp. High ankle sprain for Varian Low. So, we've always expected four to six weeks for him. Brett Toe, backup center, maybe a factor in the guard competition coming back from the concussion. Saw him on the exercise bike earlier this week. Keon White also has an abductor injury. I saw Keon, the defensive end, standing watching practice yesterday. I feel this is a week- toeek situation. Usually when a guy is standing out there watching practice and not having to rehab 24/7, it is a decent sign as to his availability and the relative short term. Other defensive end Mike El Williams seems that he's been ramping up his rehab. Remember he tore his ACL 6 weeks after Nick Bosa. So uh Bosa they've expected ready for week one. He wasn't even on the pup list. Mike Williams. That is much more of a question, but it does seem that he's doing well and he was also standing and watching practice for the 49ers. One more injury is Malik Mustafa and the strained hamstring. Sounds like that was something that was expected the last few weeks. It's been a couple weeks since the 49ers safety exited with that injury. As you can tell, none of these injuries except for Ricky Pierce Sols, and we've already talked a lot about that, are injuries that are keeping a player out for the entire season. And I would say that all of them that I just listed are injuries that the 49ers hope are resolved by week one. There are issues around the entire league injury-wise. I think that there's been PTSD regarding the 49ers injury situation, maybe rightfully so, given what happened last year, but it's important not to overreact to injuries in the sport of football, which is essentially synonymous with injuries. The 49ers can field the healthiest possible team, not just by week one, but by January and February. Well, that that's the the bigger key. You cannot win a Super Bowl in August, but you can certainly lose one. I was on KMBBR a little bit earlier and we talked about all things 49ers training camp. So here from Francisco Park, this is what used to be a reservoir and because it's up on a hill, Russian Hill, you water. They used gravity to uh service the northern neighborhoods like North Beach of San Francisco. But anyway, here from Francisco Park with a view of the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz. How about you listen in to my KMBBR interview? I'm settling back in here into the city for the season and I think that the dog days of are over because the first practice against somebody else has come and now tomorrow we finally have a game. So the toughest stretch is behind us and it's really starting to feel real. I love that. >> Yeah. Kind of the first chapter ending and now we go into the game starting tomorrow against the Titans chapter 2 and then eventually leading to the opener September 10 in Australia. So David, if you had to kind of write the theme piece, you know, so you're that your teacher says, "What did I do this summer?" What would be the theme from July 27th to now? And is it injuries? You know, it's funny because obviously the Ricky Piol situation was a gut punch, but that was an injury that he suffered last year. Just something that has never fully healed. And I think that because last year especially was so so difficult with the injuries for the 49ers, I think there's this PTSD and and I think that the media and social media is really ready to hop on it. So even guys that they're holding out for precautionary reasons now it turns into a national story. There's the whole substation thing going on. I think that the the injuries are actually overblown this year for the 49ers so far. and you can knock on wood. You can hope that they stay overblown because obviously things can go further south in in a hurry. So, I I don't think objectively that's the the main uh story of 49ers training camp. If it had been, they wouldn't have even conducted the joint practice with the Titans. When they start cancing joint practices like they did in 2024 when they're supposed to have one with the Saints and they didn't have enough healthy guys to confidently get through one, then I think you could seriously have that conversation. But for now, I I think that the you know, obviously they do have an older offense. Guys like Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey, you have to believe that they're going to be ready for for week one. They're managing them to to ensure that they're going to be ready for when the games count. I think so far the overarching two themes for the 49ers have been how good Brock Perie has looked at camp on the offensive side and that's really really important for that offense to be elite and the 49ers are going to need it to be the locomotive that pulls the train and two uh what Raheem Morris is doing to the defense because his resume has stops at many different types of schemes right he he's run four down front five down front 434 all this stuff and He's majored in secondary coaching. He's a DB guy and he has brought the changes that we thought that he would bring based on his resume to this 49ers defense and he's creating this hybrid scheme that I think is going to be fascinating to track over the course of this season. >> David, you're right. To your point, there's been a lot of talk this offseason about that change from Robert Solid to Raheem Moore. So, with both of them being on the field yesterday for the joint practices, were you able to notice some of those differences? maybe different styles and schemes that Raheem is going to go with this season. >> There was one play that really stood out to me. I was standing five yards away from it. You know, sometimes you're really far away at the joint practices. Sometimes things develop right in front of you. And it was Will Levis, one of the backup Titans quarterbacks, was rolling to his left and Jaden Duggar and Larry Worth, who two 49ers rookie linebackers were pressuring him and sprinting out toward the the sideline to cut off his his throwing uh vision on on the roll out. And between those two guys, there's almost 14 feet of combined wingspan. Jaden Duggar has a 7 foot wingspan. Larry Worth is not too far behind him. And they both had their arms outstretched up. And Will Leves could not see over both of these defenders. Two extremely unusually tall linebackers. I've yet to actually find a linebacker in NFL history like a stack linebacker with a 7 foot wingspan other than Jaden Duggar. Normally those guys are going to play edge rusher and and he's going to play some edge for the 49ers as well. But they they are very very insistent on this hybridized defense where the guys in the front seven are playing in multiple different spots. And Morris is huge on length. I mean, he wants length to clog passing lanes to do what we saw Worth and Duggar do yesterday to Will Le just completely choke off and any vision uh to where he might want to throw the football. And then Levis just had to throw the ball away and and Larry Worth was fired up and it was it was right next to me. So I it just kind of you know was imprinted on my mind. Oh this is what Raheem Morris wants from this defense. He wants extreme length and extreme adaptability because we have seen a practice where Jaden Duggar even worked with the defensive ends and I'm sure that he's going to be rushing the passer from that position but he's also going to be playing that linebacker position for the 49ers. >> Interesting stuff to see Raheem Morris as he uses these pieces here. And uh yeah, Jaden Duggar linebacker rookie is getting some buzz here. Speaking of another rookie, I want to ask you about Romelo Height and the pass rush. You know, listen, we talked about earlier in the show, last year's pass rush just just was one of the worst they've had in the Shanahan era, if not the worst. Nick Bosa's week to week with tendonitis. I don't know the Keon White situation. Maybe you could fill me in. We know Odigizu was a big ad. We hope for Alfred Collins and CJ West, but is Romelo Height as a result because of their need for pass rush and because how he's flashing going to be a guy who plays this year and gets reps and and and sort of the correlary is how you're feeling about the pass rush in general on August 12th. >> Well, so it's really interesting because he falls into a similar bucket Romelo height as the other two guys that I was talking about as Jaden Duggar and Larry Worth. Now they call it the feverback position. And that's that's the new that's the new terminology. And KJ Wright, the linebacker's coach, explained that it's because fever means you're sick and and you have to be a football sicko to to play the position because you you've got to learn a bunch of different spots. Some of the feverback candidates are going to be more linebacker rooted like a Jaden Duggar or a Larry Worth. Some of the feverback candidates like a Romelo Height are going to be more edge rusher rooted. So it's whatever position is more of your home base that that that's where you're rooted. So Romelo Height is more of an edge rusher, but he's also the lightest edge rusher the 49ers have had in these 10 years under Shanahan and Lynch. He's under 240 lbs. He is extremely quick off the ball, but even in college, he he executed several coverage drops and Chris Caceric says that he eats a lot of grass with his strides because he's he's very very quick and and has long strides as well with I think 6'4 height. So, uh, Romelo Height has been very intriguing in in a similar way that he can execute the adaptable defense that Raheem Morris is going to want to implement with the 49ers, but he definitely is the most polished pass rusher out of that trio of guys that I've talked about. Why one concern with Romelo Hy and this is going to remind you guys a little bit of D Ford and I know there have been comparisons to D Ford with the get off but he's jumped off sides a lot in in practice in one-on- ones during team drills and it's obvious why he his biggest comparative advantage is his get off. So he wants to maximize that but because he's a little bit lighter he can't afford to get swallowed up by a tackle. So, he has to have that initial step and it's led to to him jumping off sides quite a bit. The 49ers are trying to work on that and he's trying to work on that. He might be more effective in home games and in games where the 49ers have a big big crowd advantage, which is a lot of road games, too, because with that noise, he's going to be able to to better time up snap counts. And that first step, if he gets it off on time, not too early, is looks really, really lethal. but he's going to have to learn how to uh deal with NFL hard counts and and all that so he's not jumping off sides. >> David, the rookie that has gotten the most headlines this off seasonason is Dejon Stribbling. What can you tell us about his connection with Brock Pury throughout camp and how he looked yesterday against the Titans? >> I mean, he he might be the best receiver in the class, guys. I yesterday he clearly looked better than Carnell Tate who was the top pick of the class, but he had the benefit of of Perie throwing to him and and Pertie's been on fire this training camp. So, it's hard to to make that comparison when the situations are different. But if you just look at the large picture of work, and I I go back to college, too, for Dejon Stribbling. He played in three different systems, succeeded in all three, showed at Oklahoma State that he could run the intermediates and could separate on on just some of the the garden variety routes 10 to 20 yards down the field. showed at Old Miss that he could run the goal balls and and could catch the screen and run away from 4-4 corners that played for Georgia. I mean, there you put on the highlight tape, there's a catch and and run touchdown where stribbling runs away from a corner who was drafted who ran a 440 at the combine. So, he's got legit 4-3 speed when the pads are on. And then you look at him now performing in in camp and you see the size, you see the 6-3 height, you see the muscle, he's separating. He he can generate separation outside of of the scheme. You know, it's him and Mike Evans are the two guys that Persol was able to do that, but he's hurt now. So, he could really really beat man coverage. And more important than anything is the fact that he catches everything that's thrown his way. He only dropped one pass last year at Miss. He hasn't dropped anything yet over the course of training camp. And then the other day, Leonard Hankerson, the receivers's coach, he just mentioned that one thing that sold the 49ers on Dejon dribbling was that he would not back down from trying to cross sift block Ruben Bane, a an edge rusher, a defensive end who went number 15 overall to Tampa Bay, who's about 40 to 50 pounds heavier than him in college. And apparently the 49ers fell in love with dribbling when they saw that toughness because it showed them that he can run block in their system. And two, showed them that this guy could probably run over the middle of the field and and hold on to the football because he he has the guts to to try to get in there and and block somebody who's 50 pounds heavier than him. And all of the things that they kind of scouted have have shown up on the field so far. So now we have to see it carry over to games. But every indication is that that he's the real deal at this point. >> Yeah, I mean that he's having a great camp for sure. Here we're talking to David Lombardi of the SF Standard who course covers the 49ers comprehensively. Read them at sfstandard.com. There's so many different things we can ask you about, but just in the final few minutes here, I just look at the running back depth chart because obviously we know about Chris McAffrey and I don't know if you feel about him being held out if that's okay, if you know he's he's such a Ferrari Maserati. were so sensitive to his every tweak, but behind him, you know, we were so excited about Kalon Black the first few days of camp. I don't know what his status is. Uh, you know, Jordan James at the end of last year, there was a hope that he would flash, but he has this rib thing. So, just tell fill us in a little bit on the running back depth chart situation, you know, for the next four weeks. >> Well, you mentioned earlier Keon White. He actually has a similar injury. It's an adductor. It's a core muscle injury as Kalon Black. So, based on my understanding that that'll take a few weeks. It's already been a little bit of time for both of those players. So, they I think they hope to to have him back by by week one, although I haven't fully confirmed that yet. And Jordan James, I would expect back by by week one, probably even earlier for sure. That's a fractured rib. So, a little bit more straightforward than the adductor injury. Those are those are tough injuries for the 49ers. They were running with only three running backs for the joint practice yesterday. Cle Herbert actually had a couple nice cuts and runs. And they've got Patrick Taylor Jr. who has been in the in the system here for a couple years now and then and sincere McCormick who's been a practice squad running back for the team. I wouldn't worry about McCaffrey. I think that it they're more than happy with the work that he's already put in and then he's going to be ready to go for for week one based on what he's already done timing wise with the offense. Now it's a matter of management for McAffrey. I think that the plan proved to be really good for him last year. He was able to give him 413 touches and he has looked even more explosive than than last year. And I think it's cuz he's got a a year removed from the Achilles tendonitis in 2024. So even though he's gotten older, uh he's further away from the really troublesome injury in 2024. And and I would expect Christian McCaffrey to have a big year, but you do need to manage it, right? And then they've talked about the importance of that, which is why they have Jordan James, why they have Kalon Black. And there going to be opportunities for both of those guys. The key is to get healthy, get back. And one thing Klay Kubak said the other day that really resonated with me, he said, you know, guys get hurt in the league. The the pros are able to be ready regardless. The pros are doing the film study behind the scenes or are taking mental reps. And yeah, maybe it will take him a week to knock off the rust, but if Kalon Black is who the 49ers think he is, even though he misses some of this training camp, they they think that he could still be a big positive contributor for this team once he is back from the doctor injury. >> Yeah, I'd like to see him. So Dave, let's leave it at this. Given how, you know, the 49ers are not planning to play a whole lot of starters, if any, tomorrow night against the Titans, what should a 49er fan look for tomorrow night? Well, last year they didn't play their starters in the first preseason game. They never do with Kyle Shanahan. They usually wait until the second game to play the starters for a couple series and then the third game to play them for a quarter or maybe even a half. But last year they played the Broncos and the Broncos put their starters out there and the 49ers ran their essentially their second team defense which was a ton of youngsters especially last year. And I don't know if you guys remember, but the first two drives where that was the matchup, Broncos ones versus 49ers rookies, the 49ers dominated Denver. Like that Denver I don't I don't even know if they picked up a first down. The Denver media was freaking out. And I thought that was a really really good indication of things are going to go well for the 49ers this year if they can stay healthy. And obviously they didn't. But the the youngsters for the 49ers in in that first preseason game actually ended up playing really well early in the season before all the injuries happened and then they lost their leaders and Bosa and Warner. So, this might actually be a little bit more of a measuring stick for for the 49ers depth than than people want to give it credit for because they do get to play the first unit of an opposing team. The Titans are going to play everybody. I know it's a young team, but they did add quite a bit of talent this off season. I really like Robert Salah as a coach, and I think it should be a really interesting test for some of the younger guys like a Jaden Duggar, like a Larry Worth, you know, that we were talking about. And if they can have similar success to what they did last year against Denver over those first two possessions, that'd be a big arrow up for the 49ers. >> Good stuff, man. It's that time. We're finally ready to see those those guys in uniform on the field tomorrow and then uh on we go. So, thanks for the uh time. Love the coverage in the SF Standard and we'll chase you down the road. >> Yeah.

title: 49ers FAST REACTION: Stribling, Rourke — wow…
text: Fast reaction. Shout out to the guys here in the Levi's Stadium engineering room. Titans and the 49ers in the books and 49ers rookie class looked really good today. I I want to talk about Jayden Digger and then, you know, an honorary rookie is Curtis Rourke, the quarterback who had to sit out all of last year as he recovered from his ACL. He balled out. 12 of 14, 101 yards and he was throwing to De'Shawn Stripling. I do not want to hear any more about mock drafts and consensus and how well people sitting on their couch know better than actual NFL teams about what might fit in the NFL. De'Shawn Stripling looks like a first round talent and the 49ers got him in the second round. So, to me, that's the definition of value. Now, I can't wait to see De'Shawn Stripling play with Brock Purdy and company. Today, seven catches, 63 yards. Cordell Flott, the Titan's starting cornerback, was in on the coverage of the two most impressive catches from De'Shawn Stripling. The first one you saw the strong hands and he's 6'3 so he got up but it was a comeback route and and he was just stronger at the point of contact than Cordell Flott. Then there was the 33-yarder well placed from Curtis Rourke. Great catch near the sideline for Stripling. He He looks the part. He has looked the part over training camp. Next week you're going to get to see De'Shawn Stripling for a couple of possessions with Brock Purdy. And then in the third preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders, you're going to get to see De'Shawn Stripling probably for a quarter or maybe even a half with Brock Purdy. And then, you know, today he was running on the inside as a slot receiver and he was playing on the outside. Ricky Pearsall had his surgery today so we know the 49ers are looking for a flanker. Maybe De'Shawn can fill in at flanker, but I think they love him at that big slot position. The one play that he didn't make was the throw that was a little bit behind him from Curtis Rourke. It just wasn't the the right play called against that coverage on third down because the throw had to be behind him to avoid one of the underneath defenders. Stribling couldn't quite catch it. That's the first ball that I haven't seen Stribling catch throughout all of this training camp and preseason so far. And he only dropped one pass all of last season at Ole Miss. So, the guy's got great hands and it was revealing to to see him play in this preseason game today. On defense, Ji'Ayir Brown is going to play. My article's already up on the San Francisco Standard today really confirmed what a lot of the 49ers coaches have been talking about. This rookie, Ji'Ayir Brown, has a 7-ft wingspan. I've done research over the course of the past several months and I have yet to find a inside linebacker in NFL history with a wingspan of 7 ft. And you saw it put to use today when he chased Cam Ward down to the near side of the field and prevented Cam Ward from getting the edge. First, you saw the long strides. Ji'Ayir Brown was eating up grass, but second, you saw the long arms as he dove and made the stop. With Ji'Ayir Brown, the reason that you don't have players at linebacker with 7-ft wingspans is because normally they're playing edge rusher. The 49ers though have decided that they want this guy to be a stack linebacker, and they're obviously moonlighting him at a at edge rusher, too. They're inventing a new position. It's called the fever back, where he's going to play both. But immediately today, we saw the potential advantage of putting a Ji'Ayir Brown. We saw the vision that Raheem Morris and K.J. Wright, the linebackers coach, have. We saw the vision for this guy when he was chasing Cam Ward to the sideline. Now, the one you know, big concern when you have a guy that's this tall and obviously is lanky is will he be physical enough to play on the inside at stack linebacker. Is he going to be able to throw his body in there and make some run stops working against guards, interior linemen who are trying to work up to the second level? And Jaden had a tackle for loss early in this game. So, to me, he passed a lot of the tests that you'd want to see. And the one benefit that's really big is that the 49ers got the Titans first team offense. Right, the score of the game doesn't matter. This is the preseason. What you want to look at is how did the 49ers backups, cuz they didn't play their starters, play against the Tennessee Titans first team? Jaden Dogger, we saw working against Tennessee's first team. Grayson Halton, did you see his sack today? Dane Brugler, who writes his draft report every year, he said that Grayson Halton, 49ers fourth round pick, closes like a banshee. Well, today not only did he close like a banshee on his sack, Grayson Halton beat the highest-paid left guard, or the highest-paid guard in all football, Peter Skoronski, 25 million a year. He just bulldozed past him, made him look very bad, and then closed like a banshee against Cam Ward. So, we know Grayson Halton, the super explosive edge rusher. We've heard his name and we've heard him yelling at practice ever since he came off that bone bruise. He's been impressive in his get-off for the 49ers. He was impressive as hell today beating a 25 million-dollar guard in Peter Skoronski. For comparison, Grayson Halton's salary average annual value is only 1.4 million. So, you could see some real real value there for the 49ers. They opened this game Oh, by the way, facing that Titans first team, the 49ers played it to a 7-7 tie before Tennessee went to their backups, and the 49ers out-possessed Tennessee by about 9 minutes over the course of time when Tennessee starters were in and the 49ers backups, young players were in. Tennessee had an opening touchdown drive where I thought that Alfred Collins didn't look great to me on that opening drive, especially on the It looked like he got completely turned around and played the the touchdown run for Tennessee to open this game. It That was from Tony Pollard, one of their starters, didn't play that right. That was the the worst showing from this 49ers defense of the night. After that, the 49ers backup defense actually stopped the Titans first team offense in their tracks, and then we saw that play from Grayson Halton, we saw the Dugger play against Cam Ward near the sideline. That was on the second drive for Tennessee. So, the defense for the 49ers with those youngsters really settled in, and I still remember last year when I'm sitting here, same game, preseason, Denver Broncos joint practice then turned into uh preseason opener, and what we saw in that game was that the Broncos put their first team offense out against the 49ers second team, young youngsters defensively. And the 49ers just snuffed snuffed them out. The youngsters really showed out in that first game. That's exactly what you want to see if you are Raheem Morris and company. Now, speaking of the Titans first team and the 49ers second team, Curtis Rourke is a seventh-round pick. Sat out last year with the ACL. Curtis Rourke, the seventh-round pick, looked better than Cam Ward, significantly better, than Cam Ward, Tennessee's quarterback, who was the number one overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft. That should be a little bit of déjà vu. I put the There's something familiar about this place Yoda meme from uh Star Wars from The Empire Strikes Back when when when uh, the Luke Skywalker and uh, is on Dagobah and and he recognized something familiar about about the planet that he was on. Well, there's some familiarity here for me with a seventh-round pick outperforming first-round picks or even outperforming the number one pick in the entire draft. We've seen that story with Brock Purdy over and over and over again to the point of big money. And on a much smaller scale, in a much smaller sample just to begin the preseason here. Curtis Rourke, the seventh-round pick, looked a whole lot better than the number one overall pick Cam Ward who had his first team around him. Curtis Rourke had De'Shawn Dribbling who was awesome, was going to be a starter, but he didn't have Mike Evans, he didn't have Christian McCaffrey, he didn't have George Kittle, he didn't have uh, you know, we can go through an entire list of 49ers offensive stars who sat today. Rourke, as I said, 12 of 14, 101 yards, 14 of the toughest rushing yards that you'll ever see. There was a play early on, it was a fourth-down conversion where Cody Barton, the linebacker, and there's some interesting history with Cody Barton, blitzed and was on Curtis Rourke's back and Rourke just shook him off and then ran for the first down. And there was a flag against the Titans to boot on the play. I mean, super physically impressive stuff for somebody who hadn't played in a real game since 2024 when he was at Indiana. He played on a torn ACL that season for Indiana to show you how tough this guy is. I think that toughness really really showed for Curtis Rourke today. Good accuracy, good mobility. Uh, the opposite of when it came to accuracy was true for Adrian Martinez. After Rourke went 12 of 14 and then got hurt with a rib injury, we're going to check in on his status when we talk to Kyle Shanahan in a little bit. But after Rourke got hurt, Adrian Martinez came in and started three for 10. We saw some better passes from Martinez as it turned into the time in the second half, but uh, you saw the difference between a very accurate quarterback today and one who definitely was not as accurate for the 49ers. Starting offensive line today, Austin Pleasants left tackle, Robert Jones stays in the lead at left guard. Now, Jones had to face Jeffrey Simmons. Remember, this was the first team Tennessee Titans defense. This was not the 49ers playing against a bunch of scrubs at the start of the game. Jeffrey Simmons, John Franklin-Myers, those are two of the better defensive tackles in the league. Jeffrey Simmons, especially, is elite. I thought that Robert Jones more than held his own, and obviously the 49ers were able to march in for a touchdown against that first team Tennessee defense. Patrick Taylor Jr. Well-deserved touchdown run for him. Had a nice effort on the catch, but they said he was barely out of bounds the play before. He broke his shoulder, severe shoulder injury last year in the preseason, missed all of the year. So, today meant a whole heck of a lot for Patrick Taylor Jr. Back to the line. Pleasants, Robert Jones, Drake Nugent at center, Connor Colby was playing right guard. The more Connor Colby plays away from left guard, the the more I believe that he's just fighting for a roster spot to show that he has swing guard capability.
